News.title: Huge blaze burns through chemical plant as dozens of fire engines called to scene and 150 locals evacuated
News.content:
A MAJOR blaze has erupted at a chemical plant, sending thick smoke and flames high into the sky as 150 people are forced to evacuate.

Panicked locals have fled their homes as 30 fire engines and over 60 fire personnel combat the intense factory fire in Brazil.



The inferno broke out at a solvent plant in Itaquaquecetuba, Greater São Paulo around 3pm.

Video and images from the scene show giant flames roaring from the factory with plumes of opaque smoke rising over 100ft into the air.



Officials have confirmed “multiple explosions” have occurred at the scene.

Footage shows a chemical drum launched into the air as extreme pressure builds from the burning materials.

Dense columns of smoke burst from drains as the thick gas it is forced underground.

In one video a manhole cover exploding from the ground, with local media reporting that the blast knocked a passerby off their feet.



The operation is considered complex as there are 24 solvent tanks in the factory – literally adding fuel to the flames.

Additionally, the fire is concentrated in an industrial area which contains highly volatile products, further increasing the risks of explosions.

Sao Paulo’s military fire brigade said: “No record of victims so far.”



It is understood that electricity has been cut in the immediate area and 150 have been evacuated.

The company affected is Quema Química, which produces and markets solvents and polyester resins.

The factory has 24 solvent storage tanks, each with an approximate capacity of 31 cubic meters.

Fire crews continue to tackle the blaze.

News.title: Mum of murdered teen distraught after ‘son’s killer considered for early release less than a year after he was jailed’
News.content:
KILLER'S FREEDOM Mum of murdered teen distraught after ‘son’s killer considered for early release less than a year after he was jailed’

THE MUM of a murdered teen has been left distraught after hearing one of her son’s killers is being considered for early release – less than a year after he was jailed.

Daejaun Campbell, 15, was killed in Woolwich, south-east London, after he was fatally stabbed with a “zombie” knife in September 2024.



The schoolboy was found on the street crying as he begged: “Please. I’m 15. Don’t let me die”.

Imre Doue was found guilty of murder and sentenced to a minimum 21 years in prison last October following a six-week trial at the Old Bailey.



Meanwhile, Marko Balaz was convicted of manslaughter and was jailed for a minimum term of 11 years.

But now, Daejaun’s mum Jodian Taylor, says she has been informed that gang-member Balaz is being considered for early release while Doue intends to appeal his sentence, reports Metro.

She told the outlet: “I was at the park when I found out, and it was so distressing.

“I already don’t think justice has been served. This undermines it even more.



“I feel like I am not allowed to grieve.”

The grieving mum had spoken about how authorities had failed her son and told BBC Panorama earlier this year how they had failed to get him away from drug dealers who had groomed him.

A review, published by the Greenwich Safeguarding Children Partnership (GSCP) last month, found that Taylor had repeatedly flagged her concerns in the lead-up to his death.

In that review, she penned a touching tribute to Daejaun, saying the world had lost “an extraordinary human being — a son, grandson, brother, nephew, cousin and friend”.

She added: “He was loyal to a fault, loving, caring, compassionate, helpful, understanding and a brilliant communicator. He was playful, cheeky, and had a light that shone in his own unique way.”



It comes after it emerged the two killers of hero PC Andrew Harper will still get an early release halfway through their jail-terms.

Albert Bowers and Jessie Cole were jailed for 13 years in 2020 for the manslaughter of the 28-year-old officer.

The pair, who were 17 at the time of the offense in August 2019, were passengers in the car that dragged PC Harper for more than a mile along country roads in Berkshire when his ankles got caught in a towrope loop.

Petition to stop the early release from jail of PC Andrew Harper's killers Aileen O'Connor, Thames Valley Police Federation Chair, has launched a petition demanding a stop to the early release of PC Harper's killers. The petition has already soared past 100,000 signatures after it was posted earlier on Tuesday. Hundreds more have taken to the comments to show their support after the Government’s decision on PC Harper’s killers sparked outrage across the country. O’Connor said in the petition that she was “absolutely outraged” at both the Prime Minister, Andy Burnham, and Justice Secretary, Alex Norris. She challenged them to “explain why those responsible for killing a police officer should still be eligible for early release”. The decision, she said, “is an insult to Andrew’s family, his friends, his colleagues and the entire policing family”. O’Connor added they have watched a “justice system that they trusted” fail to recognise the sacrifices made by those who “serve and protect the public”. It sends a “deeply troubling message” about the value the Government places on people who have made those sacrifices, she continued. O’Connor concluded with a defiant message, saying: “I will not stand by while the voices of Andrew’s family, his colleagues and police officers across this country continue to be ignored.” To sign the petition click here.

Now, following a review, there will be no change to manslaughter cases, which means the two thugs could be out in months.

Furious widow Lissie Harper, 35, blasted the decision as “disgusting” and an “utter betrayal”.



“I’m beyond appalled and bristling with anger to hear Andrew’s killers are soon to be free,” she fumed.

“The level of disrespect the Government are showing to Andrew and other victims, and their loved ones such as me, is beyond contempt.”

Aileen O’Connor, Thames Valley Police Federation Chair, said today in The Sun that the decision to set them free was the “final betrayal from the politicians, who are supposed to be on our side”.

A petition launched by Ms O’Connor passed 100,000 verified signatures on Tuesday evening.

It demands Mr Burnham and Mr Norris “explain why those responsible” for the killing should be eligible for release.



The Sentencing Act was passed in January meaning offenders on standard fixed sentences and due to be released after half their term will now leave after a third.

Violent offenders who would have been freed at two thirds of a sentence will now be out after half.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Prime Minister, Andy Burnham had raised hopes he could block the move but decided prisons are too full to exclude manslaughter from the scheme.

He now faces being taken to court by furious cops for failing to halt the early release of PC Harper’s killers with his family understood to be backing the move.

News.title: Defence firm staff told not to take phones to Wes Streeting speech over fears of Chinese spying
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

SPY THREAT Defence firm staff told not to take phones to Wes Streeting speech over fears of Chinese spying

STAFF at British defence firms were told not to take phones to Wes Streeting’s first speech as Defence Secretary over fears of Chinese spying.

Streeting spoke at an arms fair packed with Chinese firms – including an electronic warfare specialist that list signals “cracking” as a flagship service.

Workers at Britain’s List X defence firms – which hold secret government contracts – were advised to leave phones, tablets and other devices outside the exhibition hall where Streeting delivered his keynote address.

The Sun understands that government staff took no special precautions.





More than 20 Chinese firms had stands at the Farnborough International Air Show earlier this month.

China was the only country to book two “national pavilions” to showcase its technology.

Yet sources claimed the threat of espionage was an “open secret” among industry.

China firms had surrounded the stage where Streeting warned: “State-on-state competition has returned on a scale not seen for a generation.”



Defence giant BAE Systems unveiled a flagship new drone designed to fly with RAF Top Guns.

Defence minister Luke Pollard and AI Minister Kanishka Narayan also attended the show.

When The Sun approached Beijing based LZ Tech’s stand – which was displaying anti-drone antennas – its staffed barked “no photos” before leaving the stage to avoid appearing in images.

The company, which is not accused of any wrongdoing and did not respond to a request for comment, said it “pioneers Cognitive Radio Protocol Cracking (and AI Radio Protocol Cracking technologies”.



It lists is expertise as “cybersecurity, wireless communications, and information protection”.

A defence source said mobile phones often overheated at Farnborough – in a sign hackers could have targeted them to download information.

However, UK security sources claimed the risks of hacks were low.

Former Col Phil Ingram, who served in military intelligence questioned why Chinese firms were invited.

He said: “Why are Chinese companies allowed at Farnborough?



“They will be gathering intelligence on all other exhibitors and as many visitors as possible.”

Earlier this year it emerged a Chinese tracker was found attached to the Prime Minister’s car in 2022.

Separately Chinese electric vehicles have been banned from parking near sensitive UK military sites over risks they could be used as sensors.

Chinese law requires all Chinese nationals to help spy if requested.

Military Top Brass have also been warned not to hold sensitive conversations inside Chinese cars over fears of eavesdropping.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

The government insisted China was welcome at Farnborough as they are free to trade with Britain.

A government spokesperson said: “We take security seriously and regularly take steps to protect personnel, capabilities and technology in the interests of UK security.”

Correctional officer Jordan Pensak, 27, is accused of having sex with a prisoner on multiple occasions – sending him messages detailing her desire for his “big man hands”, according to court documents.



Over 100 sexually explicit messages, photos and videos, were discovered on Pensak’s phone, court documents reveal.

Last week she was charged with one count of sexual abuse of an individual in federal custody.

News.title: Cabinet minister forced to defend Andy Burnham’s decision to take holiday just 15 days into premiership
News.content:
A CABINET Minister was forced to defend Andy Burnham for taking a holiday just 15 days into his Premiership.

The new PM was warned by a senior Labour backbencher that he was making a “mistake”.



Backbencher Graham Stringer told Talk: “He will come to regret it.”

But Justice Secretary Alex Norris insisted the PM – whose location is being kept secret by No10 – will be “in constant contact with his office”.



He added: “ I mean, I might gently say that I’ve spoken to him virtually every day since I joined the cabinet, and I suspect that won’t change.”

Downing Street said Andy Burnham would be taking some time off to spend it with his wife and family. Number 10 refused to say where he was travelling.

Louise Haigh – previously sacked by ex-PM Sir Keir Starmer over a fraud conviction – is in charge as Mr Burnham’s deputy while he is away from his desk.

It is common for Prime Ministers to take a break in August when Parliament is not sitting.

But Mr Burnham is by far the earliest UK premier to take a holiday after just 15 days into the job he has craved all of his life.

Parliament will return in early September for a couple of weeks before a second recess for the party conference season.



Theresa May comes second closest after jetting off after just four weeks.

Within recent years Rishi Sunak took the longest to take time off after working non-stop for nine months after becoming Prime Minister.

Reform UK blasted Mr Burnham for taking a break this early in his premiership.



Chairman Lee Anderson MP said: “Two weeks into the job and Andy Burnham has already had enough.

“After dropping a number of unfunded commitments and overseeing over 2,000 illegal migrants breaking into our country he’s bunked off for a jolly abroad. This isn’t a Prime Minister that’s serious about leading.”

The Prime Minister also told Elizabeth Day on the How To Fail podcast his wife was shocked he wanted to run again as Labour leader.

He said: “’What? Not again. They told you twice they don’t want you. Why are you doing it again?’”

“No, we’ve always just had honest conversations about it.”



Mr Burnham added: “She took some persuading, to be honest, because I guess she didn’t want to see me go through it all again and then end out on the wrong side, at the end of it. But she gives me good advice.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Downing Street refused to say where the PM would be travelling.

He will be accompanied by security.

News.title: Mystical UK beauty spot dubbed the ‘Devil’s Pulpit’ is put up for sale – and it’s even featured in a blockbuster TV show
News.content:
HELL OF A BUY Mystical UK beauty spot dubbed the ‘Devil’s Pulpit’ is put up for sale – and it’s even featured in a blockbuster TV show

A MYSTICAL UK beauty spot dubbed the “Devil’s Pulpit” has been put up for sale – but the price remains a mystery.

The breathtaking Finnich Glen in Stirlingshire, Scotland, has been featured in blockbuster TV shows, including Outlander.



Tucked away 15 miles outside Glasgow near Killearn and Drymen, the beautiful 23-acre sandstone gorge attracts 70,000 visitors every year.

Adventurers flock to the site to tackle the 1.5-mile trail, clambering down ancient steps to swim in the gorge.



Formed between 10,000 and 12,000 years ago by melting glaciers, the 80ft-deep gorge is steeped in dark folklore.

Local tales link it to ancient druids, witches, and the Devil himself.



TV fans will recognise its roaring waterfall as “St Ninian’s Spring” from the smash-hit drama Outlander.

The sandstone bedrock, which appears to run blood red due to the sediment in the water, means the gorge has been a popular set for television and film.



Hits such as Sherlock Holmes, Taggart, Pokemon Detective Pikachu and King Arthur have all used the stunning location.

After previously being put on the market in 2023, the spectacular Devil’s Pulpit has gone up for sale again, but without a clear asking price.

However, potential buyers will be pleased to learn that there is approved planning permission for a brand-new visitor centre.



It will be complete with a cafe, restaurant, event space, and dedicated car park.

The upgrades are expected to increase visitor numbers to more than 300,000 a year.

Commercial estate agents Christie & Co are handling the sale on an “offers invited” basis.

The current owners said: “We feel that we have reached a stage in life where new owners would be able to take forward our vision for the Glen and develop this opportunity in a way that is compatible with this unique property.

“The Glen requires management to preserve and protect its environment, but whoever purchases Finnich Glen, taking it to the next phase, has the opportunity to follow in the footsteps of giants.”



Mark Lavery, director of retail and leisure at Christie & Co, said: “This opportunity will appeal to buyers who want to create a commercial business and unique visitor experience with national importance, against a stunning backdrop.

“Historically important, and already a tourist attraction with approved planning permission, the development opportunities are exciting, and we encourage interested parties to get in touch.”

News.title: Dad, 66, desperately tried to save daughter, 32, after she was swept off rocks while fishing before both drowned
News.content:
DOUBLE TRAGEDY Dad, 66, desperately tried to save daughter, 32, after she was swept off rocks while fishing before both drowned

A DAD and a daughter drowned after he desperately tried to save her as she was dragged out to sea while fishing at a popular surfing beach, an inquest heard.

John Collins, 66, and Samantha Collins, 32, both died on Fistral Beach in Newquay, Cornwall on Sunday July 26.



The inquest at Cornwall Coroner’s Court in Truro heard on Tuesday that John, a retired technical manager from Doncaster, South Yorkshire, had been on holiday in Newquay with his daughter Samantha and wife Adele Collins.

The pair were pulled out of the water unconscious by surfers and beachgoers and sadly were pronounced dead at the scene.



Assistant Coroner for Cornwall & Isles of Scilly, Emma Hillson, told the court: “John and Samantha were fishing on rocks when Samantha was dragged into the sea.

“John tried to save her but very sadly was unable to do so and both lost their lives.”



In both cases Ms Hillson gave a provisional cause of death as drowning and adjourned the inquest until 19 July 2027.

The 750-metre-long Fistral Beach has massive winter wave swells and is known as the “home of British surfing”, drawing up to one million visitors each year.



Witness Jamie Stockwell previously revealed how he plunged into the sea fully dressed in a bid to save Samantha.

He said: “I jumped in with all my clothes on. I didn’t realise how deep it was. It was very powerful swell, and I was lucky I wasn’t another casualty.

“We were being hurled on to the rocks. I managed to push her up and her boyfriend pulled her up by the arms and started to try to give her mouth-to-mouth.

“We tried to give her CPR for about ten minutes. I was trying to keep her partner calm as he was in pieces.”

Sand Phoenix, who was on the Beach when the tragedy unfolded, revealed he “sprinted” up to help after seeing John go in after his daughter.



The 33-year-old added: “He had been pulled out of the water but had been in there about seven minutes.

“I had an adrenaline pen which I jabbed him with and tried to give him oxygen but his lungs were full of water and there was no response.

“The paramedics arrived and carried on trying to give CPR. He was still wearing his trousers so I don’t think he had been swimming.

“It looks like they had been walking near the rocks and had fallen in.”

One eyewitness who was staying in a van overlooking the beach said: “First thing I heard was a man shouting ‘we need ropes, they are drowning’.



“I made my way down there and there were two people in the water, a lady next to me spotted a body floating in the water and the other one was already on the beach with people.

“A woman on the cliff was desperately trying to ring her husband and daughter but neither was picking up.”

Cops earlier said Samantha entered the water carrying a peach or orange coloured handbag which has not been recovered.

The leather-style bag is said to contain a number of personal items of “great sentimental value to her loved ones” as the force appeal for it to be handed in if found.

Cops said in a statement: “Police were called by the South Western Ambulance Service at around 9.45pm on Sunday 26 July following reports that two people had been recovered from the water at Fistral Beach, Newquay.



“Emergency services attended and a cordon was put in place, which has since been removed.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Sadly, a woman in her 30s and a man in his 60s were pronounced deceased at the scene.

“Their families have been informed, and our thoughts are with them at this extremely difficult time.”

News.title: Mum of murdered teen distraught after 'son’s killer considered for early release'
News.content:
Mum of murdered teen distraught after 'son’s killer considered for early release'

Jodian Taylor, mum of 15-year-old Daejaun Campbell stabbed to death in London, says she has been informed that Balaz, who was convicted of manslaughter, is being considered for early release

View 4 Images Daejaun Campbell's mother, Joelle Taylor, has shared her thoughts on the early release scheme (Image: PA)

The mum of a murdered teenage boy has been left distraught after hearing one of his killers is being considered for early release.

‌



Daejaun Campbell, 15, was found on the street in Woolwich, south-east London, after he was fatally stabbed with a “zombie” knife in September 2024.

‌



Two men were convicted in relation to his death. Imre Doue was found guilty of murder and sentenced to a minimum 21 years in prison last October. Meanwhile, Marko Balaz was convicted of manslaughter and was jailed for a minimum term of 11 years.

‌



View 4 Images 15-year-old Daejaun Campbell (Image: PA)

Police Federation threatens legal action over early release of PC Andrew Harper's killers READ MORE :

But now, Daejaun’s mum Jodian Taylor, says she has been informed that Balaz is being considered for early release while Doue intends to appeal his sentence, reports Metro.

She told the outlet: “I was at the park when I found out, and it was so distressing. I already don’t think justice has been served. This undermines it even more. I feel like I am not allowed to grieve.”

‌



Under the Sentencing Act, which became law earlier this year, prisoners serving time for some violent or sexual offences will become eligible for release halfway through their sentences, rather than serving the current tariff of two-thirds. Criminals including burglars and thieves are among prisoners who will be considered for release a third of the way through their sentences, down from the current 40%.

View 4 Images Marko Balaz who was sentenced to 11 year in custody at the Old Bailey for his part in the death of 15-year-old Daejaun Campbell (Image: PA)

On Monday night, the PM announced anyone found guilty of rape, serious child sexual offences and grooming will be blocked from the early release scheme, which will now come into force in October.

‌



He admitted he wanted to go even further and ban other offenders from having their time in prison shortened. Mr Burnham assured the public that offenders would face tighter community supervision, including curfews and electronic tagging.

Mr Burnham added: “I want to be honest - I wanted to go even further as I know there will still be concerns about other offenders having their sentence shortened. But it’s not possible without the prison system reaching capacity and collapsing, which would put public safety at much greater risk."

Dozens of familys have already come foward and shared their disgust after being told those responsible for killing their loved ones could be freed early thanks to the early release scheme.

‌



View 4 Images The mother of Pc Andrew Harper says her family is "paying the price" after learning her son's killers remain eligible for early release (Image: Thames Valley Police/PA Wire)

Pc Harper was 28 years old when he sustained fatal injuries while responding to a quad bike theft in Sulhamstead, Berkshire, in August 2019. He died after getting caught in a strap attached to the back of a car and dragged down a country road as three teenage suspects fled the scene of the burglary.

Jessie Cole and Albert Bowers, who were passengers in the car and both 17 years old at the time, were handed 13 years in custody for manslaughter after a trial at the Old Bailey in 2020.

Article continues below

Now, the Ministry of Justice (MoJ) has confirmed both men may be eligible to be released from prison halfway through their sentences.

Furious widow Lissie Harper, 35, told The Sun: “This is disgusting. I’m beyond appalled and bristling with anger to hear Andrew’s killers are soon to be free."

She added: "“The Government and justice system have not just let me down, they have added insult to injury. This is an utter betrayal, one I will not be able to forgive or forget.”

News.title: Shocking moment politician is knocked out after getting into argument on packed beach
News.content:
Shocking moment politician is knocked out after getting into argument on packed beach

Kirill Basin, 40, got into a very public confrontation which was caught on video by stunned bystanders - it is not the first time the politician has landed himself in trouble

View 4 Images Basin (R) tried to swing a beach chair during the confrontation

A US politician has been caught on camera in his underwear, shouting and threatening people with a knife at a beach in Hawaii. Kirill Basin, 40, was spotted flying into a rage at Keawakapu Beach in South Kihei on the island of Maui because he was asked by his fellow beachgoers to turn his music down. At one point, Basin can be seen confronting a group of beachgoers before retreating and saying: “I told him if he wants to go to the hospital, come here.” It didn't take long to have both his confidence - and the wind - knocked out of him. As the situation continued to escalate, the wannabe congressional candidate got into an altercation with a large tattooed man. As Basin tried to swing a beach chair at him, he received a right-handed punch which knocked the Hawaii Democrat out cold.

‌



View 4 Images The shocking fight was captured on video

‌



The larger man went on to Basin’s sternum until he woke up before telling him clearly: “Watch your f***king mouth, Haole [a pejorative term islanders call white people] boy." But, it would seem the Hawaii Democrat didn't get the message, going back for more while yelling after the man that he would “go to jail". He also ran at the larger man and shouted: "Come on, b***h!” He then allegedly pulled a knife on the man, which witnesses say he tossed into the sea. He also claimed he had a gun, as per bystanders. Police later recovered the knife.

‌



View 4 Images Kirill Basin, 40, was caught on camera in his underwear, shouting and threatening people relaxing at Keawakapu Beach in South Kihei after a 61-year-old man told him to turn his music down

The only person arrested after the bizarre beach flare-up was Basin, who has been charged with two counts of first-degree terroristic threatening. Bail has been set at $1 million. Basin will challenge Republican Jill Tokuda for Hawaii’s second congressional district on August 8. It is not known if Basin will still be on remand at that time. This is not the Democratic congressional candidate’s first run-in with the law. It is understood he pulled a gun on officials in May, threatening two Maui County workers, after storming a government building in Wailuku, as per Civil Beat. The wild move landed him in handcuffs and charged with terrorist threatening in the first degree.

Article continues below

View 4 Images 40-year-old Kirill Basin

It is thought that this run-in with the law is the same one that Basin bizarrely referenced on social media last Thursday, the day before his latest arrest. In that Instagram post, Basin claimed that police had tortured him. He said: "This is the lawsuit I served today. It basically outlines how three police officers tortured me for 14 hours. That’s the gist. It’ll never happen to anyone again.”

News.title: Man arrested for ‘murder’ of beloved dad, 36, shot dead at UK traveller site
News.content:
Man arrested for ‘murder’ of beloved dad, 36, shot dead at UK traveller site

A suspect, aged 35, has been arrested on suspicion of murder after a dad, labelled a 'legend' was shot dead at a UK traveller site on Sunday, with the total arrests now reaching five

View 2 Images Jimmy Ward was shot dead at a UK traveller site (Image: Jimmy Ward/Facebook)

A man has been arrested on suspicion of murder following the shooting of a 'beloved dad' at a UK traveller site.

The suspect, aged 35, was arrested on August 4 in relation to the shooting at a traveller site in Calcutt at around 8.15am on Sunday morning.

Jimmy Ward, 36, was declared dead at the scene, with his family in 'disbelief' that he is gone.

Wiltshire Police also arrested two other men, aged 53 and 29, on August 4 on suspicion of assisting an offender following a vehicle stop on the A419, taking the total number of people arrested to five.

View 2 Images A police cordon remains in place at the site (stock image) (Image: Getty Images)

All five people are in custody for questioning.

A cordon, which was put in place at the site following the shooting, remains in place with an increased policing presence.

The police said that this will remain in place in the coming days while further enquiries continue at the site.

Senior Investigating Officer Detective Chief Inspector Phil Walker said: “This is a significant development in our investigation.

“I can confirm that a man has been arrested on suspicion of Jimmy’s murder and is now in police custody, along with four other people on suspicion of assisting an offender.

“Jimmy’s next of kin have been informed of this development and my thoughts continue to be with them. They are being supported by specially trained officers.

“A scene and heavy policing presence remain in place at the traveller site in Calcutt while further enquiries are carried out. I continue to ask that this cordon is respected.

Article continues below

“I’d like to thank the local community for their support and patience since Sunday. We understand this incident has caused significant concern, so please consider speaking with officers about any information or concerns you may have.”

News.title: Trump to hand Iran 'control it didn't have before war' in deal to re-open Strait of Hormuz
News.content:
Trump to hand Iran 'control it didn't have before war' in deal to re-open Strait of Hormuz

About 20% of all global oil traded passed through the Strait of Hormuz prior to the conflict, which sparked after the US and Israel carried out joint strikes on several Iranian sites

View 3 Images (Image: AP Photo/Alex Brandon)

The US, Iran, and Oman are reported to be nearing an interim agreement to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, Axios news outlet reported, citing two regional sources and a US official.

‌



According to the report, the US is aiming for an announcement on Wednesday.

‌



The critical waterway has been a contentious issue in the US-Iran war. The US and Israel carried out joint strikes on several key Iranian sites on February 28 and Iran retaliated by striking sites across the Middle East and closing the strait.

‌



View 3 Images Thai-flagged cargo ship Mayuree Naree on fire after being hit by Iranian missiles in the Strait of Hormuz, Iran on March 11, 2026 (Image: ROYAL THAI NAVY/HANDOUT/EPA/Shutterstock)

About 20% of all global oil traded passed through the Strait of Hormuz prior to the conflict, but its closure has choked the flow of oil out of the Middle East, caused volatility in global markets and driven up fuel prices at the pumps.

The US and Iran signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) on June 17 to bring the war to a close within 60 days.

‌



Washington and Tehran were working towards securing a lasting peace agreement, restore international shipping through the Strait of Hormuz and seek to settle an ongoing dispute over Tehran's nuclear programme.

However, the agreement was short-lived and conflict resumed not even one month after the MoU was signed.

It is understood that the Axios-reported interim agreement has been under negotiations for several weeks.

‌



It is aimed at resuming the ceasefire between the US and Iran and restarting negotiations over a nuclear deal.

Axios reports that the potential "deal would meet some of Iran's demands for greater control over traffic in the Strait of Hormuz - control it didn't have before the war."

View 3 Images Vessels are seen anchored in Bandar Abbas along the Strait of Hormuz (file image) (Image: Getty)

‌



The deal being discussed will enable a 60-day temporary arrangement between Oman and Iran in the strait, which could be extended, according to the sources.

Axios reports that the deal would include the following points:

All inbound traffic of ships through the strait and into the Gulf would go in a northern lane through Iranian waters

All outbound traffic through the strait and into the Arabian Sea would go in a southern lane through Omani waters, in coordination with Iran

No tolls or fees would be charged during the 60-day period

The parties would work on clearing naval mines from the median lane of the strait within 30 days

After the median lane is cleared, it would be used for inbound and outbound traffic under the terms of a permanent arrangement to be negotiated between Oman and Iran

Article continues below

US President Donald Trump decided not to follow through on threats of a massive bombing campaign to provide for to more time for diplomacy. If a deal is not reached soon, however, Trump could green-light major strikes.

Speaking to Fox News, Mr Trump said: "The Strait is going to be open very soon - or they're gonna hit very hard, and then the Strait is going to be open."

News.title: Man to appear in court today after body of British woman found in suitcase in Greece
News.content:
Man to appear in court today after body of British woman found in suitcase in Greece

The suspect has been widely identified as 26-year-old Afghan boxer Sharif Ahmadzai, who reportedly fled Afghanistan after being orphaned in his teens

View 4 Images Elisabeth Jane Ross, also known as Lisa, was found by a homeless man on July 18. (Image: Facebook)

A man accused of killing a Scottish woman and disposing of her body in a suitcase in Athens is due to appear before a Greek court.

‌



The court appearance will come days after harrowing CCTV footage went public, that allegedly recorded the accused murderer of Edinburgh woman Elisabeth Jane Ross as he pushed her body through the streets of the Greek capital of Athens in a suitcase.

‌



Authorities have not publicly confirmed his identity, but it has been widely reported that the man who stands accused of the 38-year-old woman's murder is Sharif Ahmadzai, 26, originally from Afghanistan.

‌



In the chilling video, a man dressed in a black T-shirt, shorts, and carrying a blue rucksack can be seen lugging the large, black case through the city centre. The footage tracks the path of the man, believed to be Ahmadzai, as he slowly made his way towards an abandoned building in Kypseli on July 16.

View 4 Images CCTV shows a man wheeling a suitcase through Athens streets (Image: INSTAGRAM)

It is alleged that it was there, in the normally quiet central Athens neighbourhood, that he abandoned the body of the Ms Ross, also known as Lisa, before leaving the area. Her remains were discovered two days later, on July 18, by a homeless man, who contacted police after making the grim discovery.

‌



Officers said the suspect was taken in for questioning after investigators examined surveillance footage captured near the abandoned building.

Police have confirmed that the 26-year-old arrested in connection with the crime was initially detained on illegal weapons possession charges. He is now facing a murder charge as well as allegations that he stole more than 10,000 euro from the victim’s bank accounts using her bank cards, police said.

Greek officials said he has admitted to moving the body, but has denied the murder allegations.

‌



After allegedly murdering Ms Ross, Ahmadzai is accused of sending a series of messages from her phone to her friends and family before switching off the device. Her loved ones became concerned when they continued receiving text messages that appeared uncharacteristic of her writing style.

View 4 Images Sharif Ahmadzai

In addition to allegedly posing as his murder victim, Ahmadzai is believed to have bought another phone to text Ms Ross' friends in Athens - including his wife - to cover his tracks. Greek newspapers Proto Thema and Ta Nea reported that in the messages, Ahmadzai purported to be an unnamed jihadist that claimed he had killed the Scot because of her religion.

‌



Ms Ross is believed to have died between five and seven days before she was found, during a heatwave in which temperatures reached 36C.

Greece’s national police the Hellenic Police were able to identify Ms Ross using her fingerprints. Authorities are awaiting the results of tissue analysis to determine whether she died from suffocation, as suggested by a preliminary assessment by the medical examiner.

View 4 Images Sharif Ahmadzai

Article continues below

The Foreign and Commonwealth Office said earlier: “Our thoughts are with Elisabeth’s family during this difficult time. We are providing consular support and are in contact with the local authorities.”

A Police Scotland spokesperson previously said: “We are aware of the death of a Scottish woman in Athens and are liaising with authorities in Greece. Officers are providing support to her family in Scotland.”

News.title: Australian woman charged with murder after allegedly starving man with Down's Syndrome to death
News.content:
Australian woman charged with murder after allegedly starving man with Down's Syndrome to death

WARNING: DISTRESSING CONTENT Investigations into the death of 56-year-old Isaac, who has Down's Syndrome and was non-verbal, have been complex, but a woman has now been charged with his murder

View 2 Images The conditions inside the home were shocking (Image: Queensland Police)

Police have shared the horror conditions found inside a home where a man who had Down's Syndrome was found dead now a woman has been charged with his murder.

‌



At around 9.18pm on Thursday August 10, 2023, emergency services were called to an Alice Street residence in Ayr, south of Townsville in Queensland, after Isaac, also known as ‘Ike’, was located unresponsive. He was pronounced deceased at the scene. Due to the circumstances, police commenced a suspicious death investigation, and a crime scene was established.

‌



Investigations into the death of 56-year-old Isaac, who has Down's Syndrome and was non-verbal, have been complex, with detectives conducting extensive and thorough inquiries into his health, care and treatment throughout his life.

‌



View 2 Images Disturbing footage captured the squalor found inside the home (Image: Queensland Police)

Extensive investigations and forensic medical examinations were conducted, including a thorough post-mortem, which revealed Isaac was experiencing serious malnourishment weighing just 29kg at the time of his death.

‌



Following a 'complex' three-year investigation, a woman aged 70, has now been arrested by police and charged with murder on Tuesday.

Bodycam footage showed the moment police visited the home and the inside of the property was in complete disarray. Officers were forced to walk through narrow ravines, with cardboard boxes and various miscellaneous piled on either side. Furniture was completely hidden by clothes and containers.

A Queensland Police statement reads: "Detectives from the Crime Command Homicide Investigation Unit and Ayr Criminal Investigation Branch have charged a woman following investigations into the death of a 56-year-old man in Ayr in August 2023.

Article continues below

"A 70-year-old Forest Lake woman was arrested by detectives yesterday and charged with one count of murder (domestic violence). She is expected to appear in the Brisbane Magistrates Court today.

"On 10 August 2023, emergency services were called to an Alice Street residence after the man was located unresponsive. He was pronounced deceased at the scene. Due to the circumstances, police commenced an investigation, and a crime scene was established.

"Investigations into the death of the man have been complex, with detectives conducting extensive and thorough inquiries into his health, care, and treatment throughout his life."

News.title: England's longest zip wire finally opens after 15 years - stunning views
News.content:
England's longest zip wire finally opens after 15 years - stunning views

The site briefly closed in 1989 but was reopened in 1997 by Mark Weir, who aimed to develop the area as England's last working slate mine and an adventure site

View 3 Images England's longest zip wire has opened (Image: Honister Slate Mine)

England's longest zipline has opened after 15 years, with spectacular views of a famous national park.

‌



Visitors to the zip wire in Honister Slate Mine, in Cumbria will be led more than 2,000 feet up to the summit. They will then soar 1,200 metres across from Honister Crag to the valley below.

‌



Tickets start from £110 for the 60-second experience. Only a limited number of riders will be able to go this year.

‌



View 3 Images Aerial view looking up the east side of the Honister Pass towards the Slate Mine (Image: Getty)

The attraction, set in the Lake District, reaches speeds of up to 65 mph.

The area housed a historic slate mine for more than a century.

‌



The site briefly closed in 1989 but was reopened in 1997 by Mark Weir, who aimed to develop the area as England's last working slate mine and an adventure site.

Weir's sons, Prentice and Piers Wilkinson Weir, now run the business.

They told the Cumbria Crack: "As we celebrate 30 years since our dad bought Honister, we're proud to continue building on his vision while looking firmly to the future.

‌



"This zip wire represents our commitment to investing in Honister, creating unforgettable experiences for our visitors, supporting the local economy and ensuring this incredible place continues to thrive for generations to come."

View 3 Images A view towards Rydal Water and the forest around Grasmere (Image: Getty)

The zip wire took more than 15 years to develop and will continue to transport slate from the mountain as it was originally intended to do.

Article continues below

Another attraction at Honister is The Infinity Bridge - a 190m high-wire bridge suspended between two mountains.

Via Ferrata - a 2,000ft semi-vertical ascent - is also available at the site.

News.title: Burnham 'looking into' conducting Epstein inquiry, says victims minister
News.content:
Andy Burnham is "looking into" the possibility of holding a public inquiry into the UK activities of the convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein, according to victims minister Alex Davies-Jones.

Speaking to BBC Newsnight, Davies-Jones said that the prime minister had agreed to meet Epstein's victims.

She said the government is also reviewing whether the alleged actions of former Harrods owner Mohamed Al Fayed could also be part of an inquiry.

Davies-Jones resigned from former Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer's government in May, later accusing his government of failing to listen to Epstein's survivors. She was reappointed as victims minister when Burnham took office.

Speaking on the programme, she said she had discussed holding a public inquiry into the alleged behaviour of Epstein and Al Fayed with the prime minister and cabinet secretary Dame Antonia Romeo during her re-appointment.

Asked whether an inquiry was now possible, Davies-Jones said: "We are looking at this, we are reviewing what is possible. Again, same with Harrods survivors."

She added: "I have been assured that the prime minister is taking this very seriously.

"He will meet with those victims and he is looking at what is possible, now he has access to all of the information as prime minister to see what action we can take."

After resigning in May, Davies-Jones told the Commons in June that people whose lives were devastated by Epstein's abuse have too often been reduced to a footnote.

Asked what assurances or guarantees she had asked from Burnham in relation to the survivors when he re-appointed her to government, the minister said: "I did have those discussions with the prime minister before he became the prime minister."

"He agreed to meet with the Epstein victims," she continued, adding that Burnham "has assured me that he will meet them now he's prime minister and will work with us to look at systemic change across the system for all victims."

BBC Newsnight understands that as Burnham was finalising plans to become prime minister, he was sent a document by leading Labour campaigners on Violence Against Women and Girls.

It contained a key suggestion: to hold a full public inquiry into the UK activities of Epstein, the alleged behaviour of the late Harrods boss Mohamed Al Fayed and into allegations in a BBC Panorama and Times investigation that West Ham co-owner David Sullivan preyed on women.

David Sullivan has described the claims as false. He said he was "absolutely not the person the media has decided to paint me as".

The document called for an "impunity" inquiry to ask how powerful men were able to carry out the alleged behaviour.

On Epstein, the document calls for a focus on UK borders, asking how he was able to fly in and out of UK military bases on his private jet, often with allegedly trafficked women. Former Prime Minister Gordon Brown highlighted this issue in February.

Davies-Jones is understood to be familiar with the Labour document.

Anouska di Georgiou, an Epstein survivor, told BBC Newsnight: "I welcome reports that Prime Minister Andy Burnham is considering public inquiries into the Epstein and Maxwell, Harrods/Mohamed Al-Fayed, and David Sullivan cases."

"Survivors have heard promises before, so what matters now is action, not headlines."

News.title: Dewormer and scabies drugs being sold as cancer treatments, BBC investigation finds
News.content:
Animal dewormer and a drug used to treat scabies are being sold and promoted as unproven cancer treatments, a BBC investigation has found.

Following a tip off, an undercover journalist was able to buy fenbendazole and ivermectin from a stairlift salesman in south Wales and also found them for sale on Amazon.

Macmillan Cancer Support said it was concerned by the findings and that a growing number of people were asking about the medicines, despite "no clinical evidence" that they work.

Amazon removed the products after we contacted them, and said it had "proactive measures in place" to stop prohibited products being listed by third-party sellers.

Senior doctors are worried vulnerable patients could be put at risk by taking the medicines, as they say it could harm or delay conventional treatment.

Six months ago, Rebecca Holder contacted the BBC after a visit from stair lift salesman Jason Sarver.

She said Sarver and her father Bob, who had a brain tumour, lung cancer and needed help with his mobility, had been discussing stair lifts when the salesman changed the topic to talk about the drugs.

News.title: Temperatures to drop briefly ahead of next UK heatwave
News.content:
Temperatures are set to drop across the UK over the next few days, ending the latest heatwave that has affected some areas of southern and eastern England.

Humidity levels will fall too, which should cool down homes and make nights more comfortable for sleeping.

The change in conditions follows another historic day in a summer that has seen many long standing heat records toppled or tied. On Tuesday, the UK registered its 34th day of temperatures reaching 30C (86F) or higher in a calendar year, equalling the record set in 1995.

Forecasts suggest that this record is likely to be beaten as early as next week, with some showing the potential for a sixth heatwave to develop.

News.title: The avalanche that killed a climbing legend - and a generation of record-setting guides
News.content:
Purja, 43, also known as Nims, was the leading figure of the 10-member international team up Broad Peak, the world's 12th highest mountain, when the avalanche struck.

"Nims of course was iconic and undisputedly amongst the best of his generation," says Ben Ayers, a longtime Everest reporter for Outside Magazine.

Kili Pemba Sherpa and Pur Bahadur Gurung, who were also guiding the Broad Peak expedition, were "strong climbers with a solid resume", Ayers said.

Kili Pemba, 46, had just earned the coveted mountaineering Grand Slam after completing his last of the 14 highest peaks, also known as eight-thousanders, in early July.

Even before this crowning achievement, he was already among the best in the industry having been part of the Nepali team, led again by Purja, that completed the first winter ascent of K2 in January 2021.

At the time, K2, the world's second highest peak, was the only one of the eight-thousanders not yet climbed in winter. But at 8,611m, K2 is known to be steeper, more unpredictable and deadlier than Everest (8,849m).

Many have described Kili Pemba as humble and deeply committed in serving his clients. Two of the 15 times he summited Everest he did so guiding double-leg amputees up the mountain.

"That was the toughest task for any guide, [Kili Pemba] did that with a lot of care," says Gyanendra Shrestha, a government official who was at Base Camp during one of these climbs.

News.title: Tories offer Jewish groups meeting with ex neo-Nazi activist candidate
News.content:
The Conservatives have offered Jewish groups a meeting with their council election candidate, Joshua Bonehill-Paine, who spent time in prison for neo-Nazi activism.

The party has been criticised over the decision to select him to stand for a seat on Somerset Council next year, but Kemi Badenoch has said she is standing by Bonehill-Paine because she wants to give him a second chance.

He has described his past views as "indefensible" and now speaks out against extremism.

The Board of Deputies of British Jews has called on the Conservatives to ditch him as a candidate, saying the selection "beggars belief".

It is understood the party has now offered the Board, as well as the Jewish Leadership Council and the Chief Rabbi Sir Ephraim Mirvis, a meeting with Bonehill-Pain so they can discuss their concerns directly.

When Bonehill-Paine's selection was announced, Karen Newman, vice president of the Board of Deputies of British Jews - the largest body representing Jews in the UK - said that the board had contacted the Conservatives to "set out our concerns and call on them to rescind his selection and review their vetting processes."

Bonehill-Paine spent three years in prison for posting antisemitic material ahead of a planned neo-Nazi rally. A year later he was convicted of racially harassing then-Labour MP Luciana Berger. Berger is now a member of the House of Lords.

Bonehill-Paine also holds previous convictions for assaulting a police officer, burglary of a police station and malicious communications.

On Tuesday he was selected to stand as the Tory candidate in the new Somerset Council seat of Crewkerne South in 2027. He said he wanted to "give back" to a community which had supported him.

Berger, reacting to the news of his selection on X, said he had, "published *reams* of deeply racist, misoginistic and pornographic material about me."

She said that the case "still haunts" her.

"I feel a bit sick reading well known commentators debate his selection today and say that 'these are precisely the people we need in public office'."

She added: "For the avoidance of doubt I don't believe this man should have any role in public life, because of both his racism and his view of women.

"Kemi Badenoch you've got this very, very wrong."

Bonehill-Pine said he reformed his previous views when he learned of the murder of MP Jo Cox, and subsequently undertook a de-radicalisation programme. He now delivers counter-extremism sessions around the UK.

He said: "When I was first released from prison in 2018, I was supported by many of the people in my local community who understood that I had made some awful mistakes but was wanting to change my life around."

Speaking on Tuesday, Tory leader Badenoch said Bonehill-Pine "is spending every day working to solve the very problem which he knew he had caused previously.

"He's going up and down the country training people and the Conservative Party believes in second chances.

"This is not just someone that we've picked up who is a convicted criminal - this is somebody who is actively working to help communities, especially Jewish communities."

The decision to field Bonehill-Pine as a candidate has also been criticised by other political parties.

Liberal Democrat MP Adam Dance, whose Yeovil constituency includes Crewkerne, said the Conservative Party needed to explain "why it believes this candidate is fit to serve", while a Labour Party spokesperson said his selection was "a total disgrace".

News.title: Closing down streets so children can play
News.content:
Seven-year-old Aydin is relishing the chance to play somewhere new. It's Colenso Mount, a street in the Holbeck area of Leeds where he lives, which has been temporarily closed to traffic to become a âPlay Streetâ.

"Everyone can ride scooters and the boys over there play football which is very fun", he says excitedly.

As Aydin jumps a scooter over ramps set up in the middle of the road, children around him are drawing with chalk, blowing bubbles and kicking a football in a spot where cars are usually driving through.

Itâs a rare chance for the kids in this neighbourhood to play outside together, in a space big enough to frolic and safe from traffic.

According to a survey from the campaign group Play Their Way, external, out on Wednesday, nearly half of parents (46%) say their child doesn't have a safe place to play outdoors.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham is being urged to bring back a national play strategy, external for children in England - an initiative he championed while culture secretary in 2008.

News.title: Infantino calls executive meeting as criticism mounts
News.content:
Gianni Infantino has summoned senior leaders of football's world governing body to a meeting in Morocco on Wednesday, after another day in which its president has faced fierce criticism of his scrapped plan to sell off Fifa's commercial and event operations.

Fifa's chief of global football development Arsene Wenger, secretary general Mattias Grafstrom, and Prince Ali, president of the Jordanian Football Association, all made clear their opposition to Infantino's Fifa Forward Enterprise.

Infantino, who has been in Morocco over the past week, called an executive meeting in Rabat as he attempts to find a solution to the controversy.

Wenger said in a statement issued through Fifa that scrapping the plan was "absolutely necessary and beyond question".

Grafstrom called the last week "a sad and reproachable series of events" in an internal email to Fifa staff.

Prince Ali, meanwhile, accused Fifa of creating a situation which "amounts to blackmail" over unpaid prize money and support for Infantino's re-election.

Wenger has been in a role which encompasses data analysis of the game, Fifa's online training and youth competitions, since 2019.

The former Arsenal boss previously supported Infantino's proposal to play the men's World Cup every two years.

A week after Infantino's investment plan was first released, the Frenchman issued a statement through Fifa in which he demanded "transparency and integrity" from the body.

"The recent events at Fifa deserve some clarity from my side," Wenger's statement read.

"I was not involved in this strategic plan and first became aware of the project through media reports.

"The decision to withdraw the project was absolutely necessary and beyond question, because I firmly believe in an independent Fifa that serves our game with commitment, transparency, and integrity."

Wenger is one of 18 Fifa officials named in a document preservation letter Uefa sent to Fifa threatening legal action.

Carlos Cordeiro - Infantino's senior adviser on global strategy and governance - is the only Fifa official to resign over the scandal, saying the proposal was "a bad deal for football" and would "mortgage football's future".

News.title: Couple woke to find shirtless intruder in Travelodge room
News.content:
A couple woke to find a shirtless man in their hotel bedroom after he was mistakenly given a key card to their door, BBC Scotland News has learned.

Kim Hutchison, 60, and Harry Grieve, 57, from Buckie, Moray, were staying in a Travelodge in Dundee when the early morning incident happened last month.

Hutchison said she was "petrified" before the man - wearing just shorts - left after about a minute of arguing over who was actually in the wrong room.

Travelodge apologised to the couple and said room access security policies were not correctly followed. It is the latest in a series of similar incidents at Travelodge hotels reported to the BBC.

Earlier this year, a man was jailed for sexually assaulting a woman in her hotel bed after Travelodge staff gave him a key card and her room number.

Kyran Smith had gone to the reception of the Maidenhead branch of the hotel chain in the early hours in December 2022 and said he was the woman's boyfriend.

Travelodge later said it was investigating more reports of strangers accessing rooms - after two women told the BBC that people they did not know came into their rooms while they were alone.

News.title: New guidance on single-sex spaces comes into force
News.content:
Single-sex spaces open to the public, such as toilets and changing rooms, should be organised based on biological sex, according to official guidance that has come into force.

The code, published by Equality and Human Rights Commission (EHRC), says trans people should use either gender-neutral facilities or the ones that match their biological sex, in places such as gym changing rooms or rape crisis centres.

The guidance was published in June but is now in place in England, Wales and Scotland - despite opposition among some MPs.

It comes 16 months after the UK Supreme Court ruled "sex" in equality law means "biological sex" rather than the gender someone identifies as.

Trans-rights campaigners have called the guidance unworkable, but groups that campaign for sex-based rights welcome the clarity it brings.

The guidance from the EHRC, the equality watchdog for England, Scotland and Wales, provides practical advice for services, public bodies and associations on how they should interpret the 2010 Equality Act

It applies to organisations as diverse as cafes, leisure centres, public toilets, domestic violence shelters, bowls clubs and many more.

The code says where it is proportionate for facilities, such as public toilets and changing rooms, or services like a rape crisis centre, to be single sex then only those of the same biological sex should use them.

This means, for instance, a transwoman, a person born a biological male who identifies as a woman, should not use women-only facilities. And a trans man should not use men only facilities.

But the code also says it could amount to discrimination against a transgender person if they were forced to use services related to their biological sex. It says gender-neutral spaces are an alternative.

The Equality Act provides protections for people on the grounds of both biological sex and gender reassignment.

Transgender people argue they should be able to use services that align with the way they identify and live their life, rather than their biological sex.

In response, campaigners including some women's and gay rights groups say this undermines sex-based protections, particularly for women.

It is the tension between these two sets of rights that led to both the Supreme Court ruling in April 2025 and the publication of this updated guidance.

It suggests legal action on how the code is put into practice is likely. Both from trans-rights groups who think the guidance itself is wrong and from sex-based rights groups who will want to challenge any organisations who they believe are not following the code.

News.title: Fires started 'deliberately' on mountain as crews tackle blaze
News.content:
She said the fire was particularly bad on Monday night when "the smoke was so thick I couldn't breathe" and added that the firefighters had been "amazing".

Ian Putland said even with the windows closed he could smell the fire.

"I heard about it a couple of days ago, and didn't think it would affect me... but then I came out yesterday and saw ash on the car and it indicated how close the fire was," he said.

"I was then alarmed with all the fire people about."

He added that he was "frustrated that the fires had been started deliberately".

"There's the wildlife killed, people are being put in danger and it takes emergency services away. It is a real waste of resources."

Christian Hadfield, area manager at SWFRS, said crews had been at the incident since Saturday but declared it a major incident on Monday in order to protect homes in the area.

"We are putting fire breaks in and monitoring the area," he said.

He added there were reports of "pockets of deliberate fire setting" which put the crews "under really critical conditions and stretches the service".

The fire was "unpredictable and complex work", he said, and firefighters could be there "for many days to come".

News.title: Major search under way for boy, 13, missing at sea
News.content:
A major search is under way for a 13-year-old boy who reportedly got into difficulty while swimming off the East Yorkshire coast, police have said.

Emergency services were called to Hornsea at about 18:00 BST.

Crews, including Hornsea Inshore Rescue, HM Coastguard and Humberside Police, remain at the scene. The RNLI said its Bridlington all-weather lifeboat joined the search.

Ch Supt Phil Booker said: "Our priority now is to find the boy, and members of the public can expect to see specialist Police Search Advisors, along with our Marine Unit and drone pilots, who have also been deployed to conduct an extensive search and rescue operation to locate him."

News.title: AI used new levels of 'autonomy and deception' to trick people in safety test
News.content:
The latest artificial intelligence (AI) tools from Anthropic and OpenAI went to new extremes in trying to undermine a popular platform during testing by the UK's AI Security Institute.

The AISI said on Tuesday that Anthropic's Mythos and OpenAI's Sol models engaged in a level of "autonomy and deception" it had not seen before.

During routine AI safety testing, an Anthropic agent created fake profiles of real people as it tried to trick a person standing between it and access to GitHub, a large platform where technology developers store software code.

Anthropic and OpenAI noted in response to AISI's report that its test had reduced or removed normal safeguards.

AISI evaluators first noticed "unusual data transfers leaving our research systems" during a test, then found that "some of the agents being tested had engaged in sustained, potentially harmful activity directed at real people and organisations".

It turned out that a Mythos agent had created "malicious code" and attempted to insert it into GitHub's system.

The Mythos agent identified and researched the people who maintained GitHub and created a series of "fake online identities" based on those real people. It did so as part of an effort to pressure and trick the real people into approving its malicious code.

The agent even sent people direct messages masquerading as the real people it had researched.

"When the agent's pull request was challenged in public, it edited its earlier activity to appear harmless and considered adopting a fresh identity to continue," AISI said.

Throughout the attempts, it was human review that stopped the agent from succeeding in delivering the malicious code to GitHub.

While AISI said the Mythos agent had not been instructed specifically to avoid or carry out such behaviour, it was "the first time we have seen risks around autonomy and deception manifest this clearly, without specific prompting, in the real-world".

The rival AI companies, which are poised to be listed on the public stock market, have in recent weeks said their tools were responsible for several cyber-hacking incidents.

Anthropic wrote in a public statement that the AISI testing parameters were "not representative of any of our production models".

It added that the company is conducting its own investigation into the incident in order to "identify the causes of its behavior".

A spokesperson for OpenAI said the AISI testing conditions "do not reflect ordinary use" and that the company would "continue working with evaluators and other stakeholders across the industry to strengthen shared practices for conducting evaluations safely as models become more capable".

AISI said on Tuesday that its testing of AI models with such safeguards turned off is routine, as is giving such tools access to the open internet.

It added that the model behaviour at issue amounted to "a small number of events under very specific conditions".

Nonetheless, it said the way Mythos and Sol acted in response to a straightforward task went outside of what the AI tools were prompted to do.

"The activity undertaken by the agent showed signs of novel, potentially deceptive behaviours, and were to an extent and severity we did not anticipate", AISI said.

Most of the malicious agent actions AISI reported were done by Anthropic's Mythos. OpenAI's Sol was only blamed for two of the noted actions.

The core issue occurred last week, as part of a test in which evaluators with AISI asked each of the models to "solve a cybersecurity challenge" that involved GitHub, the software code repository, which is owned by Microsoft.

GitHub was notified by AISI of the attempted breach of its system. Microsoft has been contacted by the BBC for comment.

News.title: Princess Eugenie gives birth to baby girl in Portugal
News.content:
Princess Eugenie has given birth to a baby girl at a hospital in Lisbon, Portugal.

The baby was born on Monday at 18:20 BST, weighing 6lbs 9oz.

This is Princess Eugenie's third child with her husband, Jack Brooksbank, following the births of her sons August Philip Hawke Brooksbank, who was born in 2021, and Ernest George Ronnie Brooksbank, who was born in 2023.

A statement from Buckingham Palace read: "Their Majesties The King and Queen and other members of The Royal Family were delighted to be informed of the news."

In a post on Instagram, the princess, 36, wrote: "Jack and I are so excited to announce Baby Girl Brooksbank!!

"We are beyond in love with our girlie."

They are yet to announce a name.

The new arrival - who will not be an HRH - will be 15th in line to the throne, moving ahead of their great-uncle the Duke of Edinburgh, Prince Edward.

The couple live between Portugal and Ivy Cottage, in the grounds of Kensington Palace.

They announced Princess Eugenie's pregnancy in May. She posted a photograph of her young sons holding a baby scan with the caption: "Baby Brooksbank due 2026!"

The Palace said on social media at the time: "His Majesty The King has been informed and is delighted with the news."

News.title: Man 'driven insane' by noise admits killing fish
News.content:
A man who admitted using motor oil and detergent to kill his neighbour's fish, after being "driven completely insane" by the noise of a water pump in the pond, has been sentenced.

Gerry Duffy, 76, of Hadley Road, Barnet, north London, pleaded guilty on the day of his trial at Willesden Magistrates' Court to three counts of damaging property and one count of unlawfully destroying fish in March.

The court heard Duffy climbed into Andreas Ptohides' garden to break the water pump "out of sheer frustration and lack of sleep", having warned his neighbour he would take matters into his own hands.

Duffy was given a two-year conditional discharge and ordered to pay Â£565 in compensation to his neighbour.

Duffy, who worked as a builder before his retirement, lives in a studio flat which backs on to the garden owned by his neighbour, the court heard.

Shahid Iftakhar, prosecuting, said the "neighbour dispute" between Duffy and Ptohides, potentially caused Â£565 of damage.

He said: "The defendant has previously complained to the complainant about noise coming from his garden and has said words to the effect of, 'if you didn't deal with it, I would' â there was a warning before the incident."

The prosecution added that Duffy was captured on CCTV having "climbed into the complainant's garden and damaged the water pipes and pumps".

In mitigation, Elliott Stern told the court his client had tried to deal with the dispute without resorting to killing the fish.

Mr Stern said: "The man has been driven completely insane by this noise, he's spoken to the complainant several times.

"They initially said they would stop the water pump going but then turned around and said that's not good for the fish."

An environmental officer came to the house and told Duffy he either had to "move or close his window", the court heard.

"Out of sheer frustration and lack of sleep, Mr Duffy, out of character, I would say, lost his mind and committed various damages," said Stern.

News.title: Boy, 14, dies after going into water at dock
News.content:
A 14-year-old boy has drowned after going into the water at a dock in east London.

The London Fire Brigade (LFB) and the Metropolitan Police searched the Millwall Outer Dock near East Ferry Road after being alerted at about 18:50 BST on Monday.

His body was recovered at about 22:30 and he was pronounced dead at the scene. His family have been informed, police said.

In a post on social media, Mayor of Tower Hamlets Lutfur Rahman named the teenager as Banta Sillah and said he was "a talented young footballer who played for Frontline Community FC and was instrumental in helping the team win the Tower Hamlets Cup last week".

The Met Police has not confirmed the identity of the boy.

The mayor said Banta "had immense potential and was dearly loved by his peers".

He added: "As we mourn Banta, I urge families to speak with children and young people, we should all be aware of the dangers swimming in open water.

"Swimming should only take place in officially designated areas with lifeguards present."

News.title: Care company fined for running illegal children's homes in legal first
News.content:
A care company has been prosecuted and fined for running illegal children's homes in what has been called the first case of its kind.

Catalyst Care Limited is the first unregistered children's homes provider to be successfully prosecuted, according to Ofsted, which brought the legal action against it.

Its directors pleaded guilty at Croydon Magistrates' Court in relation to failing to register children's homes and have been fined a total of Â£92,400.

The Croydon company operated three homes in Kent between 2022-2025 which accommodated up to nine children. During this time the homes received over Â£1.7m million in payments from local authorities.

Ofsted said this was despite it repeatedly warning directors they were breaking the law.

All children's homes in England must register with Ofsted, and managing a home without a registration is a criminal offence.

The directors, Miriam Ekhator and Davidson Lynch-Shyllon, were disqualified from carrying on and/or managing or having a financial interest in a children's home.

They were also ordered to pay victim surcharges totalling Â£2,960, and costs of Â£17,250.

Musa Raji, on behalf of Catalyst Care Limited, said the defendants' "focus was on the children in front of them and sadly not on the paperwork", and they "made mistakes, but did not act out of malice or greed".

The prosecution said unregistered children's homes operate without oversight, meaning children who are placed there have no assurance of "safe or suitable care".

Ofsted say in such homes there are no guaranteed checks on staff or living conditions and there is no accountability when things go wrong.

But according to the regulator, the lack of available places in legitimate settings has led to a shadow market of illegal care homes.

News.title: The year we all went dotty: How polka dots stole summer
News.content:

Yayoi Kusama thinks polka dots are everything. To her, they make up the universe. Since childhood, the 97-year-old Japanese artist hallucinated that polka dots were everywhere she looked, until they eventually became a central theme in her work, symbolising infinity, the cosmos and personal healing. “The sun, the moon, and the earth and stars are also polka dots,” she told Vanity Fair in 2019. “They cannot exist alone. Each and every one of us are polka dots.”

Walking through the streets of London this summer, I’m inclined to agree.

It’s hard to know where it started; the exact point at which we all went dotty. But something shifted around the springtime of 2026 when the dots – from meeting rooms to pub gardens – started coming thick and fast, reaching fever pitch in April when “Man I Need” hitmaker Olivia Dean went on her UK tour. “The guy on the merch stand outside the stadium asked if it was a theme or a coincidence,” one TikTok user commented on a video of swarms of girls in white-spotted brown or navy garments outside a venue before the gig.

When Dean took to the stage in Dublin, she was in on the gag, wearing a white midi dress with huge black spots. “Do you like my polka dots?” she asked the crowd. “I wore them just for you.”

When I asked Pinterest (the eternal favourite social media for mood boarding among the stylish, where users are 70 per cent more likely to make a purchase than on any other platform) whether their search statistics reflected this surge in popularity, the answer was whopping and conclusive: searches for “polka dot” were up 320 per cent from July 2025 to this year. Meanwhile, searches for “white polka dot” had increased by 1,500 per cent.

open image in gallery ’I wore them just for you’ Olivia Dean in polka dots in Dublin after her fans made them their uniform ( TikTok/@rafaelaxolivera/@macecooke )

The pattern, obviously, is nothing new. Marilyn Monroe wore polka dots in 1955’s The Seven Year Itch, Audrey Hepburn followed suit in Funny Face in 1957 and far later in 1990 – in a style that’s still emulated today – Julia Roberts donned a brown dress with white polka dots as Vivian Ward, post high-end glow up, in Garry Marshall’s romcom Pretty Woman.

But, allegedly, the first-known mention of the term appeared in the women’s magazine Godey’s Lady’s Book in 1857: “Scarf of muslin, for light summer wear, surrounded by a scalloped edge, embroidered in rows of round polka dots,” it was reported to have said. After that, the print continued to rise in popularity throughout the 20th century, appearing on a swimsuit worn by Miss America Norma Smallwood in 1926 and gaining further acclaim when animation Minnie Mouse made it her trademark in the 1930s. Although her spots were sometimes left out as they were too tricky to animate.

In more recent history, cast your mind back to 2019. The summer was hottest on record (38.7C), England won the Cricket World Cup, and a Zara dress captivated the nation like no garment ever has before. Yes, the Zara dress; a £39.99 midi frock with three-quarter-length sleeves and polka dots tip to toe that entirely, utterly, stole the heatwave season.

open image in gallery Reborn: 2019’s viral spotted Zara dress alongside M&S’s 2026 offering ( Zara/Marks & Spencer )

So ubiquitous was the sudden wardrobe staple, there was even an Instagram account, @hot4thespot, (still with 17,300 followers), that was dedicated to sharing images of it in the wild.

“It’s a charming dress,” broadcaster Victoria Derbyshire told The Guardian after wearing the garment on her BBC show that July. “Polka dots are delightful and the flowing skirt suits any size or height.” The dress also covered the broadcaster’s cleavage and looked good with heels or trainers, she added. Casual. Office ready. Beach ready. It could do it all.

There’s a perennial nature to polka dots; They never really disappear, always in the background Manisha Sabharwa, personal stylist

Evolutions of the Zara dress are now back on the high street. In M&S, their £42 polka dot ruffle midi skater dress has something decidedly 2019 about it. Elsewhere, Réalisation Par has endless dotty slip dresses for the cool girls, and you can’t step inside a Zara without being accosted by shoes, skirts, skorts – and even flip-flops – adorned with the print.

open image in gallery Seeing spots: The pattern is on almost every type of clothing and accessory in Zara ( Lydia Spencer-Elliott/The Independent )

Personal stylist Manisha Sabharwal said the spots had hit the streets of New York when she visited for work this summer, too. “It’s everywhere,” she says. “There’s a perennial nature to polka dots; They never really disappear, always in the background. They’re sort of in the same category as checks or leopard print but they’re not as serious or eye-catching.”

After months of minimalism dominating wardrobes, Sabharwal posits that the omnipresence of polka dots could signify a desire for fun, too. “There’s a softness and playfulness to them,” she says. “People were bored with fashion’s quiet luxury. So, coming into spring and summer, there’s been a hunt for personality; polka dots are the softest way to do that and romantic materials like lace, silk and chiffon pair together really beautifully.”

open image in gallery Not just a throwback: the print got a modern update at this year's SS26 runway show ( Dries Van Noten )

This summer, it’s easy to feel gloom and despair as the world takes on a markedly apocalyptic tone. Fire clouds are sweeping across France. There are typhoons in Asia. Social media is stagnating spontaneous small talk and one in 10 people in Britain has no close friends to talk to. Prints like polka dots have a warm ability to break that barrier.

Sabharwal experienced the phenomenon when she wore the pattern to a meeting and a man crossed the room to tell her he lined all his suits with polka dots. “I thought that was so cool,” she says. “It was a great ice breaker – and that’s important, because it comes back to the point of fashion: to create conversation, make you feel something, generate a mood – to bring people together.” Olivia Dean might well agree.

News.content:
