Eating well on a budget is supposed to be a matter of sensible planning: batch-cook your lentils, embrace the slightly tired vegetables at the back of the fridge and never enter a supermarket without a list. In practice, when the day has run away with you and dinner needs to be on the table before everyone loses patience, the cheaper option can often feel like the easier one too.

That tension is familiar to plenty of households. New research commissioned by Lidl found that almost seven in 10 Britons believe healthy eating costs more, while nearly half said they had chosen a less healthy option in the past year because it was cheaper. There is no shortage of advice telling us to eat more vegetables, beans, pulses and wholegrains; the more pressing question is how to turn all that good intention into a dinner people actually want to eat, without spending half the evening cooking it or half the weekly food budget buying it.

Enter Miguel Barclay, the chef behind the bestselling One Pound Meals series, who has teamed up with Lidl to create seven so-called £1 Planet Plate recipes. Inspired by the Planetary Health Diet – a framework developed by scientists to encourage eating patterns that support both human and environmental health – the collection is less interested in demanding a total kitchen overhaul than in making a few useful adjustments to familiar meals.

“I’ve always believed that great food doesn’t have to come with a big price tag,” Barclay says. “The key is making the most of simple, affordable ingredients and knowing how to bring them together in a way that’s delicious and balanced. These £1 Planet Plate recipes show how little changes, such as adding more vegetables and beans, can be easy to create at home, without compromising on flavour or affordability.”

Thankfully, that does not mean seven earnest bowls of undressed lentils. Barclay’s recipes borrow from the kind of food people already cook and order: chicken kra pow served with cauliflower rice, a creamy leek, courgette and bean cassoulet, chickpea masala and a mushroom and spinach stroganoff with mashed potato. A pork ramen comes topped with charred sweetcorn, while a beef hotpot stretches a modest amount of mince with green lentils beneath a layer of golden potato.

There is some clever thrift built in, too. Wholemeal wraps are cut into small tacos for roasted cauliflower, red cabbage and kidney beans, while the trimmings become nachos rather than going in the bin. Across the collection, yoghurt supplies creaminess, beans and pulses add substance and vegetables are treated as part of the pleasure rather than a worthy side order.

These are straightforward, forgiving recipes made from supermarket ingredients, designed for weeknights rather than lifestyle manifestos. Because eating a little better becomes far more achievable when dinner still tastes like dinner.

Chicken kra pow and cauliflower rice

open image in gallery A lighter take on the Thai favourite, with fragrant basil, chilli and cauliflower rice ( Miguel Barclay/Lidl )

Serves: 1

Prep time: 10 minutes | Cook time: 20 minutes

Ingredients:

½ cauliflowers

20ml sesame oil

160g chicken drum fillets, finely chopped

2 garlic cloves, finely diced

1 fresh red chilli, sliced

34g green beans, quartered

14g fresh basil

10ml soy sauce

4 pinches salt

2 pinches black pepper

Method:

1. Blitz the cauliflower in a food processor by pulsing until it resembles rice. Then pan fry over a medium heat in a splash of sesame oil for about 8 minutes until tender and cooked.

2. Meanwhile, chop the chicken into very small pieces, season with salt and pepper, then pan fry with garlic, chilli and green beans in a splash of sesame oil over a medium heat for about 10 minutes until cooked through.

3. Add a small handful of basil, along with a splash of soy sauce for the last 30 seconds of cooking, then serve with the cauliflower rice.

Creamy leek, courgette and bean cassoulet

open image in gallery Cannellini beans turn this creamy vegetable cassoulet into a filling midweek dinner ( Miguel Barclay/Lidl )

Serves: 2

Prep time: 20 minutes | Cook time: 20 minutes

Ingredients:

1 courgette, sliced into 2mm thick circles

10ml olive oil

1 leek, sliced into 3mm thick circles

1 chicken or veg stock cube

400g cannellini beans

4 tbsp 0% Greek yoghurt

4 pinches salt

4 pinches black pepper

Method:

1. Pan fry the courgette circles in a splash of olive oil with a pinch of salt and pepper over a medium heat for about 7 mins until slightly coloured on both sides, then remove from the pan.

2. In the same pan, add the leeks and pan fry in the remaining olive oil along with a another pinch of salt and pepper over a medium heat for about 7 minutes until softened, then add the stock cube and cannellini beans, along with some liquid from the tin. Simmer for 5 minutes (adding a splash of water if it gets too dry), then stir in 2 tablespoons of greek yoghurt and simmer for another 30 seconds.

3. Stir through the cooked courgettes and serve.

Chickpea masala

open image in gallery Chickpeas and aubergine make this quick curry hearty, affordable and full of flavour ( Miguel Barclay/Lidl )

Serves: 2

Prep time: 5 minutes | Cook time: 20 minutes

Ingredients:

100g rice

200g water

2 small onion, sliced

10ml sunflower oil

2 tsp curry paste

200g chickpeas

½ aubergine, diced

400g chopped tomatoes

2 tbsp 0% Greek yoghurt

2 pinches salt

Optional:

10g coriander, chopped

1 red onion, sliced

Method:

1. Add the rice to a saucepan, along with the water and simmer over a medium heat with the lid on for about 10 minutes or until all the water is absorbed and the rice is cooked.

2. Meanwhile, pan fry the onion, chickpeas and diced aubergine in a splash of oil over a medium heat along with the curry paste and a pinch of salt for about 7 minutes. Next, add the tinned chopped tomatoes. Simmer for a few minutes before adding a tablespoon of Greek yoghurt.

3. Top with chopped coriander and sliced red onion (optional)

4. Serve with rice.

Mushroom and spinach stroganoff

open image in gallery Mushrooms, spinach and peas bring plenty of substance to this meat-free stroganoff ( Miguel Barclay/Lidl )

Serves: 2

Prep time: 15 minutes | Cook time: 30 minutes

Ingredients:

4 potatoes, diced

1 onion, sliced

10ml olive oil

2 large flat cap mushroom, sliced

1 tsp smoked paprika

4 tbsp 0% Greek yoghurt

100g fresh spinach, washed

80g frozen British petit pois

4 pinches salt

2 pinches black pepper

Method:

1. Boil the diced potato in lightly salted water for about 15 minutes until cooked through, then drain and mash with a fork.

2. Meanwhile, pan fry the onion over a medium heat for 3 minutes in a splash of olive oil. Then add the garlic and mushroom, along with salt, pepper and paprika. Continue to fry for 5 minutes until cooked, then add the yoghurt, spinach and peas, along with a splash of water. Simmer for a minute or 2 until the peas are cooked, then serve with mashed potato.

Charred sweetcorn and sliced pork ramen

open image in gallery A quick pork ramen made richer with charred sweetcorn, soy and sesame ( Miguel Barclay/Lidl )

Serves: 2

Prep time: 10 minutes | Cook time: 15 minutes

Ingredients:

½ pork shoulder steak

200g Freshona sweetcorn, drained

2 pinches chilli flakes

2 cloves garlic, finely diced

10ml sesame oil

2 spring onions, sliced

1 chicken or veg stock cube

800ml boiling water

2 portions dried noodles

20ml soy sauce

2 pinches salt

2 pinches black pepper

Method:

1. Season and pan fry the pork steak over a medium heat in a splash of sesame oil along with a pinch of salt, pepper and chilli flakes, for about 5 minutes on each side until cooked through and nicely coloured on the outside. Add the sweetcorn into the pan with the pork half way through cooking. Then remove both from the pan and set to one side.

2. In the same pan, using the leftover oil, fry the garlic and spring onion for 2 minutes before adding the stock cube, boiling water and noodles. Simmer for about 4 minutes until the noodles are cooked through.

3. Slice the pork very thinly, then add to the ramen along with the charred sweetcorn and a splash of soy sauce, then serve.

Beef and lentil hotpot

open image in gallery Green lentils help stretch the beef without losing the comfort of a classic hotpot ( Miguel Barclay/Lidl )

Makes: 1 pie

Prep time: 5 minutes | Cook time: 30 minutes

Ingredients:

1 small onion, diced

10ml olive oil

1 clove garlic, sliced

20g grass fed mince beef

200g green lentils, drained

1 carrot, diced

200g tin chopped tomatoes

½ beef or veg stock cube

½ tsp cumin

1 potato, sliced about 5mm thick

2 pinches salt

2 pinches black pepper

Method:

1. Pan fry the diced onion in a splash of olive oil over a medium heat for about 3 minutes before adding the garlic and minced beef. Season, then continue to fry for a further 8 minutes before adding the lentils, diced carrot, chopped tomatoes, ½ a stock cube and the cumin. Simmer for 5 minutes to reduce the sauce a little.

2. Pre-heat the oven to 200C.

3. Transfer everything to an ovenproof dish and top with the potato slices, then brush with olive oil. Sprinkle with salt and pepper, then cook in the oven for 20 minutes or until the potatoes are cooked through and the top is golden.

Cauliflower and red cabbage tacos with offcut nachos

open image in gallery Tortilla trimmings become crunchy nachos in a recipe designed to waste less ( Miguel Barclay/Lidl )

Makes: 6 tacos

Prep time: 20 minutes | Cook time: 30 minutes

Ingredients:

2 wholemeal tortilla wraps, cut into smaller circles

¼ cauliflower, cut into florets

75g red cabbage, thinly sliced

¼ tin kidney beans, drained

5ml olive oil

1 tsp cumin

1 tsp smoked paprika

3 tsp Hellmann’s Chilli Charger Mayo (you can also make this by mixing mayo with tomato ketchup and paprika)

5 g coriander, chopped

1 pinches salt

1 pinches black pepper

Method:

1. Preheat your oven to 200C.

2. Using a circular template (for example a large mug), cut out 3 mini tortillas from each large tortilla and set to one side, then cut the offcuts into triangles to make nachos.

3. Lightly coat the cauliflower, cabbage, kidney beans and tortilla offcuts in olive oil, salt, pepper, cumin and paprika. Then roast everything on a baking tray in the oven, with the nachos on a separate tray, for about 15 minutes, or until cooked and slightly coloured.

4. Warm the mini tortillas for the last 1 minute in the oven.

5. Add the cabbage, cauliflower and beans to the heated mini tortillas, along with a drizzle of Chilli Charger Mayo sauce.

6. Finish with some chopped coriander and serve.

These recipes were created by Miguel Barclay as part of Lidl GB’s £1 Planet Plate collection, designed to make balanced, budget-friendly meals easier to cook at home. Find out more here.

Samantha Morton is opening up about losing her role in Spike Jonze’s 2013 sci-fi romance film, Her.

Morton — who is currently earning rave reviews for her role as the Greek sorceress Circe in Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey — was originally the voice of Samantha, the AI operating system that Joaquin Phoenix’s Theodore Twombly falls in love with.

However, Samantha was recast in post-production, with Johansson taking over the role. The film went on to receive five Oscar nominations, including Best Picture, and won for Best Original Screenplay.

“I have to say that it’s every director’s prerogative in regard to the final cut of the film. For any job, you’re never guaranteed to be in it in the end. But with that, I was surprised. A little sad would be an understatement,” Morton told Josh Horowitz on his Happy Sad Confused podcast recently.

“The time I had on set with Joaquin [Phoenix], working with Spike on the script and finding Samantha, and all the work that we did was really special. We did some mad stuff,” the 49-year-old British actor continued.

open image in gallery Samantha Morton is currently earning rave reviews for her role as Circe in ‘The Odyssey’ ( Getty )

open image in gallery Joaquin Phoenix stars in Spike Jonze’s ‘Her’ as a man who falls in love with an AI operating system, which was initially voiced by Morton before her role was recast and given to Scarlett Johansson ( Warner Bros )

“They designed and built a booth for me to record all my sound. I would be in this black, padded phone box, or I’d be in the trunk of a car. I think my version of Samantha was very different. She’s English,” she explained.

“Scarlett Johansson has a beautiful voice; she’s incredibly evocative. I got it, but I was sad. It does hurt when you’re fired from something. What I would have wished for was another chance in a booth to do an American accent. But Scarlett Johansson — I mean, come on.”

Morton is one of the many stars that make up the stellar cast of The Odyssey, which follows the Greek hero Odysseus (Matt Damon) as he spends more than 10 years trying to get back to Ithaca and his family after the Trojan War. Tom Holland, Robert Pattinson, Lupita Nyong’o, Zendaya and Charlize Theron also star.

Speaking ahead of the film’s July 17 release, Nolan claimed Morton received a reaction on set that he hasn’t seen since he directed the late Heath Ledger in 2008’s The Dark Knight.

open image in gallery Johansson took over as Samantha in ‘Her,’ which went on to be nominated for five Academy Awards, including Best Picture ( AFP/Getty )

“This was a massive film and [Circe] is someone who comes in and changes the dynamic,” Nolan told the Los Angeles Times.

“In some weird way, the film lived or died over that character. She was the fulcrum. I’ve always admired Samantha’s work, she brings so much depth of thinking about her role, there are no limitations on her performance.”

Nolan went on to recall that after one of Morton’s takes, “the crew gave her a round of applause.”

He said he discussed the moment with his wife and producing partner Emma Thomas, and that “she remembered that the last time that had happened was with Heath Ledger on The Dark Knight.”

Lloyd Robertson, who served as chief anchor of CTV National News for 27 years and became one of Canada’s most trusted journalists on the country’s top-rated nightly television newscast, has died. He was 92.

CTV News said Robertson’s family confirmed his death Tuesday.

For generations of Canadians, Robertson chronicled many of the defining events of the late 20th and early 21st centuries, from elections and wars to the Sept. 11 attacks.

Robertson joined CTV in 1976 and became chief anchor and senior editor of CTV National News in 1984. He led the network’s flagship evening broadcast until retiring in 2011, ending each newscast with his trademark sign-off: “That’s the kind of day it’s been.”

Before joining CTV, Robertson spent more than two decades at the Canadian Broadcasting Corp., where he anchored the national newscast from 1970 until leaving for the rival network in 1976. He later said he left because union rules prevented anchors from writing scripts, choosing stories or reporting in the field.

Robertson later said covering the Sept. 11, 2001 attacks and their aftermath was among the most difficult assignments of his career.

“For more than six decades, Lloyd Robertson helped Canadians make sense of the world. For millions of us, he was a familiar face in our living rooms. A reassuring voice in moments of uncertainty. A calm and steady presence through the moments that shaped our nation,” Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said in a post on social media.

Robertson was voted Canada’s most trusted television journalist by TV Guide Canada readers for 11 consecutive years.

“I’m not a talking head,” Robertson once said. “I deal in the news every day. I ask questions. I do reports. I analyze. I edit.”

Born in Stratford, Ontario, Robertson began his broadcasting career at a local radio station in 1952 before joining CBC in 1954.

He was appointed to the Order of Canada and inducted into the Canadian Association of Broadcasters Hall of Fame in 1998. In 2007, he became the first journalist inducted into Canada’s Walk of Fame.

After stepping down as chief anchor in 2011, Robertson remained with CTV as a special correspondent. He later received lifetime achievement awards from the Radio Television Digital News Association and the Canadian Journalism Foundation.

Robertson married his high school sweetheart, Nancy, in 1956. They had four daughters.

News.title: Tupac Shakur was killed in Las Vegas in 1996. Here's who was there that night
News.content:

New details about one of hip-hop's most enduring mysteries — the 1996 killing of rap icon Tupac Shakur — could finally come to light in the upcoming trial of Duane “Keffe D” Davis.

Davis, 63, is accused of orchestrating the drive-by shooting near the Las Vegas Strip that also wounded rap music mogul Marion “Suge” Knight. Davis' jury trial will begin Aug. 10, nearly three years after he was arrested in 2023. He pleaded not guilty.

On the night of Sept. 7, 1996, Shakur was in the passenger seat of a black BMW that Knight was driving when a white Cadillac pulled up on their right side and gunfire erupted. Knight was wounded but survived. Shakur died a week later at the age of 25.

Police and prosecutors say the shooting stemmed from a fierce competition for dominance in a musical genre that pitted East Coast members of a Bloods gang sect against West Coast members of a Crips sect that Davis has said he led in Compton, California.

That night, three others were with Davis in the Cadillac, but none of them faced charges in Shakur’s killing before they died.

Here’s what we know about who was in both vehicles from authorities, court records, grand jury testimony, interviews and Davis’ 2019 tell-all memoir, “Compton Street Legend.”

Tupac Shakur

Shakur is considered one of the most influential rappers of all time. He had five No. 1 albums, was nominated for six Grammy Awards and was inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame in 2017. He received a posthumous star in 2023 on the Hollywood Walk of Fame and he will appear in the upcoming video game " Stranger than Heaven."

His death came as his fourth solo album, “All Eyez on Me,” remained on the charts, with some 5 million copies sold. He also used the stage names 2Pac and Makaveli. As an actor, he starred in several films.

Shakur was born Lesane Parish Crooks in New York in 1971, and his name was changed a year later. His late mother Afeni Shakur, and late stepfather Mutulu Shakur, were active in the Black Panther Party in New York. Tupac Shakur was not close with his biological father, William “Billy” Garland.

Two of the rapper’s siblings, Sekyiwa “Set” Shakur and Maurice “Mopreme” Shakur, have criticized authorities for inaction and slowness in charging anyone with their brother’s death.

Marion “Suge” Knight

Knight founded Death Row Records, a Los Angeles-based music label that represented Shakur at the time of his death. Knight’s moniker was shortened from “Sugar Bear,” his nickname growing up in Compton.

Knight and Shakur were headed to a nightclub when their car was shot at near the Las Vegas Strip. Knight was grazed by a bullet or shrapnel.

Now 61, Knight is serving a 28-year prison sentence in California for running over and killing a Compton businessman outside a burger stand in January 2015. The case capped the former rap music mogul’s downfall from his heyday as one of the biggest — and most feared — names in the music industry.

Davis said he and Knight knew each other growing up and even played on the same youth football team in Compton. Knight went on to play college football at the University of Nevada, Las Vegas. Briefly, during the 1987 NFL players’ strike, he was a replacement player for the Los Angeles Rams.

In his memoir, Davis describes Knight and himself as the “only living eyewitnesses to what truly happened.”

“Like two rams locking horns, Suge and I looked each other dead in the eye," he writes when describing the moments right before the shooting.

Orlando “Baby Lane” Anderson

Law enforcement authorities long suspected that Anderson was the gunman. He was 22 at the time. Though Davis was his uncle and 12 years older, he described their relationship as that of brothers, friends and even father-son.

Shortly before the drive-by shooting, Anderson was beaten in a brawl at the MGM Grand casino involving Shakur and his associates, including Knight. Authorities, authors and Davis himself say the shooting was an act of retaliation for beating up Anderson.

“Them jumping on my nephew gave us the ultimate green light to do something,” Davis writes in the book.

Davis said he obtained a handgun from an associate and tossed it into the back seat of the Cadillac but did not say who fired the fatal shots. Anderson was sitting in the backseat of the car, behind his uncle.

Neither the Cadillac nor the gun used in the shooting were recovered, according to retired Las Vegas police Detective Clifford Mogg, who was assigned to the investigation in early 2018.

“We were never able to identify the person who rented the car, where it was rented from, and then when it comes to the gun, we have never recovered as of this date, the weapon that was used in the murder,” Mogg said in testimony to the grand jury.

Anderson, who denied involvement in Shakur’s killing, died two years later in what police said was an unrelated shooting at a Compton car wash.

Deandrae “Freaky” Smith

Also known as “Big Dre,” Smith was in the back seat of the car that night, sitting next to Anderson.

Although authorities have said they believe Anderson pulled the trigger, the grand jury testimony challenged that theory.

Denvonta Lee, a former associate of Davis, told the grand jury that it was Smith who shot Shakur and Knight. He said Anderson tried reaching over Smith but didn’t have a “clear shot” out the left-rear passenger window.

The former associate, who wasn’t in the car but recounted a conversation he had with Smith days after the shooting, said Smith took the gun from Anderson, opened fire and let Anderson take credit for Shakur’s death.

Smith was 30 when he died in 2004 of natural causes, according to the Los Angeles County coroner’s office.

Terry “Bubble Up” Brown

Brown was driving the Cadillac from which the shots were fired.

Davis said in his memoir that they were driving toward Las Vegas Boulevard that night but spotted Shakur “hanging out of the window” of the BMW and waving to fans. Davis told Brown to make a U-turn, and they drove slowly past the rapper’s convoy until Davis said they “found who we were seeking.”

Brown died in a 2015 shooting at a medical marijuana dispensary in Compton.

The Los Angeles County coroner’s office said his full name was Terry Tyrone Brown, although Brown has been referred to as both “Terrence” and “Terrance” in investigative records.

___

Associated Press writer Jessica Hill and former Associated Press writer Ken Ritter in Las Vegas contributed.

Inside Neil Armstrong's boyhood home, at the top of a creaky stairway, sits his bedroom where he launched model airplanes out of the rear window to measure how far they'd fly.

Hanging in the room now are autographed photos of astronauts who've visited the privately kept house to see where Armstrong’s first steps to the moon began.

Owned by a retired history teacher devoted to preserving its past and charming character, the home is for sale for the first time in nearly 40 years. What will become of it remains uncertain.

All over Armstrong's hometown of Wapakoneta, there are reminders of his history-making moonwalk. But few places played a bigger role early in his journey than 601 W. Benton St. — the house where the Armstrong family settled in western Ohio when he was a young teenager.

It's where Armstrong built planes out of balsa wood and glue in the dining room and constructed a basement wind tunnel to test his models. He'd often pedal his bike from home to take flying lessons at an airstrip.

At age 16, Armstrong made his first solo flight and got his pilot's license. Just 20 years later, he rocketed into space for the first time. After the 1969 moon landing, he taught at the University of Cincinnati.

A parade of astronauts has visited Armstrong’s house

Today, Armstrong's two-story boyhood home is an occasional stop for visitors of the Armstrong Air and Space Museum in Wapakoneta, even though the house itself isn't open for tours.

When Karen Mikesell bought the place in 1988, she had no idea who once lived there until another teacher soon told her.

As a history teacher who later became a school principal, Mikesell felt a responsibility to "keep it like the Armstrongs had it,” she said.

She's hosted nine astronauts, including Buzz Aldrin, who flew to the moon with Armstrong and Michael Collins in 1969.

Aldrin stepped inside the bedroom upstairs a few years after Armstrong died in 2012, Mikesell recalled, "and the tears just streamed down his cheeks.”

Over the years, she's been given a moon rock and received a piece of gold foil that covered the Apollo 11 capsule — a gift from one of the Navy frogmen who helped recover the command module and its crew.

Some astronauts autographed their photos with personal messages to Mikesell — “thanks for taking such great care of Neil's home!” wrote Mike Foreman, who flew on two space shuttle missions.

“You can read books, but you can never have those kinds of experiences that I was able to have because I lived here,” she said. “I could go on and on.”

House holds many reminders of the first man on the moon

Armstrong's family bought the home in 1944 after his father had moved them about a dozen times with his job as a government auditor. The oldest of three children, Neil was born in a farmhouse just outside Wapakoneta, today a city of just under 10,000 people.

The house on Benton Street with its big front porch has changed little on the outside. Inside, the layout is similar too, though it has been updated.

In the backyard, a garage that Armstrong and his father built with scrap lumber still stands, though a chicken coop where he and his friends gathered for Boy Scout meetings is long gone.

Armstrong's old bedroom is now decorated with photos and paintings of the moon landing. Hanging from the ceiling is a model of the Wright brothers’ first production airplane — the aviation pioneers were from nearby Dayton and an inspiration for Armstrong.

She never met Armstrong, who was famously private. She did talk with his parents, siblings and children about the 1908 home and its place in Armstrong’s upbringing.

A part of American history is for sale

Mikesell, who's 82, said she hopes someone might be willing to buy the house and donate it to the Armstrong museum, which doesn't have the funds to acquire the property, according to Logan Rex, its spokesperson.

She is just one of a handful of people who’ve owned the home since the Armstrongs sold it in the mid-1960s. By the time she bought the house, the rooms were covered with wallpaper in a rainbow of colors, so she sought to restore its original look.

While the house, which is listed at $430,000, isn't legally protected from alteration, Mikesell is also optimistic that the new owners will respect it — whether it remains a private residence or becomes a place for overnight stays.

“It’s time to let someone else have the opportunity to be as blessed as I’ve been," she said, "and to take care of it and keep it as a part of history.”

The man who prosecutors say orchestrated the 1996 killing of rap icon Tupac Shakur is scheduled to go to trial Monday, almost 30 years after the fatal drive-by shooting in Las Vegas.

Duane “Keffe D” Davis, 63, faces a single count of murder with a deadly weapon with the intent to promote, further or assist a criminal gang in Shakur's death. He's been jailed since late 2023 and has pleaded not guilty.

For decades, Shakur's unsolved killing has gripped hip-hop fans. He's considered one of the most influential rappers of all time with songs that speak to the human experience of love, heartache and familial relationships. When Shakur died, he was in the midst of a fierce battle for dominance in a music scene increasingly shaped by rival gangs.

The trial, which is expected to last about a month, likely won't reveal who pulled the trigger. Instead, prosecutors hope to prove that Davis was the shot caller and provided the weapon. Gunfire came from the Cadillac that Davis was in, and he's one of the only people there that night who is still alive. Prosecutors say if Davis hadn't written explicitly about the killing, or talked about it in interviews, it's likely no one would have been charged.

Cold case is revived on Tupac Shakur's killing

On Sept. 7, 1996, Shakur was in the passenger seat of a black BMW and Death Row Records co-founder Marion “Suge” Knight was driving. They had just watched Mike Tyson knock out Bruce Seldon and were headed to a nightclub where Shakur was scheduled to perform. But at a red light near the Las Vegas Strip, a white Cadillac pulled up beside them, and gunfire erupted.

Shakur was shot multiple times and died six days later, while Knight survived with minor injuries. Knight is serving a 28-year prison sentence for a fatal hit-and-run.

The case went cold until Davis began making public statements about his involvement as a leader of the South Side Compton Crips. In 2019, he published a tell-all memoir. The book, along with interviews Davis gave, revived the police investigation.

Davis' defense attorneys argue there is no evidence he directed the shooting and the state relies on witnesses who weren't there. The defense said Davis left the narcotics trade in 2009 and worked a steady job before illness forced him to retire in 2014.

For Shakur's family, the last 30 years have been exhausting and stressful, his stepbrother Maurice “Mopreme” Shakur said. Sitting through the trial will be retraumatizing, Shakur said, but he's “cautiously optimistic” justice will come.

“I hope that the trial is fair, and we find out the truth,” he said.

Shakur's death a result of longstanding gang feud, witnesses say

Hundreds of pages of grand jury transcripts portray Tupac Shakur's shooting as a culmination of a longstanding feud between rival record labels — Death Row Records and Bad Boy Records — and rival gang sects Mob Piru and South Side Compton Crips.

Witnesses said South Side Compton Crips hung out with and provided protection to Bad Boy Records, which was founded by Sean “Diddy” Combs and included rappers like The Notorious B.I.G., or Christopher Wallace. Mob Piru, part of the larger Bloods gang, was associated with Death Row Records, which featured rappers like Shakur, Snoop Dogg and Dr. Dre.

The rival gangs fought and retaliated against each other both before and after Shakur's death.

Prosecutors allege Davis orchestrated the shooting to get revenge after Shakur and his entourage beat up Davis' nephew, Orlando “Baby Lane” Anderson, at the MGM Grand hours before Shakur was killed.

Davis' book will be front and center at the trial

The prosecutors' case relies on “Compton Street Legend,” the book Davis co-authored about the shooting and his time in the Crips, as well as police and media interviews he participated in.

Davis' attorneys unsuccessfully fought to block the use of the book and a recording of a 2008 police interview in the trial. They argued the book was fictionalized and had a co-author, making it impossible to know which parts Davis wrote. They also argued Davis' interview with a federal task force investigating the deaths of Wallace and Shakur was supposed to be confidential and not used against him.

The memoir says that Shakur and his entourage “crossed the line” when they beat up Anderson.

“We couldn’t let no record company studio gangsters do us like that,” the book says.

Davis was in the passenger seat of the Cadillac and passed a gun to the back seat earlier that night, according to the book. When they encountered Shakur and Knight, Davis claimed to see Shakur reach for a weapon and wrote that “one of my guys from the back seat grabbed the Glock and started bustin’ back.”

No weapon was found in Knight and Shakur’s car, according to retired Las Vegas police Detective Clifford Mogg, who was assigned to the investigation in early 2018.

The trial could bring closure — or more questions

Mopreme Shakur said nothing would bring back his stepbrother.

“That would be justice for me,” he said. “But we all know that is unattainable.”

Mopreme Shakur said he wants allegations that Combs was involved to be explored further. In his book, Davis claims that Combs wanted Knight and Shakur killed. Combs has denied having any involvement in Shakur's death.

He's serving roughly four years in prison after being convicted of prostitution-related charges. Combs' attorney did not return emailed requests from The Associated Press for comment.

Shakur's influence in the music industry endures

Shakur sold over 75 million records worldwide with hits like “California Love,” “Changes” and “Dear Mama.” His songs spanned from party anthems to deep social commentary. The issues he discussed still resonate with people 30 years later, history professor Jeffrey O.G. Ogbar said.

“I can’t think of anyone else in the history of hip-hop who’s had a greater impact in such a short period of time,” said Ogbar, who is the founding director of the Center for the Study of Popular Music at the University of Connecticut.

News.title: The underground lab where ‘princess mosquitoes’ are treated like royalty
News.content:
Beneath the grand Art Deco headquarters of the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine lies a vast labyrinth inhabited by weird and wonderful creatures.

In this maze of subterranean labs, store rooms and corridors live colonies of disease-bearing insects and arachnids from all over the world, from bed bugs, sand flies and microscopic dust mites to the so-called kissing bugs that spread Chagas disease – a sinister condition that can cause its victims to drop dead of heart failure without warning, albeit decades after the first (silent) infection.

Behind a series of doors, contained in stacks of mesh boxes, you can even find the flies that spread trachoma, the Dickensian eye disease that is still a leading cause of blindness around the world. But be warned: entering the room is not for the faint of heart – the flies feed on human excrement and the smell is impossible to forget.

There are also many varieties of mosquito, including several species of the Anopheles genus that spread malaria, Culex and Aedes mosquitoes that are also vectors for human and animal diseases, and even Toxorhynchites, perhaps better known as the elephant mosquito, a friendly giant which doesn’t bite people but preys on other mosquitoes.

These animals have been studied intensely since the insectaries were established in the building’s vaults in the 1960s, underpinning many breakthroughs in the control, surveillance, and understanding of vector-borne diseases in the developing world.

LSHTM researchers are now looking closer to home. They have established the UK’s first laboratory colony of Aedes vexans mosquitoes, a species native to the British isles, to study whether they could harbour diseases like West Nile virus, Rift Valley fever, Zika or Japanese encephalitis.

News.title: What I saw in a week on the front line of Afghanistan’s hunger crisis
News.content:
May 15 and 16, 2026

It is the weekend, a small moment to rest, although there is still a lot of work waiting for me. A week in the field does not mean that work in Kabul stops. I try to catch up on my emails and have a planned online interview for an international staff position – since in Europe, Friday is a normal working day. I also review parts of new proposals for donors and our financial planning.

On Saturday, however, I take a short break. Together with the base management team in Helmand, we visit a historical site called Qala-e-Bost, believed to have been built around 3,000 years ago. It is a rare moment to step away from work, followed by lunch with the team.

May 17, 2026

Sunday morning, the first working day of the week, we visit Basrhan Sub Health Centre, run by one of our local partners. As a nurse and former nurse trainer, I feel very much in my element in these health centres. It allows me to engage easily with the team and discuss their work.

I speak with the outreach officer and the vaccinator. They explain that this facility supports 18 outreach locations, each visited at least once a month. They provide vaccinations, raise awareness, and connect communities to the health centre. These visits often take place in simple settings, like mosques.

Immunisation is now well accepted. In the beginning, there was some resistance, but trust has grown over time. Every child is tracked, and if a child misses a vaccination, community health volunteers follow up at home. For extra polio vaccinations, this is carefully recorded by marking a finger of the child – helping ensure that no child is missed. The goal is clear: a polio-free Afghanistan.

I also speak with a mother. She is wearing a burka, so I cannot see her face. She tells me she is 22 years old and holds her 12-month-old son on her lap. She came because he has a fever, but I see a healthy child – something that stands out after my time in the TFU.

She brings her child regularly for follow-up and growth monitoring and the child has never been in a treatment program for malnutrition. She speaks positively about the services. “We are lucky,” she says. “The staff treat us well, and we have access to care in our community.”

News.title: World’s first seahorse hospital fights to protect them from extinction
News.content:
With careful precision, marine biologist Linda Albonetti extracts a 10cm-long injured seahorse – a heavily pregnant male – from an aquarium tank to apply healing ointment to its wound.

Linda, 29, coordinator at the world’s first specialist seahorse hospital, is currently caring for around 50 of these tiny creatures, all of which were brought in by local fishing crews after becoming snagged in their nets.

The seahorse will be kept for a few more days before it is released back into the Adriatic Sea, giving it time to recover from the cut to the soft, bony plates that form its outer carapace.

What the team here are doing is a literal drop in the ocean, a small attempt to fight back against the potential extinction of these remarkable fish.

In Europe and around countries like Indonesia, they are being poached in their millions for sale to a voracious Asian traditional medicine market where they are consumed as an aphrodisiac and alleged cure for impotence, asthma and kidney problems.

“There is definitely a downward trend in the overall seahorse population because they are being collected for the Asian market,” says Linda. “Technically, they cannot be exported to countries such as China, but there is no specific law preventing that trade. They do not have the same protections as sea turtles, for example.

“It is not happening in this part of Italy yet, but it is further south, off the Mediterranean coast. That is why it is so important that we monitor their numbers and maintain a good relationship with the local fishermen.”

News.title: The 13 best castle hotels in England
News.content:
Few places capture the imagination quite like a castle, and England is home to some of the most remarkable places to spend the night. If it’s not the romance of waking up in a canopied four-poster bed, or losing ourselves in centuries-old tapestries and visceral oil paintings, we are lured by tales of brave knights and plotting dignitaries, duplicitous royals and ghosts parleying secrets in the hallways.

Part of the magic is spending an afternoon wandering grounds and gardens followed by evenings in front of a roaring fire, or dining in a banquet hall that may have hosted medieval kings and queens. While not every castle has crenellated battlements, glistening moats or royal connections, each stony stronghold on our list has something special that makes it worth travelling for. In this modern age that might include a spa, fine-dining restaurant or extra touches like free admission to exhibitions and museum tours. Here’s our pick of the best castle hotels in England.

News.title: Careless Liverpool concede same goal twice in second-half capitulation against Leeds
News.content:
Soldier Field in Chicago hosts an all-Premier League tie encounter as Liverpool take on Leeds as both sides bring their US tours to a close. Both Premier League encounters between these sides last season ended in draws; a 3-3 draw at Elland Road was followed up by a 0-0 stalemate at Anfield. The draw at Elland Road was immediately followed by Mohamed Salah speaking to the media, claiming he had been thrown under the bus.

It is a new era at Liverpool as former Bournemouth boss Andoni Iraola has replaced Arne Slot at Anfield. They kicked off the Iraola era in Nashville, Tennessee, with a 4-2 win over Sunderland, following that up with another victory in New York on Wednesday night, beating Wrexham 1-0, and will be aiming to make it three wins from three on their US tour.

“I think it [the US tour] has been really, really useful,” Iraola said in an interview on the official Liverpool website. Obviously, you spend a lot of time with the players, with the staff, you get all the information you can. And I think there is also an evolution, it has to be. We start to understand each other better, what we need to do. Every game, I hope we can get closer and closer and put ourselves in a position where the few players that still are not here start to train also, they are helped by the others.”

Virgil van Dijk and Cody Gakpo resumed training back on Merseyside whilst Alexis Mac Allister, Alisson and Victor Munoz are yet to return to training following their World Cup exploits. The trio of Florian Wirtz, Alexander Isak and Ryan Gravenberch are all set to feature for the first time this pre-season.

Leeds’ pre-season campaign began with a 3-2 loss to Championship Wrexham in Tampa, Florida before beating Sunderland 1-0 in New Jersey courtesy of a long-range strike from Lukas Nmecha. Former Liverpool man Harry Wilson joined Leeds on a free from Fulham this summer.

“Really tough but that is expected,” Wilson said. That is what pre-season is for, building up a base for when the season starts, making sure you are in the best physical position you can be to attack the season. It has been good. I played against them [Leeds] twice last year when I was at Fulham. Both games were really, really tough games.

“I think when the fans have got a good team to support, I think that [the atmosphere at Elland Road] goes up a notch. I think the size of the club was a massive part of me coming. Then speaking to the guys, the chairman, the sporting director, and seeing kind of the plans and the aims for the club, it is something I wanted to be a part of.”

Team news to follow shortly.

News.title: Oil plummets as Trump calls off Iran strikes
News.content:
Oil prices have plunged after Donald Trump called off strikes and said the US and Iran would hold further peace talks.

Brent crude, the international benchmark, sank as much as 9.5pc early on Monday to less than $82 a barrel after the US president said he had halted plans for “disastrous” strikes.

Mr Trump said: “Obviously, they don’t want to be attacked. They knew the extent of the attack because they saw it forming.

“Now what we’re doing is we’re talking to them in the form of a negotiation. It begins tomorrow afternoon.”

Mr ‌Trump also ordered oil companies to lower petrol prices for American ‌consumers ‌and criticised ⁠Chevron’s chief executive for not crediting his administration for supporting the fossil fuel industry.

The president said that he had been asked by Iran as well as US partners Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates and Qatar to hold off on strikes. He halted plans for a major attack against Iran on Saturday, which he said would have been the biggest since the Second World War.

Mr Trump claimed the sides were on the “perimeter” of a peace deal.

Oil’s sharp fall also sent the cost of government borrowing lower on Monday over hopes that it would ease inflation.

The yield on 10-year UK gilts, a benchmark for what the Treasury pays to borrow money, dropped from 5.05pc to 4.98pc, while the equivalent US bonds dropped from 4.74pc to 4.69pc.

Stock markets in Europe also rose, with the FTSE 100 up 0.2pc, the Cac 40 in Paris up 0.3pc and the Dax in Frankfurt climbing 0.1pc.

News.title: Inside the trial for a vaccine to end malaria
News.content:
A small group of brave volunteers were given an experimental vaccine in Oxford this week in a bid to bring to an end the centuries-old scourge of malaria.

“I’m on my second vaccine now. Then I’m due to have my third vaccine soon, and then in November, I’ll be given malaria,” said an upbeat Mike Luciw, a 32-year-old local who works in recruitment.

“The hope is to help find something that could save millions of people.”

There are already two licenced vaccines for malaria but the new Oxford “RH5” shot is not like anything that has come before.

The existing jabs only act against malaria as it moves towards the liver in the early stage of infection, and provide only partial protection.

The new combination vaccine, in contrast, is designed to fight it off both at the liver stage and in the wider bloodstream, effectively knocking it out altogether.

The project is being run by the husband and wife team of Simon Draper, Professor of Vaccinology and Translational Medicine at the University of Oxford, and Professor Angela Minassian, an infectious disease specialist and clinical lead for their malaria programme in Oxford’s Department of Paediatrics.

“The dream for malaria … has been to have these two lines of defence, liver and blood, so if the first line fails, you’ve got a second,” says Prof Draper, who leads on the science.

“Our dream is to have a vaccine that gives over 90 per cent efficacy in African children,” adds Prof Minassian, who heads the clinical trials for the new jab.

News.title: Dowman weaves his magic and new signing shines as Arsenal hit ground running
News.content:
Hello and welcome to our live coverage for this pre-season friendly between Girona and Arsenal at Estadi Montilivi in Catalonia.

With the transfer speculation surrounding Vinícius Júnior’s and Bruno Guimaraes’ potential moves to Arsenal ramping up, the reigning Premier League champions are in action against Girona as they step up their preparations ahead of the upcoming campaign.

Unlike other Premier League heavyweights, Arsenal have kept their pre-season tour relatively local with a selection of games in Spain, Ireland and England, before they face Manchester City in the FA Community Shield on August 16 at the Millennium Stadium in Cardiff.

Arsenal beat League One side MK Dons 3-0 in a behind-closed-doors friendly on July 25 at the Sobha Realty Training Centre, thanks to goals from Reiss Nelson, Ethan Nwaneri and Ceadach O’Neill.

After featuring in this victory and setting up Nelson for the opener, Christos Tzolis will be looking to continue his positive momentum with his new club, after joining Arsenal for £34m earlier this summer. Sports.title: Beleaguered Fifa boss Infantino holed up in desperate crisis talks to cling to power as Wenger joins blackmail rebellion

GIANNI INFANTINO has called an emergency crisis Fifa meeting in a desperate attempt to cling on to his power.

And now Arsene Wenger has joined the growing group distancing themselves from the Swiss chief.



Infantino, 56, sparked chaos around world football last week when news broke of his shock plans to sell off stakes in the World Cup.

That sparked a furious backlash from swathes of football – including Uefa and other continental confederations, who threatened to boycot the World Cup and even plotted to launch a rival tournament to “paralyse Fifa”.



Under overwhelming and mounting pressure, Infantino was forced to make an embarrassing U-turn and ditch his money-grabbing scheme – and now faces a fight to keep hold of his Fifa presidency.

Now he is taking extreme measures to try and retain any support he can.

According to The Times, Infantino is currently holed up in Rabat and has called senior Fifa staff to the Moroccan capital for the urgent gathering.

There was also said to be a meeting of senior Fifa staff on Tuesday without Infantino present, where all but one opposed the controversial World Cup financial plot.

Even so, the chief’s remaining loyal right-hand men are shamelessly appealing to many of the 211 member associations to publicly back the president, who faces an election in March if he survives that long.

But few have done so – including, crucially, Saudi Arabia, hosts of the 2034 World Cup.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Jordan FA president Prince Ali bin Al Hussein launched a damning attack on the Swiss and his organisation, making accusations of “blackmail”.

It is even claimed Fifa withheld funds owed to the Jordan FA – and that the Asian national team federation would benefit from backing Infantino.

Prince Ali bin Al Hussein, 50, wrote on X: “There is no shortage of issues regarding Fifa.

“We have been waiting for reward money for our players since December for the Arab Cup in Qatar, which is a Fifa event.



“The money our team should receive for having reached the final has not been delivered yet, while at the same time Fifa brags about how many billions they have in reserve.

“It is clear the problem really is with leadership.

“For months, Fifa has been refusing to help us on any of these or other matters – until it was verbally communicated to me during the World Cup that if I endorsed Infantino it would go a long way to helping our FA out.

“We pride ourselves in Jordan in upholding ethical values.

“We did not endorse him before and certainly will not now.



“But the whole situation amounts to blackmail and we refuse to give in to that.”

Within the top brass at Fifa, both Arsene Wenger and Secretary General Mattias Grafstrom have slammed Infantino’s disgraceful plans.

Wenger admitted it was “absolutely necessary” to scrap the scheme – which included setting up a company called Fifa Forward Enterprises (FFE) with a stake held by Donald Trump’s son-in-law’s brother Joshua Kusher – and that he had no idea about it until it became public knowledge.



Fifa’s head of global football development does not intent to quit and said: “The recent events at Fifa deserve some clarity from my side.

“I was not involved in this strategic plan and first became aware of the project through media reports.

“The decision to withdraw the project was absolutely necessary and beyond question, because I firmly believe in an independent Fifa that serves our game with commitment, transparency and integrity.”

Grafstrom, meanwhile, sent an email to Fifa staff in an attempt to boost morale after “a sad and reproachable series of events”.

Grafstrom said: “We have all been thrown into the middle of a turmoil, which is difficult to comprehend and accept, but, as Secretary General, I urge you to remain focused on what has always united us: serving football and serving our 211 member associations.



“A sad and reproachable series of events — which were thankfully concluded with the FFE project permanently abandoned — for as much as we feel dismayed by them, should not overshadow this reality.

“I assure you that you as members of the administration, you will be defended and safeguarded from the political context we currently experience.

“You do not need to worry.

“Individuals, unstable moments and unfortunate episodes come and go.

“The institution, its mission and its responsibility towards world football continue, and that is why we should always keep our professionalism, sense of perspective and composure.”

Sports.title: Ex-Newcastle chief Amanda Staveley ‘in offer to buy David Sullivan’s 38.8% West Ham stake to own MAJORITY 63.9% of club’
Sports.content:
AMANDA STAVELEY reportedly offered to buy David Sullivan’s West Ham stake – and become the majority shareholder.

The former Newcastle co-owner’s firm PCP has the backing of US and Far East-based investors.



And after being the face of the Saudi takeover at St James’ Park, she is keen to spearhead a bid to take control of West Ham following their relegation to the Championship.

As reported by The Football Boardroom, Staveley approached Sullivan to buy out his 38.8 per cent stake in the Hammers for around £228million.



She also approached the Gold family over purchasing their 25.1 per cent at a price of £150m.

Together, that would total 63.9 per cent of the club for £378m.

Should PCP’s bid prove successful, they would become the majority owners of West Ham.

However, Daniel Kretinsky owns 27 per cent through 1890 Holdings and the WHU LLC holds the remaining eight per cent, led by J Albert Smith.

Staveley’s offers would value the entire 100 per cent stake of West Ham at just shy of £600m.

Sullivan could be forced to sell his portion of West Ham with the independent football regulator investigating his position following allegations of sexually exploitative and predatory behaviour.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Sullivan, 77, denies all allegations and resigned from his position as Joint Chair of the club to fight them.

His former co-owner and business partner David Gold died in January 2023, with his family retaining his 25.1 per cent stake in West Ham.

Daughter Vanessa took control of the Gold stake and revealed in a statement just days ago that she intends to sell them to Staveley’s consortium.

Gold said: “I have now reached an agreement to sell my family’s shareholding to a consortium of PCP Capital Partners, led by Amanda Staveley and Mehrdad Ghodoussi, in partnership with Ashland Forest Capital Partners.



“While the process has not yet concluded, I wanted to be open with our fans about where things stand and my intentions.”

However, Staveley – who was part of the Newcastle takeover in 2021 and remained a shareholder until 2024 – could have seen her hopes dashed.

That is because Kretinsky moved to try and block her buying the Gold shares.

The Czech businessman – who owns Royal Mail – was primed to take control of the club when Sullivan resigned in June.

Kretinsky is a minority owner as it stands – he is also majority owner and president of Sparta Prague.



However, he agreed to buy 16 per cent of West Ham from the Golds to take his stake to 43 per cent – with existing shareholders getting pre-emption rights offered before being opened up externally.

But with Staveley exploring the option of buying out both Gold and Sullivan, that would take her ownership to a majority.

In response, Kretinsky is selling two per cent of the club to fellow Czech Jakub Havrlant.

That means he could then buy the Golds’ 25.1 per cent and stay at the 50 per cent mark – enough to ensure Staveley cannot supercede his ownership without becoming the majority shareholder.

Should he exceed 50 per cent, that may trigger a clause forcing Kretinsky to buy Sullivan’s stake at an inflated price.



Staveley, meanwhile, has made no secret of her ambition to get back into football – and hinted at going for West Ham as well as the land around the London Stadium.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

She told Bloomberg: “Whatever club we take, there will be a big property play as well. We won’t just do a football-led.”

The news came just hours after it was reported that Staveley has failed to settle a £750,000 debt with her former club Newcastle.

Christian Norgaard completed a medical at Everton on Tuesday ahead of his permanent move away from Arsenal. The Danish midfielder was signed only a year ago from Brentford in a surprise deal worth an initial £10m plus £2m in add-ons.

Norgaard did not play as much as he would have liked last season, making just seven Premier League appearances - none of which were as a starter. Yet, the 32-year-old veteran was highly respected around the club for his leadership and role within the dressing room

‌



And he will leave north London as a Premier League champion ahead of his £7m transfer to Everton. Norgaard had been in Girona with the Arsenal squad last weekend for the 4-1 victory over the Spanish side but did not participate in the match as negotiations with Everton advanced. He was then given approval by the Gunners to complete all formalities ahead of signing a multi-year deal with the Toffees.

Bruno Guimaraes shows true colours

Bruno Guimaraes shared an image of himself joining Newcastle’s pre-season training camp on Monday amid reports of his impending move to Arsenal, before getting back to work on Tuesday. The Magpies captain has been at the centre of a long summer transfer saga, with the Gunners keen to land the midfielder.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

‌



Guimaraes is understood to have agreed personal terms with Arsenal, having told Newcastle of his desire to leave, but will not force through a move if an agreement isn’t reached between the two clubs. He showed that, and with it his professionalism as captain, by joining up with the rest of the Newcastle squad.

The 28-year-old Brazilian was initially meant to return from his extended post-World Cup break on Sunday but the club were happy for him to arrive 24 hours later. He did exactly that and posted an image of him in La Manga, where they are training in Spain, showing he is still a Newcastle player.

It was reported earlier this week that the Magpies rejected an opening official bid from Arsenal worth £75m. And the champions of England are expected to wrap up the deal shortly, following the latest reports surrounding the deal.

Sports.title: Two Champions League rule changes announced by UEFA ahead of new season
Sports.content:
Two Champions League rule changes announced by UEFA ahead of new season

UEFA has updated its regulations and made changes which will affect the nine English clubs playing in either the Champions League, Europa League or Conference League in the 2026-27 season

View 2 Images Qualifying for the 2026-27 Champions League has begun (Image: Kristian Skeie - UEFA/UEFA via Getty Images)

UEFA have announced two rule changes ahead of this season's Champions League. Qualifying for the competition has already started, with the draw for the league phase not until late August.

‌



The same goes for UEFA's other primary competitions, the Conference League and Europa League. And the regulations for each competition have been updated, with two changes announced on Tuesday.

‌



Firstly, the yellow card threshold has been raised. A player will now need four yellow cards rather than three to pick up the first one-match ban.

‌



And secondly, UEFA have removed its long-standing regulation that prevented stadium clocks moving beyond 45 and 90 minutes. This change has been seen in the Premier League for the last two years.

The draw for the Champions League play-off round was made on Monday. Celtic are the only British club involved in the round and will face LASK of Austria in their bid to reach the league phase.

‌



Five English teams will play in the 2026-27 Champions League. Arsenal, Manchester City, Manchester United, Aston Villa and Liverpool qualified through their league position.

In the Europa League, Bournemouth, Crystal Palace and Sunderland will feature. And in the Conference League, which Palace won last season, Brighton are the Premier League's sole representatives.

What do you make of the rule changes? Have your say in the comments section.

‌



View 2 Images Paris Saint-Germain will once again bid to defend their crown (Image: Carl Recine/Getty Images)

UEFA has been in the headlines over the past week after its 55 member nations unanimously voted to pull out of FIFA competitions during an emergency virtual meeting on Friday. It comes after FIFA controversially unveiled plans to sell off its competitions to private investors.

In response, the European body said: "As a result of today's discussion, no UEFA national teams will participate in any FIFA competition for so long as these proposals remain alive, unless this proposal has been abandoned in its entirety and binding assurances have been given that FIFA will never again open its governance or competitions to private ownership."

‌



UEFA invited other confederations to follow their lead and reportedly believe that a number of Asian countries are also against the plan. "National associations around the world are now presented with an ultimatum: accept the irreversible capture of football's greatest competitions or bear the consequences," it added.

"This is not a 'democratic decision', but governance by intimidation - an act of coercion unworthy of an institution entrusted with the stewardship of the global game."

Sports.content:
Jose Mourinho’s three things he wants from Vinicius Jr as Arsenal transfer outcome awaits

Arsenal transfer target Vinicius Jr has been sent a clear message by Jose Mourinho as the Gunners await a final decision on his future

View 2 Images Real Madrid boss Jose Mourinho has revealed to Vinicius Jr what he expects of him (Image: (Photo by WOLFGANG JANNACH / APA / AFP via Getty Images))

Jose Mourinho has told Arsenal transfer target Vinicius Jr to enjoy himself, be positive and continue playing his style of football. The 25-year-old is back training in the Spanish capital after his break following Brazil's World Cup exit but the focus has instead been on his future amid significant interest from the Gunners.

‌



Vinicius has just one year remaining on his current contract and while there has not been a breakthrough in extension talks for some time, that could be about to change with new discussions set to take place on Wednesday.

‌



As such, Arsenal could be about to learn a definitive transfer outcome over his future with Real's stance clear that he either agrees to extend or is sold this summer.

‌



OPINION Arsenal may be using Vinicius Jr transfer talk as smokescreen for another huge deal by Fasika Zelealem

In the meantime, the forward has been putting in the hard yards alongside his Real team-mates under Mourinho's watchful eye.

In a video posted to Real's official social media channels, he lifted the lid on exactly what the new Los Blancos chief expects from him.

‌



The 26-year-old said: "He wants me to be just as I've always been - happy, positive and playing my own style of football."

Content cannot be displayed without consent

A large number of Real Madrid's recent posts have centred on his comeback, with a 'train with Vini Jr' montage shared on Monday.

In the latest clip, Vinicius goes on to discuss the training sessions he has taken part in so far and looks ahead to the forthcoming season — comments that strongly suggest he has no desire to leave.

Real chiefs appear to be the ones pushing for a departure, with the contract proposal that has been available for some time falling short of Vinicius' salary expectations. Since his return, there have been claims that an enhanced offer has been tabled which would see him earn approximately €22m (£18.9m) per year, though even that remains insufficient.

‌



Arsenal sporting director Andrea Berta and head coach Mikel Arteta, who is now said to be heavily involved in negotiations, seem prepared to meet his financial requirements.

View 2 Images Mikel Arteta and Andrea Berta are targeting a move for Vinicius Jr

Multiple midfielders could be absent for the initial fixtures, but the Premier League champions appear poised to secure an addition that will enhance Arteta's choices. Following his belated return to Newcastle United pre-season training, Arsenal are close to finalising a deal for Bruno Guimaraes.

Progress in that transfer situation comes after Everton launched a bid for Christian Norgaard, with that deal also anticipated to be concluded this week.

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino calls FIFA crisis meeting in desperate attempt to cling to power
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino calls FIFA crisis meeting in desperate attempt to cling to power

FIFA President Gianni Infantino is under mounting pressure to step down from his role over plans to sell off its competitions, including the World Cup, to private investors

View 2 Images Gianni Infantino's plan is rapidly falling apart (Image: DANIEL DUARTE/AFP via Getty Images)

Under-fire FIFA President Gianni Infantino has called his senior staff to a crisis meeting in a bid to cling to power. The desperate move comes after Arsene Wenger, FIFA's Chief of Global Football Development, broke rank and criticised Infantino's controversial plan to sell off competitions including the World Cup.

‌



Former Arsenal manager Wenger issued a statement on Monday saying that the withdrawal of Infantino's plan was 'absolutely necessary'. Meanwhile, Infantino's close allies are said to have been urging many of the 211 member associations to publicly back him after some withdrew their support for his re-election - while the president of one federation accused him of 'blackmail'.

‌



The Times report that Infantino has called staff to the Moroccan capital of Rabat for a crisis meeting. The Swiss chief is holed up in Morocco amid the swam of backlash.

‌



It's added that a group of senior staff within FIFA had a management meeting on Tuesday - without Infantino. All bar one reportedly opposed the plan to sell off FIFA's competitions.

Gianni Infantino accused of blackmail by Jordan FA chief in brutal FIFA criticism READ MORE :

Full list of Gianni Infantino's supporters and critics as FIFA president faces fight for job READ MORE :

Wenger's comments have also piled on pressure. " The recent events at FIFA deserve some clarity from my side. I was not involved in this strategic plan and first became aware of the project through media reports," the Frenchman said.

"The decision to withdraw the project was absolutely necessary and beyond question, because I firmly believe in an independent FIFA that serves our game with commitment, transparency and integrity."

‌



Even Infantino's No.2, FIFA secretary general Mattias Grafstrom, was revealed to have slammed the plan in a leaked email. " We have all been thrown into the middle of a turmoil, which is difficult to comprehend and accept, but, as Secretary General, I urge you to remain focused on what has always united us: serving football and serving our 211 member associations." Grafstrom wrote.

Should Gianni Infantino step down? Have your say in the comments section.

View 2 Images Arsene Wenger has broken rank and criticised the scheme (Image: Jean Catuffe/Getty Images)

‌



"A sad and reproachable series of events - which were thankfully concluded with the FFE project permanently abandoned - for as much as we feel dismayed by them, should not overshadow this reality.

"I assure you that you as members of the administration, you will be defended and safeguarded from the political context we currently experience. You do not need to worry.

"Individuals, unstable moments and unfortunate episodes come and go. The institution, its mission and its responsibility towards world football continue, and that is why we should always keep our professionalism, sense of perspective and composure."

Sports.title: Amanda Staveley suffers major blow to West Ham plan as Daniel Kretinsky fights back
Sports.content:
Amanda Staveley suffers major blow to West Ham plan as Daniel Kretinsky fights back

The battle for ownership at West Ham United has intensified after Daniel Kretinsky responded to Amanda Staveley’s consortium agreeing a £150m deal with the family of David Gold

View 2 Images Amanda Staveley (Image: (Serena Taylor/Newcastle United via Getty Images))

Amanda Staveley has suffered a blow in her attempt to buy into West Ham United after Daniel Kretinsky agreed to sell just over 2% of his stake in the club to Jakub Havrlant.

‌



Within the last few days, Staveley, her husband Mehrdad Ghodoussi, and others agreed to buy a 25.1 per cent stake in the Hammers, who were relegated to the Championship last season.

‌



Staveley’s consortium agreed a £150million deal with the family of the late David Gold on Saturday. But before Staveley can buy it, existing shareholders have first refusal at the price she agreed.

‌



However, Hammers co-chair Kretinsky sold just over 2% of his stake in the club to Czech businessman Havrlant on Tuesday, dealing a blow to Staveley and her consortium. As a result of the deal, BBC Sport explain Kretinsky can now buy Gold's 25.1% stake without his own stake exceeding 50%, which would otherwise force him to make an offer for the remainder of the club.

"I am delighted Jakub Havrlant has joined the West Ham ownership group as a shareholder, subject to the pre-emption process," Kretinsky said. "He brings exceptional experience as an investor and digital innovator and I have no doubt his involvement will strengthen our club."

Gianni Infantino ripped apart as explosive FIFA email leaked after botched World Cup plan READ MORE :

Bruno Guimaraes to Arsenal saga has Newcastle in contention for all-time worst transfer window READ MORE :

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



While speaking on an episode of Bloomberg’s Leaders with Francine Lacqua recorded before West Ham confirmed her agreement with Gold on Saturday, Staveley revealed she is planning a 'big property play' in English football.

She said: “Whatever club we take, there’ll be a big property play as well. We won’t just do a football-led.

“I just want a challenge, and that’s what excites me. That’s where you get value uplift — when you take something from seedling and allow it to grow.”

‌



View 2 Images West Ham United co-chair Daniel Kretinsky (c) looks on during the UEFA Europa Conference League in 2023 (Image: (Chris Brunskill/Fantasista/Getty Images))

Royal Mail owner Kretinsky bought 27% of West Ham in 2021 and for his plan he may need the help of the club’s third-largest shareholder, the American billionaire Albert Tripp Smith, who owns 8 per cent. While The Times are reporting that there are set to be two rounds of bidding.

In the first round, shareholders have 30 days to buy their entitlement, which is up to the same proportion as their present holding. And in the second round, any remaining Gold shares can be bought by shareholders who participated in the first round.

Sports.title: Draper in tears amid injury concern during defeat in Montreal
Sports.content:
Jack Draper was left in tears after losing to Terence Atmane as the Brit's long-term arm injury appeared to resurface and hamper him on his return to action at the Canadian Open.

Playing in just his sixth tournament of the year, and a first since pulling out of Wimbledon, Draper was beaten 6-3 2-6 6-2 by France's Atmane.

After a rusty start, Draper appeared to have found form as he dominated the second set, but his performance suddenly dropped off in the decider as the power in his serves and groundstrokes reduced massively.

When trailing 4-1, Draper sat down and spent the entire changeover crying, apparently uncontrollably.

The 24-year-old carried on and almost claimed a break before spiritedly holding serve one more time, before Atmane closed out victory in an hour and 52 minutes.

Draper had established himself as one of the biggest challengers to Carlos Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner's dominance of the men's game as he moved up to a career high No 4 ranking in June 2025.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the first round match at the Canadian Open between Terence Atmane and Jack Draper.

It was around that time that Draper began suffering from a bone bruise in his left arm, an injury that has continued to hamper him ever since.

In 2026, he put together runs to the quarter-finals at Indian Wells in March and the semi-finals at Eastbourne in June, but has been unable to stay on the court consistently.

Sir Andy Murray has been part of Draper's coaching team since May, but Montreal was just the second tournament he has been able to play in during their partnership.

Draper has a wild card into next week's Cincinnati Open, but his defeat in Montreal is likely to raise fresh doubts over his participation there and at the US Open.

Sports.title: Brook stars as SunRisers thrash Spirit after setting record Hundred total
Sports.content:
SunRisers Leeds posted 241-2, the highest score in the history of The Hundred, before cruising to a comfortable victory over London Spirit.

Having been put into bat by Spirit at Headingley, SunRisers openers Mitchell Marsh and Ryan Rickelton put on a record stand of 148 for the first wicket from just 65 balls.

Harry Brook joined in on the fun once Marsh was out for 76 from 37 balls, with the England white-ball captain smashing 55 from just 18 deliveries.

Brook struck a six to bring up his half-century and take SunRisers past the previous highest Hundred total, the 226-4 set by Oval Invincibles against Welsh Fire last year.

After Brook was caught looking for one more boundary, Dan Lawrence added 10 from the final three deliveries, as Rickelton was left stranded six short a century after not finding his way back onto strike for the final eight balls of the innings.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Take a look at Harry Brook's incredible record-equalling 50, the joint fastest in Hundred history

Any hopes Spirit had of staging a remarkable fightback were quickly dampened by Johnny Bairstow getting caught behind by Rickleton from the bowling of Reece Topley with just the second ball of the innings.

Spirit captain Liam Livingstone got the scoreboard moving with 34 from 13 but saw Lhuan-dre Pretorius fall to Topley at the other end before losing his own wicket to Nathan Ellis.

James Coles and James Rew soon also departed to leave Spirit 56-5 from 26 balls, and with the game all but over.

From there, Matthew Revis (38 from 21), David Willey (83 not out from 46) and Jamie Overton (27 not out from 15) put up some resistance, but there was never a realistic prospect of Spirit chasing down the target.

Sports.title: Several athletes 'unaccounted for' after Commonwealth Games in Glasgow
Sports.content:
Reports in Uganda say that four members of the nation's boxing team have gone missing in Scotland; Police Scotland says it has received reports of several athletes who are unaccounted for following the end of the 2026 Commonwealth Games on Sunday

Commonwealth Games: Several athletes 'unaccounted for' after Glasgow event, according to Police Scotland

Several athletes are "unaccounted for" after the Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games, according to Police Scotland.

The Ugandan sporting news website NBS Sport said that four members of Uganda's boxing team have reportedly gone missing in Scotland.

They said the athletes did not re-join the rest of the delegation before the team's scheduled return to Uganda on Tuesday.

A Police Scotland spokesperson said: "Police Scotland has received reports of several athletes who are unaccounted for.

"Inquiries are ongoing to assess the circumstances, and early engagement is taking place with the Home Office."

Speaking to the Press Association on Monday, Commonwealth Games chief executive Phil Batty said: "We've welcomed nearly 3,000 athletes to the city from 74 nations.

"We want to deliver a safe and secure games, so we work really closely with Police Scotland, the Border Force, and UK visas and immigration to make sure everyone arrives and departs in line with regulation."

PA understands that the Home Office will take action accordingly if it is made aware of any breaches of immigration law, and that it takes all necessary steps to prevent people who could abuse the immigration system from entering the UK.

The Home Office maintains a policy of not routinely commenting on individual asylum cases, with claims considered on their individual merits in accordance with the UK's international obligations.

The Ugandan ministry of education and sports has been contacted for comment.

Sports.title: Sutherland leads SunRisers to tight win over Spirit
Sports.content:
SunRisers Leeds kept their faint hopes of progression from The Hundred group stage alive with a hard-fought five-wicket victory over London Spirit at Headingley.

Spirit made 136-7 after being put in to bat, but Australian duo Phoebe Litchfield (30 from 17) and Annabel Sutherland (37 not out from 21) led the SunRisers home with two balls to spare.

Spirit got off to a flying start with the bat, but SunRisers finally got their first wicket when Amy Jones hit Dani Gibson into the hands of Kate Cross at 68 for one.

London continued to accelerate but their momentum was halted when a rain shower caused a 30-minute delay and Grace Harris, who went past her half-century, also perished as they fell from 91 for one to 136 for seven at the halfway stage.

In reply, Phoebe Litchfield and Bryony Smith also enjoyed themselves at the top of the order and it looked like SunRisers would chase the score down at a canter.

SunRisers closed in on victory, but Gibson and Deepti Sharma fell to create some late drama.

However, a flurry of shots from Jess Jonassen and Sutherland took the hosts close to the finish line before the latter's six gave them the win.

Meerkat Match Hero Sutherland said: "It's nice to get the win. Jess came out with real clarity, and she's got a beautiful swing of the bat. It was nice to see a few go to the rope from her.

Sports.title: Falcons make Robinson highest-paid running back in NFL history
Sports.content:
The Atlanta Falcons have agreed to a three-year contract extension with Bijan Robinson that will make him the highest-paid running back in NFL history.

According to Spotrac.com, the extension, which runs through to the 2030 season, is worth up to $75m (£55m), with the $51m (£37m) guaranteed portion a record for a running back.

Robinson will need to achieve multiple incentives to earn the full $75m (£55m), but even without doing that, the base level three-year $66.75m (£49.6m) deal will give the 24-year-old highest annual salary an NFL running back has ever earnt.

The $22.25m (£16.5m) per year takes him past the previous high mark of $20.6m (£15.3m) being earnt by Saquon Barkley at the Philadelphia Eagles.

Robinson reposted the NFL's Instagram post detailing the extension on Tuesday morning, writing "God this is for you! Blessings. Love this team and this city!"
