On Saturday, the Falcons announced signing left guard Matthew Bergeron to a four-year contract extension. The team gave new contracts to wide receiver Drake London and tight end Kyle Pitts during the offseason.

The new deal comes after Robinson spent the first week of training camp, including Monday's first day in pads, as a spectator.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights as Robinson had a huge game to lead the Falcons to victory over the Buffalo Bills last season.

He attended the practices but did not participate in an apparent contract "hold-in" as he sought a new deal ahead of the start of the NFL regular season on September 10.

A panel of eight AP Pro Football Writers ranked Robinson the league's top running back in a pre-season poll. Robinson led the NFL with 2,298 yards from scrimmage and scored 11 TDs last season.

Robinson has been the focus of Atlanta's productive ground game since he was the No 8 overall pick in the 2023 NFL draft. He flourished as a dual-threat back last season, finishing fourth in the league with 1,478 rushing yards while adding 820 receiving yards.

Steven Jackson in 2006 is the only other player ever with at least 1,400 rushing yards and 800 receiving yards in the same season.

Sports.title: Infantino to hold crisis meeting with senior FIFA staff
Sports.content:
Under-pressure FIFA president Gianni Infantino will hold a crisis meeting with senior staff in Morocco on Wednesday.

Senior staff have been asked to attend the meeting in Rabat after the pressure on the Swiss ramped up on Tuesday as:

Arsene Wenger and Infantino's number two criticised his plans to seek private investment in the World Cup

Jordan accused FIFA of "blackmailing" them over World Cup money in return for their support for Infantino

Ex-FIFA president Sepp Blatter backed Lise Klaveness to replace Infantino

Infantino is now set for crunch talks on Wednesday with senior FIFA executives, including secretary general Mattias Grafstrom, after the president was forced to withdraw his plan to create FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), a company to run the commercial and operational aspects of FIFA's tournaments.

Will Infantino resign at crisis meeting?

Sky Sports News' Kaveh Solhekol:



"This is going to be a very, very tense meeting. We don't know how it's going to end up.

"What is his stance going to be at this meeting? Is he going to throw in the towel and say, 'I can read the room. I can feel which way the wind is blowing. I'm losing support all over the world. I'm losing support inside FIFA as well. I'm going to do the honourable thing and resign.'

"Or is he going to say, 'I fight on. I'm the FIFA president. If you want me to leave, you're going to have to take me down. And I still believe that I have significant support around the world, especially in South America, Africa and Asia.'

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports News takes a closer look at the controversies of Gianni Infantino's tenure at FIFA

"To get to the top of FIFA, you need to be a politician. And if you're a politician, surely you have some instincts. You can sense that you are losing support. You can sense that your position is untenable.

"You sense that you have to do the right thing and resign. Of course, it's going to be in terrible circumstances and he's going to resign in disgrace. If he does decide to resign, this is not the way he would have liked to go out.

"But he's made a cataclysmic error of judgment. And it was not just one quick decision that he got wrong. What we know is that he was plotting with some people close to him for quite a long time to sell off a stake in the World Cup to private investors.

"I haven't spoken to anybody who knows how FIFA works and how football politics works who thinks that Infantino can survive."

Wenger says FIFA U-turn 'necessary'

Former Arsenal manager Wenger, FIFA's chief of global football development, issued a statement on Tuesday saying he was "not involved" in the plan but that the decision to withdraw it was "absolutely necessary and beyond question".

Wenger had faced criticism in recent days for his silence over the FFE plans but spoke out on Tuesday to welcome the withdrawal of the project, adding: "I firmly believe in an independent FIFA that serves our game with commitment, transparency, and integrity."

Image: Arsene Wenger (left) with Infantino

FIFA secretary general Mattias Grafstrom, the second most senior figure in the organisation after Infantino, sent an email to FIFA staff addressing the "sad and reproachable series of events" of the last week "which thankfully concluded with the project being permanently abandoned".

Grafstrom also thanked FIFA staff for their efforts during the World Cup but accepted they had now been "thrown into the middle of a turmoil, which is difficult to comprehend and accept".

Grafstrom promised staff would be "defended and safeguarded from the political context we currently experience", pointedly adding: "Individuals, unstable moments and unfortunate episodes come and go. The institution, its mission and its responsibility towards world football continue."

The comments from Wenger and Grafstrom follow the resignation last week of Infantino's senior adviser Carlos Cordeiro, who described the FFE plan as a "bad deal for football".

Jordanian FA president accuses FIFA of 'blackmail'

Infantino's crisis deepened on Tuesday when FIFA were accused of "blackmailing" Jordan over World Cup money in return for their support for Infantino to stay on as president.

The support of national associations in Asia could prove critical to his survival, but the president of the Jordanian Football Association, Prince Ali Bin Al Hussein, wrote on X that his organisation "certainly" would not endorse Infantino after alleging FIFA sought to secure his support by promising it would help with the recovery of money he said was owed to the JFA.

Prince Ali, who stood for the FIFA presidency in 2015 against Sepp Blatter and against Infantino the following year, hit out at the difficulties faced by Jordanian fans seeking to enter the United States for this summer's World Cup and the "exorbitant" price of tickets, and detailed the "huge costs" in taxes his association faced due to being based in the US rather than Canada or Mexico for the finals.

He then revealed Jordan was still awaiting prize money from last year's Arab Cup, which is organised by FIFA, "while at the same time FIFA brags about how many billions they have in reserve".

"It is clear the problem really is with leadership," Prince Ali added.

"For months, FIFA has been refusing to help us on any of these or other matters - until it was verbally communicated to me during the World Cup that if I endorsed Infantino it would go a long way to helping our FA out.

"We pride ourselves in Jordan in upholding ethical values. We did not endorse him before and certainly will not now. But the whole situation amounts to blackmail and we refuse to give in to that."

Asia is seen as the key continent in any presidential contest that may yet be forced, with Europe and nations from North America, Central America and the Caribbean expected to want Infantino out while Africa, South America and Oceania are expected to back him.

UEFA has also told Infantino it is "actively considering" legal action over the FFE plan and lawyers acting on behalf of the European body have ordered Infantino and other FIFA staff to identify, locate and preserve any documents related to the project.

The plan to create FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), a company to run the commercial and operational aspects of FIFA's tournaments, first emerged in reports by The Times and The Financial Times last Tuesday, before FIFA issued confirmation of some of the details. The most controversial aspect of the plan was the idea to sell 20 per cent of FFE to private investors.

The plan was firmly rejected by European football's governing body UEFA, as well as CONCACAF - the confederation representing nations from North and Central America plus the Caribbean - and the Asian Football Confederation (AFC). UEFA also threatened to boycott FIFA competitions including the World Cup until the plan was scrapped, which it duly was last Saturday.

UEFA said it had nevertheless "lost confidence" in Infantino and a number of its associations - including those of England and Wales - have since formally withdrawn their support for Infantino, with the Scottish Football Association understood to be aligned to UEFA's position.

Blatter wants first female FIFA president to replace Infantino

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports News' chief correspondent Kaveh Solhekol discusses the potential candidates who could challenge Infantino for the FIFA presidency

Former FIFA president Blatter says it is time for a woman to be FIFA president and he has backed Klaveness to replace Gianni Infantino.

Writing on his X account, Blatter says: "Lise Klaveness deserves the utmost respect. She was the only one who always took a clear stand and did not go along with the mainstream. And at FIFA, the time is right for a woman to take the lead".

Klaveness has been the president of the Norway Football Federation (NFF) for the past four years, and before that she was a lawyer and an international footballer.

Under her leadership, the NFF have taken a principled stand on a wide range of issues, even though it has meant being isolated and outnumbered by the vast majority of FAs who have meekly gone along with Infantino's schemes and plans.

She spoke out - in Qatar - about the World Cup being hosted in Qatar in 2022, and she has also criticised Saudi Arabia being awarded the 2034 World Cup in unusual circumstances.

The NFF were among only a handful of FIFA's 211 member associations that did not send letters earlier this year supporting Infantino's re-election bid in March 2027.

Blatter was FIFA president from 1998 to 2015 when he resigned in a corruption scandal.

He was cleared of personal corruption charges by a tribunal in Switzerland last August.

Sports.title: Why have Barcelona broken transfer records to sign Kerolin?
Sports.content:
It's been brief. Kerolin only joined the Women's Super League from the NWSL 18 months ago. She now leaves as the English top-flight's most expensive export.

Kerolin's £1.25m fee breaks record held by Olivia Smith's sale from Liverpool to Arsenal last summer. Barcelona were willing to smash their own transfer policy in pursuit of the Brazilian, too, having never previously paid a fee over £500k.

But Kerolin represents an exception to the rule. It's always been that way, from the start of her journey playing barefoot with boys on the streets of Sao Paulo. She was different. The ball hurt to kick, she confessed, but she did it anyway.

Image: Kerolin played a huge part in Man City winning their first WSL title for a decade in 2025-26

As such, there is perhaps an air of inevitability about the 26-year-old's switch to the four-time European champions. This is the path she expected to follow. "Always the most highly-ranked players are playing here or in Spain," she told Sky Sports upon signing for Man City in January 2025. "To be in the vision of the world."

She leaves a WSL champion.

Being considered among the game's most elite does not necessitate playing for Barcelona, but it helps. Each of the last five Ballon d'Or recipients were representing the Catalonia club at the time of winning the prize. Kerolin is now the team-mate of its current holder Aitana Bonmati.

Indeed, if Ballon d'Or is the mission Barcelona has proven the means. It's fertile ground for notoriety and success, with silverware almost guaranteed and the chance to star in a team undergoing reinvention under Pere Romeu. A summer of change has seen plenty of big names leave: Alexia Putellas, Ona Batlle and Mapi Leon among them.

Image: Former Barcelona captain Alexia Putellas is one of three players to join the WSL this summer

But the turning point for Kerolin follows the departure of forward Salma Paralluelo, a player similar in profile to her. The 22-year-old scored twice in last season's Champions League final, a precocious young talent with a huge appetite for success, now clubless after failing to agree terms.

Kerolin, who once held transfer interest from Arsenal, is perfectly poised to succeed her. Barcelona's need for a player of Kerolin's talents is greater than that of City's, flush with versatile wingers, while the considerable fee sends a well-timed message.

Maintenance as Europe's leading superpower does not come cheap. Barcelona have been burdened by financial constraints over the past few years, reliant on their global pull to attract and retain the game's top stars. But others have caught up; no longer is their lure enough in isolation.

To keep pace, Barcelona must show willing to be as financially front-footed as their European rivals. Kerolin's capture is a statement signing for a side in need of some validation after bidding farewell to four high-profile players in as many weeks. Proof that Romeu is remodelling, rather than revolutionising his team of aces.

Nor is this move an ego trip. Kerolin made 26 WSL appearances for Man City, scoring 12 goals. Only Khadija Shaw and Stina Blackstenius have a better goals-per-90 ratio during that time. No player can match Kerolin for take-ons attempted or completed.

In fact, very few forwards boast her complete skillset. She can balance scoring with creating, on-the-ball craft with off-the-ball industry, and has explosive speed in both directions. She scores screamers, too, with quality off both flanks.

Her departure less than two years after signing will feel premature for many in Manchester, not least City's leading scorer Shaw, for whom she made a habit of assisting.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Take a look at Kerolin's best goals in the Women's Super League

But business is business; a rare deal where the benefits are mutually divided. Man City reap significant return on their investment and make space for one of their other wide forwards to make strides. Any one of Aoba Fujino, Mary Fowler, Iman Beney, or newly-recruited Beth Mead would fit the bill.

Barcelona, meanwhile, have a growing awareness of the increased competition they face to stay queens of Europe. They remain the highest benchmark for success for now, but need fresh impetus to stay there. Kerolin greatly enhances their chances.

Sports.title: Fifa accused of using ‘blackmail’ to force support for Infantino’s re-election bid
Sports.content:
The Jordan Football Association president, Prince Ali bin al-Hussein, has accused Gianni Infantino’s administration of “blackmail”, claiming that Fifa threatened to withhold financial assistance from his federation if it refused to back the president’s bid for re-election.

In a major intervention Prince Ali, who ran for the Fifa presidency against Infantino in 2016 and finished third, listed a number of problems dogging the global governing body and said Jordan’s players have not yet been paid for appearing in the Arab Cup last year. Prince Ali is head of the West Asian Football Federation, which includes influential states such as Qatar and the United Arab Emirates that have thus far backed Infantino to stay on.

It came on a day when Infantino’s authority was dealt a further blow as two more key allies distanced themselves from his failed World Cup private investment plan. His No 2, the Fifa secretary general, Mattias Grafström, was revealed to have called the botched Fifa Forward Enterprise a “sad and reproachable series of events” in an email to the organisation’s staff. Meanwhile the former Arsenal manager Arsène Wenger, who is now Fifa’s chief of global development, said the project’s withdrawal was “absolutely necessary and beyond question”.

Infantino is steadily losing backing from countries who previously had sent letters to endorse his continuation for a fourth term in charge. It is understood that Greece is the latest federation to have pulled its support, following the lead taken by countries such as England, Wales, Finland and Serbia. More European federations are expected to follow in the coming days, while a number of nations in Concacaf – the North and Central American and Caribbean confederation – are also giving serious consideration to withdrawing their backing.

Prince Ali’s statement, published on X, painted the picture of a small country facing a litany of roadblocks when it came to receiving help from the global governing body. Jordan competed in their first World Cup this year but he explained some of their fans had not received visas, despite purchasing tickets, and expressed anger at being taxed by the US for being based in the country.

“We have been waiting for reward money for our players since December for the Arab Cup in Qatar, which is a Fifa event,” his statement read. “The money our team should receive for having reached the final has not been delivered yet, while at the same time Fifa brags about how many billions they have in reserve.

View image in fullscreen The Fifa president, Gianni Infantino (centre), and secretary general, Mattias Grafström (right), with Arsène Wenger during the 2026 World Cup. Photograph: ANP/Shutterstock

“It is clear the problem really is with leadership. For months, Fifa has been refusing to help us on any of these or other matters – until it was verbally communicated to me during the World Cup that if I endorsed Infantino it would go a long way to helping our FA out.

“We pride ourselves in Jordan in upholding ethical values. We did not endorse him before and certainly will not now. But the whole situation amounts to blackmail and we refuse to give in to that.”

Other countries are understood to have been put under concerted pressure to formally back Infantino before the Fifa election in March, although details of how it was applied remain unclear in those cases.

Grafstrom’s email had urged Fifa staff to keep morale high after what was perceived to be a successful World Cup. His message stopped short of criticising Infantino by name and promised to shield colleagues from the strife enveloping their organisation.

“A sad and reproachable series of events – which were thankfully concluded with the FFE project permanently abandoned – for as much as we feel dismayed by them, should not overshadow this reality,” read a section of the email.

11:54 Is Gianni Infantino’s time up as Fifa president? - The Latest

He referred to “a turmoil, which is difficult to comprehend and accept” and said: “Individuals, unstable moments and unfortunate episodes come and go. The institution, its mission and its responsibility towards world football continue, and that is why we should always keep our professionalism, sense of perspective and composure.”

Wenger, who assumed his current position in November 2019, confirmed he had been among the many senior Fifa staff sidelined by Infantino’s plan. “I was not involved in this strategic plan and first became aware of the project through media reports,” he said.

“The decision to withdraw the project was absolutely necessary and beyond question, because I firmly believe in an independent Fifa that serves our game with commitment, transparency, and integrity.”

Fifa was contacted for comment regarding Prince Ali’s accusations.

According to reports, Infantino has called Fifa staff to a crisis meeting in the Moroccan capital, Rabat, today as he tries to cling to his position.

Sports.title: The Fifa family: which confederations could support Infantino or turn against him?
Sports.content:
The pressure is growing on the Fifa president, Gianni Infantino, with many countries withdrawing their support following the bungled World Cup sell-off. However, how key is Infantino’s relationship with each confederation and is it likely that an election contest will actually happen? We look at the key considerations, confederation by confederation.

1) How does each confederation view Infantino’s re-election?

Uefa (Europe) has firmly led the moves under way to achieve Infantino’s removal. The threat last week to boycott all Fifa competitions if the Fifa Forward Enterprise scheme was not scrapped contributed hugely to its failure. In a scathing statement on Saturday, Uefa said the current Fifa leadership had “not only lost Uefa’s confidence, but also that of many other members of the football family”, and pledged to push for change. Some Uefa member associations, including the English and Welsh FAs, have withdrawn their letters of support for Infantino’s re‑election and efforts are continuing to ensure others follow suit in a bid to weaken his position irretrievably. Nick Ames

Reports of AFC (Asia) support for Uefa are premature; the confederation is divided. The AFC has spoken out, strongly in relative terms compared to its usual pronouncements, against the proposed World Cup deal and has called for reform of Fifa. The AFC has been a staunch supporter in the past but if it looks as if Infantino is in trouble the AFC leadership, which was genuinely angry at how the proposal was made (probably more so than the actual details of the deal), could switch sides, which would probably confirm Infantino’s downfall if Uefa and Concacaf oppose but it is not a foregone conclusion – some in Asia are not convinced that Uefa has the numbers. The big problem is that, while the AFC leadership may want Infantino out, most individual Asian federations do not want him to be replaced. The AFC president, Sheikh Salman, has ambitions of his own and has been historically successful at preserving AFC unity but this will be tricky especially as west Asian nations such as Qatar, the United Arab Emirates and Saudi Arabia support Infantino and are influential in Asia. It could be that the only way to ensure Asian unity is to have an Asian candidate. Jordan’s Prince Ali bin Hussein’s claim of “blackmail” could prove a significant moment, however. John Duerden

Concacaf (North and Central America, and the Caribbean) is among the confederations that have come out strongly against Infantino and his FFE proposal, first directly rejecting it and then releasing a statement after it was withdrawn that took direct aim at Infantino. A release speaking on behalf of Concacaf’s 41 member associations called the plan “a symptom of leadership that has stopped putting football first”, and a “unilateral and egregious act of poor governance and leadership” and said that “a comprehensive reckoning with this presidency is imperative”.

That is about as direct a call for no confidence in Infantino as you are likely to get outside of an election itself. It should be noted, of course, that the Concacaf president, Victor Montagliani, is also a Fifa vice-president and would be a leading candidate to run for president should there be a united desire among confederations to oust Infantino. Montagliani has kept silent on the subject when asked in the past but this statement, which speaks for him, shows at the very least he is not immune to the idea of going against Infantino. Alexander Abnos

View image in fullscreen Victor Montagliani, pictured consoling Lionel Messi after the World Cup final, is a potential successor to Gianni Infantino. Photograph: Will Oliver/EPA

Patrice Motsepe, president of the Confederation of African Football, has said the 54 member associations are in unanimous support of Infantino’s re-election in Morocco next year. Osasu Obayiuwana

Since the rumpus over Infantino’s proposed FFE broke and died, the South American confederation, Conmebol, has been notably silent. Its president, Alejandro Domínguez, has been posting birthday wishes to individuals, clubs and institutions from Uruguay where he is visiting ahead of the 2030 centenary of the first World Cup. Unlike Uefa, Concacaf and the AFC, which publicly opposed Fifa’s aborted FFE proposal, Conmebol took several days before issuing a fence-sitting statement stressing football first, and requesting further information and clarification. That was the only official response at all, and there has been absolute silence since.

“Conmebol’s current position is best described as cautious support rather than open confrontation,” says Marina Mendez, a director of AD Sporting Industry Professionals and a friend of Conmebol who consults on football in the region. “The distinction is politically significant. It suggests Conmebol wants to preserve its institutional relationship with Fifa and maintain room for negotiation, rather than join a public campaign against Infantino. This should not necessarily be interpreted as unconditional personal loyalty. Conmebol’s approach is pragmatic: it is protecting South American football’s access, influence and negotiating position within Fifa while assessing how the international balance of power develops.”

Brazil and Argentina are the main countries, and Domínguez looks after the relationship with both, with most of the other countries expected to follow suit. “They are not federations likely to confront Infantino directly because they will always prefer to be on the right side of the non-Europeans,” says an industry insider who does not wish to be named. Marcela Mora y Araujo

It remains to be seen what the 11 Oceania Football Confederation member associations will do. New Zealand, the leading member of the confederation, was quick to come out against the World Cup proposal – though the reaction of the OFC itself was noncommittal – and there is still support for Infantino among the other federations. John Duerden

Uefa The parties go back a long way. Infantino was Uefa’s secretary general from 2009 until 2016 and it backed him strongly when he first ran for the Fifa presidency. But there has long been push and pull between the global governing body and that of football’s most powerful continent. Relations have deteriorated in recent years, Uefa fending off Infantino-led initiatives such as a biennial staging of the World Cup and a proposed investment in 2018 by SoftBank. Things appeared to reach a head in May 2025 when delegates from several European federations walked out of Fifa’s annual congress in protest at Infantino’s late arrival. They accused him of pursuing “private political interests”. That turned out to be the tip of the iceberg. The past year’s near-interminable list of Fifa-related controversies have further ensured that the differences between the two are irreconcilable. NA

AFC It has been a close relationship, Salman and AFC have backed Infantino since he beat Salman in the 2016 election. It is not just about money either, though this is of course important. He is seen as approachable, available and open. Fifa has historically been seen as a European (and to a lesser extent South American) institution in Asia, and while Infantino is from Uefa, he is seen as a leader who gives equal weight to all. One president said to me that in the past, conversations with Fifa were like receiving decrees from above but now there is a genuine dialogue. World Cup expansion has gone down well, 64 teams would be welcomed too, and there are more tournaments held in Asia these days. Infantino has already been reminding Asia about this. JD

View image in fullscreen Sheikh Salman and the AFC have backed Gianni Infantino since he beat Salman in the 2016 election. Photograph: Vincent Thian/AP

Concacaf Infantino’s most direct relationship has been as the president under whom the World Cup was awarded to the US, Mexico and Canada, after a bid from the US lost out to Qatar for the 2022 hosting rights. Aside from that, there was not much of a direct, historic relationship between Infantino and Concacaf – at least, not until the letter released by the confederation over the weekend. AA

CAF Infantino’s association with African football began in 2016, when he backed Ahmad Ahmad of Madagascar to topple the late Issa Hayatou as CAF president in March 2017. Being an eyewitness to that election, at the African Union HQ in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, I recall the anger with which Hayatou confronted Infantino and Fatma Samoura, then Fifa secretary general, over their involvement in an election.

Infantino, under Ahmad’s ill-fated four-year tenure between 2017 and 2021 – which ended in his untimely removal from office over ethics violations – got Fifa to take over the daily administration of the CAF from August to December 2019, with Samoura going to Egypt to take charge of the organisation. Many in African football saw this as a neo-colonial act and a direct violation of the CAF’s autonomy and independence. Infantino was involved in the ascension of Motsepe to the presidency in March 2021. OO

Conmebol Along comes Infantino, the Uefa salvation who promises an anti-corruption ticket. After Julio Grondona’s death, an AFA (Argentina Football Association) election found more votes than members and Fifa intervened, naming a committee of industry insiders to oversee a cleansing of the house. Infantino was present in the AFA headquarters at its inaugural press conference. Imagine Infantino launching an English FA governance intervention.

In 2018, in Buenos Aires for a Libertadores final to be played by two clubs from the same city for the first time in Argentina’s history (policing was a mess and fan violence before the second leg led to its suspension and eventual move to Madrid) Infantino was invited by the then president of Argentina, Mauricio Macri, to be guest of honour at the G20 held in the city later that week.

Infantino, as we know him today is created then, photographed gifting football shirts to the Saudi crown prince Mohammed bin Salman and Donald Trump, POTUS at the time. “Yes, that G20 was key for Infantino, because he’d inherited a corruption scandal. He needed to instil the belief that football would cease to be a mafia, that he would achieve this. And he managed,” Macri, now president of the Fifa Foundation, told the Guardian: “From an ethical point of view he is impeccable. There is nothing odd in Fifa today, Fifa manages fortunes, more than ever, because Infantino is successful; he organises competitions that are more and more profitable, and it’s all above board. I should say the same applies to Conmebol.”

The Conmebol president, Nicolás Leoz, fell in the same Fifagate swoop, although he had left office in 2013. A series of interim and short-lived presidencies ensued until January 2016 when current president Domínguez took his post. Unanimously voted in by the 10 member associations, he pushed for every professional club to have a female team and introduced “hydration” breaks before this World Cup, albeit less structured ones. Infantino has also maintained a functional and stable relationship with the AFA president, Claudio “Chiqu” Tapia. “This relationship is politically relevant because Macri has been an opponent of “Chiqui” Tapia,” Mendez says. “This demonstrates Infantino’s ability to maintain links with both sides of Argentine football’s internal power structure.” Tapia was approached for comment. MMA

View image in fullscreen Claudio Tapia of Argentina’s FA has a stable relationship with the Fifa president. Photograph: Agustín Marcarian/Reuters

OFC Like Asia, Infantino has worked hard to build relationships both of the personal and financial kind. It is common to hear officials describe him as a friend. The expansion of the World Cup to 48 teams finally gave Oceania an automatic World Cup spot – something that Fifa had promised in the past but never delivered. And the idea of having more spots in a 64-team competition was also attractive. Under Infantino, New Zealand co-hosted the Women’s World Cup with Australia. Fifa also supported the establishment of the Oceania Professional League that kicked off in January to provide much-needed pro club football for the region. JD

3) How financially dependent is the confederation on Infantino and Fifa?

Uefa Not at all. While the World Cup is Fifa’s most essential driver of revenue, Uefa can lay claim, among other things, to the highly lucrative Champions League and the vast sums that it attracts on an annual basis. Expanding its tournaments and staging them more often is one of the only ways available for Fifa to keep pace. Private investment would not harm its cause, either. Uefa’s annual revenues have recently totalled around double those of Fifa; as things stand football’s powerhouse can cope perfectly well on its own. NA

AFC Like always in Asia, it varies. There are rich federations on either side of the continent but in between there are some that are almost completely dependent on Fifa money. Bhutan, for example, gets $1.5m a year, which makes up the majority of its budget. Even Australia, which has reached the knockout stages of the past two World Cups, has lost around $17m over the past two years, which may explain its rather vague statement calling for more time when the plan was first heard. JD

View image in fullscreen Paul Okon Engstler, Jackson Irvine and Harry Souttar after Australia’s World Cup exit; even their federation, one of AFC’s richest, loses money. Photograph: Kai Pfaffenbach/Reuters

Concacaf This is a very top‑heavy confederation, perhaps more so than any other in the world. The US and Mexico have been regional powers for most of the past 30‑40 years, and recently Canada has shown signs it can compete on the field and is addressing business issues off of it. Just below them is a middle class consisting of Panama, Jamaica, Costa Rica and Honduras. The remaining 33 Concacaf nations are fairly small by comparison, and thus naturally more reliant on funding from Fifa via the forward programme and other initiatives. The fact that smaller Caribbean nations feel empowered to join with the big dogs says a lot about how at risk they feel they may be without Infantino at Fifa’s helm. AA

CAF The confederation funds activities from its own commercial revenue, so it is not dependent on Fifa and Infantino in that sense. But the majority of CAF’s 54 member associations are financially challenged and are dependent on the annual grants that the world governing body gives them to meet their operating costs. OO

Conmebol It represents only 10 nation members. Variations among them notwithstanding, the federations are self-sufficient economically and their local leagues are attractive and profitable. Their national teams are the No 1 sporting attraction, pulling in vast numbers of fans who are emotionally attached to their heroes, who in turn love to play for their country. The main sources of revenue for clubs are TV rights, marketing and the sale of players. For this, the top market is the Premier League (which operates entirely outside the FA and therefore Fifa) and the other European leagues, which are also largely independent of their FAs. Montevideo has produced more World Cup players than any other city in history, so even a financially struggling association such as Uruguay’s continues to rely more on the income from the development of youth talent than Fifa aid. There were six Argentinian managers with extensive international trajectories at this World Cup. Exporting home‑grown talent, of which there is plenty, is a bigger source of revenue than Fifa project distribution funds. Two of the most colourful stories of the World Cup, the Cape Verde goalkeeper Vozinha and the New Zealand defender Tim Payne, transferred to Chilean and Paraguayan clubs respectively following their popularity during the tournament. Popularity due in no small part to the efforts of streamers and influencers from Argentina and Brazil. MMA

OFC Oceania is made up of small federations that tend to be reliant on what Fifa gives them. So the recent World Cup proposal would, had it gone through, have made a huge difference financially. JD

4) Would a breakaway cause an existential threat?

Uefa Europe has the strongest club and international teams in the world. Parting ways from Infantino and Fifa would be unlikely to cause serious damage, although it could cause issues with clubs who have been looking to expand their global reach through the revamped Club World Cup. It is plausible that bigger teams from other continents would seek to join forces with Uefa and compete in new tournaments given the kudos and financial opportunities available when competing with the majority of the sport’s giants. NA

View image in fullscreen European clubs such as Chelsea have been looking to expand their global reach through Fifa’s revamped Club World Cup. Photograph: Justin Lane/EPA

AFC It is a generalisation but, in Asia, Fifa as an institution does not make the headlines that it does in western Europe. Usually, interest in a country comes when they are affected specifically by a decision, as when bidding for a tournament. In my experience, there just isn’t the same interest in the day‑to‑day running of the organisation. Breaking with Infantino would not be a massive threat to Asia but there is some concern about a return to a more Europe‑dominated Fifa, if that were to materialise. While pretty much everyone has supported Infantino from 2016 until the past few days, Asian federations that have done so are seen in some quarters as being corrupt and/or greedy but the Europeans, who did exactly the same, are now trying to paint themselves as the moral guardians of the sport. JD

Concacaf If a breakaway would cause an existential threat, then Concacaf is living it right now. One could certainly read it as a principled stand, but it’s hard to separate the confederation’s statement with Montagliani’s current position as Infantino’s most likely successor, should the latter need to stand down. AA

CAF The relationship between Infantino and Africa’s 54 national associations is largely seen as a “master-servant” one, in which he basically tells the FA/federation heads, through Fifa officials, to do his bidding. Those who do not toe the political line of Zurich, as decided by Infantino, may well end up having their books audited over how they have spent their Fifa grants. Many FA/federation presidents faced Fifa ethics proceedings and subsequent bans as a result. OO

Conmebol “There’s no morality involved, just politics,” the industry insider says. Mendez concurs: “It’s not a simple case of morality, it’s a power struggle and a rupture in perspectives about football in general and the business of football in particular. Today, Eurocentrism is dominating, and things like sponsored hydration breaks and Super Bowl-style half-time shows impose a North American regard hitherto unseen.” MMA

OFC Oceania welcomed the fact that Infantino had a “global” mentality and went out of his way to engage with smaller nations far from the centre of global football power. If the confederation does break away, it would want something similar in the opposition candidate and not a return to the old days when the confederation was an afterthought in the corridors of power. JD

5) How important is the current and historical relationship?

A strong relationship between Uefa and Fifa would make for a far more harmonious global football scene but, as described above, there is huge work to do before that can be repaired. NA

It’s very important – barring some new organisation stepping in to run world football in a better way, Fifa is Concacaf’s best link to the traditional power centres of world football. The US, Mexico and Canada derive a lot of their value as federations from how they’ve been able to perform at men’s and women’s World Cups – that’s not something they’ll want to give up lightly, which is perhaps why they did not threaten a boycott the way Uefa did. AA

CAF Africa’s political power within Fifa began to rise in 1974, when João Havelange successfully courted the continent as a block and made it an important pillar of his electoral victory over Sir Stanley Rous in Germany, becoming the first and only non-European, to date, to be Fifa president. Sepp Blatter, Havelange’s successor in 1998, also leveraged Africa’s support in a similar fashion to defeat the Uefa president Lennart Johansson. Delivering on his promise to the continent that it would host a World Cup during his presidency, which South Africa did in 2010, bolstered his popularity and support base on the continent. But the last 10 years of the Infantino presidency have made many resent the undue influence of the world governing body in Africa’s affairs. OO

View image in fullscreen Sepp Blatter, pictured with the then South Africa president Jacob Zuma at the 2010 World Cup, cultivated support in African football. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian

Conmebol Fifa as we know it was essentially invented, developed and moulded by the Brazil and Argentina federation presidents Havelange and Grondona respectively. They specifically wanted to break Europe’s stronghold. Initially, they started funding grassroots via “partnerships” with big brands, which benefited from reaching wider markets. A vivid example is the giant sign with a Coca-Cola bottle on every corner of the pitch, seen in places such as Russia and China where advertising was otherwise prohibited, every single time a corner kick was awarded. After Havelange’s time at the helm was up, Blatter took the lead. Blatter kept Grondona close by, his right-hand man, while the business venture grew and grew, and places for other confederations increased. When Fifagate blew up, most leaders close to the top faced trials and disgrace; Grondona was saved by death.

Infantino’s reign was a continuation of keeping Conmebol as a key ally. The historic power derived from on-the-pitch success in the region, and the crown jewel that is Lionel Messi, have contributed to keeping the small confederation big. “The relationship is neither purely personal nor purely institutional. It is built on mutual strategic value,” says Mendez. “The coming election will be Uefa versus footballistic populism,” the industry source said. “Conmebol owns Fifa.” MMA

Sports.title: Trabzonspor aim to sign Mohamed Salah this week after opening transfer talks
Sports.content:
The Turkish Super Lig side Trabzonspor say they have begun transfer ⁠negotiations with Mohamed Salah, with the club chair adding they hoped to sign the Egypt forward later this week.

“Negotiations have been launched ⁠to transfer professional footballer ⁠Mohamed Salah, ​who is in a free status, to our club,” the club said in a statement.

Speaking to the broadcaster ⁠A Spor, the Trabzonspor chair Ertugrul Dogan said that while the transfer was not completed, Salah is expected to arrive ⁠in Istanbul for a medical on Wednesday and then go to Trabzon to sign with the ​Black Sea side.

He did not confirm ‌when the contract would be ‌signed, but said it would likely be on Thursday.

Salah left Liverpool this summer after nine ‌years, having scored 257 goals in 442 appearances, where he won the Premier League twice and the Champions League once.

In the 2024-25 season Salah scored 29 Premier League goals and provided 18 assists, equalling the league record for most goal involvements in a season and setting the record for a 38-game campaign.

He was named Premier League Player ‌of the Season and won the Golden Boot and the Playmaker Award, becoming the first player to take all three in one campaign.

His output ​waned last season, with seven goals and seven assists in 27 league matches and he was left on the bench in Champions League games, leading to a public spat with Liverpool’s then-manager Arne Slot.

The 34-year-old began his career in Europe at Swiss side Basel in 2012 and ⁠later joined Chelsea. He also had brief stints at Fiorentina and Roma between 2015 and 2017 ​before joining Liverpool.

Trabzonspor – generally ​considered to be the fourth-biggest team in Turkey after Istanbul ​sides Fenerbahce, Galatasaray, and ‌Besiktas – finished third ​in the Super Lig ​last season and will enter the Europa League playoffs.

Salah had been close to joining Istanbul club Besiktas, whose football director Onder Ozen said negotiations had stalled over financial and image-rights demands, according to local media.

Sports.title: Manchester United set to appoint former Hearts manager Eva Olid as new head coach
Sports.content:
Manchester United are set to appoint the former Hearts manager Eva Olid as their new head coach to replace Marc Skinner, following his exit on Monday, multiple sources have told the Guardian.

Talks with the 40-year-old are understood to be very advanced and she is expected to be introduced to the United squad on Wednesday.

United are confident that the Spanish coach is the right person to lead them into a new chapter, as first reported by the Telegraph, as the Women’s Super League club focuses on developing young, homegrown players.

Olid led Hearts to their first Scottish Women’s Premier League title last term on a dramatic final day of the season, but it had already been confirmed in April that she was to leave the Edinburgh club this summer by mutual agreement. She was in charge of Hearts for five years and also guided them to the 2024 Scottish Cup final, where they were beaten by Rangers.

She has previously coached in the United States with Houston Dynamo, working with their women’s team and their under-19s men’s squad, before she had a spell with the Catalan Football Association.

United are understood to be impressed by her playing style and her ability to develop and improve players, and they carried out extensive background checks on Olid prior to publicly announcing Skinner’s departure on Monday, with succession planning having already been well under way.

Skinner left partly because of frustration at United’s transfer strategy. The club are understood to feel the current level of spending across the WSL is unsustainable and they want a different approach, focusing on their own younger talents and improving their academy to deliver longer-term success.

View image in fullscreen Marc Skinner left Manchester United party because of frustration over the club’s transfer strategy. Photograph: John Clifton/Action Images/Reuters

United finished fourth in the WSL last term. They start the new season away to big-spending London City Lionesses on 4 September.

The news comes on the day that the United captain, Maya Le Tissier, said her team will “stick together” and be ready for the new WSL season, despite Skinner departing.

Le Tissier and the rest of the playing squad were informed by Skinner that he would be leaving, in a meeting on Monday morning shortly before the news was announced, and on Tuesday Le Tissier and her England teammate Ella Toone paid tribute to Skinner for his contribution to the club over five years in charge, which included winning the 2024 Women’s FA Cup.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Le Tissier said the “energy he brought to the club was amazing”, while Toone told reporters: “He wanted to tell the team before it came out. It was nice that he was able to tell us [and] he was able to say goodbye, because he’s done a lot for the club. We can’t thank him enough for everything he’s done, the hard work and the passion that he’s put into leading this team.”

Le Tissier said that neither she nor Toone have been consulted on who the next head coach should be but added: “I think the club have been pretty clear with what they’ve said, bringing through the youth, that’s what something Manchester United has been kind of made for, and they’ve always done that historically. I think they’ve been pretty clear with that. When we speak to the new manager, the ambitions will be clear.

“Me and Tooney are at Man United because we want to win and we’ll be doing everything we can to make that happen. We’ve got a great team, a great squad, great girls. I’m ready to do that.

“No matter who comes and goes, we’ve always had that togetherness and that fight for each other and we stick together in tough moments. There’s been a few over the years and we’ve always come through as a team, and, yeah, this one might be difficult right now, we’re in the start of pre-season and we want to make sure that we’re 100% ready for the start of the season.

“We spoke to the girls today, we’ll stick together, we always do. We’ve got to go out on the pitch, enjoy playing football and being with each other and we’ll get through it.”

Sports.title: Barcelona sign Brazil forward Kerolin from Manchester City for club-record £1.25m
Sports.content:
Barcelona have signed the Brazil forward Kerolin from Manchester City for an undisclosed fee that sources say is in the region of £1.25m, which would represent the largest sum received for a sale by a Women’s Super League side.

The deal is also a club-record for Barcelona, and in terms of a fee received by an English club it eclipses the £1m that Liverpool received for the sale of Olivia Smith in Arsenal in 2025 and Melvine Malard’s more recent £850,000 switch from Manchester United to Chelsea.

Kerolin, 26, was part of the City side that won the WSL title and the Women’s FA Cup last season and was with the club for 18 months, after arriving from North Carolina Courage in January 2025.

City have already added the England forward Beth Mead to their squad this summer, on a free transfer from Arsenal.

The defending European champions Barcelona are understood to see Kerolin as a player who can thrive in the Champions League and become a regular goalscorer in that competition with her pace and trickery on the ball.

A statement from Barcelona, who said goodbye to the Spain internationals Alexia Putellas, Mapi León, Ona Batlle and Salma Paralluelo this summer, read: “The signing of Kerolin Nicoli is another clear statement of FC Barcelona’s ambition. The club remains committed to bringing together the best players in world football with the aim of staying at the top of the game and continuing to set the standard for excellence.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“The Brazilian international arrives at one of the best moments of her career to strengthen a squad built to compete for every trophy. With her talent, creativity and ability to decide matches, Kerolin adds even more quality to a team whose ambition remains unchanged: to challenge for every title and, once again, strive to win it all.”

Sports.title: Arsenal target Vinícius says Mourinho ‘wants me to be happy’ at Real Madrid
Sports.content:
Vinícius Júnior is settling into life under the new Real Madrid manager, José ⁠Mourinho, with a smile on his face even as uncertainty swirls around the Brazil forward’s future at the Bernabéu.

The 26-year-old, who has ⁠been ​one of the linchpins of Real Madrid’s attack in recent years, gave an upbeat assessment of his second ⁠day of pre-season training under Mourinho despite speculation linking him with a possible move to Arsenal.

“It has ⁠gone very well, getting to know the new coach and the new ​players, and training very hard,” ‌Vinícius told Real Madrid ‌TV. “Mourinho wants me to be as I have always been: happy, cheerful ‌and playing my football.”

Vinícius’s cheerful demeanour, however, masks a potentially thorny situation brewing behind the scenes. He is in the final year of his Real Madrid contract, with speculation that the club and player remain locked in negotiations while Arsenal explore a potential transfer.

Vinícius has scored 128 goals for Madrid and provided 100 assists, with the club reluctant to ​let one of their prized assets leave for free next year.

He had a busy summer playing for Brazil at the World Cup, where they were knocked out in the last 16, and his focus now is ⁠on preparing for the new campaign.

“We have to prepare physically ​so that during the ​season we have fewer ​injuries and can count on everyone,” said Vinícius, who was ​Brazil’s top scorer ‌at the ​World Cup with ​four goals.

“It was a good training session and we all left very tired, but now it’s time to rest for tomorrow. That’s how pre-season is and we have to be ready.”

Sports.title: Frank Lampard hails ‘huge’ signing as Coventry seal record £22.5m Rushworth deal
Sports.content:
Coventry have completed the club-record £22.5m signing of goalkeeper Carl Rushworth from Brighton as Frank Lampard’s side continue to prepare for their return to the Premier League after 25 years away.

The 25-year-old excelled on loan at Coventry in the Championship last season, playing an instrumental role in their promotion as champions, starting all 46 league matches and earning the Golden Glove award for keeping 17 clean sheets.

“It’s great to have Carl back with us on a permanent basis,” said Lampard, whose side begin their season at Arsenal on 21 August. “He’s a top professional, a great character and he had a huge impact on the team to help us get promoted last season. I’m looking forward to working with him again and welcoming him back into the group.”

Rushworth, who is also highly regarded within the Football Association and the England setup, joined Brighton from non-league Halifax in 2019 but departed the club without making a senior appearance. Before his season at Coventry he had enjoyed loans across the league pyramid with Walsall, Lincoln City, Swansea and Hull.

Brighton’s sporting director, Mike Cave, said: “While we would have liked to keep Carl with the club for longer, we respect his decision to secure regular first-team football in the Premier League.” Brighton are thought to have negotiated a sell-on clause and a buy-back option as part of the sale, which could rise as high as £30m including add-ons.

Rushworth represents Coventry’s fourth summer signing. Last month they eclipsed their previous transfer record when paying Eintracht Frankfurt £17m to sign the Switzerland defender Aurèle Amenda, and have also signed Loum Tchaouna and Frank Onyeka. Until Amenda’s arrival, their record outlay was £7.7m, to Antalyaspor, for Haji Wright in 2023.



Elsewhere, Aston Villa have welcomed the court of arbitration for sport (Cas) upholding their appeal to register 17-year-old striker Brian Madjo. The teenager, who was born in London but raised in Luxembourg, joined Villa from Metz in January but had been ineligible to play owing to Fifa’s regulations on international transfers of minors. Madjo, who has scored four goals in pre-season, is now available to feature for Villa.

Sports.title: ‘I can’t wait’: Dominik Szoboszlai hungry for Liverpool reset under Andoni Iraola
Sports.content:
Dominik Szoboszlai believes last season’s frustration can push Liverpool to challenge for the title again but admits the squad must produce “something special” if no reinforcements arrive before the transfer deadline.

The Liverpool midfielder upped his already impressive level last season, being named the club’s player of the year, but collectively the team went into reverse with Arne Slot losing his job as a consequence. The poor title defence from a team that won the Premier League comfortably in Slot’s debut season should, Szoboszlai insists, prompt a reaction in Andoni Iraola’s debut campaign as Liverpool head coach.

“I can’t wait [for the new season], honestly,” said the Hungary captain following Liverpool’s pre-season tour of the US. “I feel that we are ready to go again and take motivation from last season because it was not the best. We didn’t end up where we wanted to. So now we’re going to go for it again.

“Everyone is motivated. I think I see in everybody’s eyes that he wants to play and, if you want to play, you have to give your best. And from there the manager is going to decide who is going to play. But everybody is on zero right now.”

Liverpool have added the central defender Jérémy Jacquet and the versatile forward Victor Muñoz this summer but, while they remain in pursuit of Paris Saint-Germain’s Bradley Barcola, a squad that has seen Mohamed Salah, Andy Robertson and Ibrahima Konaté depart as free agents remains light in several positions.

Szoboszlai said of Liverpool’s transfer activity: “It’s not my job to tell you who we have to sign or if we have to sign someone. If the guys above and the manager decide to sign someone, then we are very happy and are going to welcome him – or them – well. If they decide not to, then we have to do something special with this squad.”

View image in fullscreen Liverpool’s new head coach, Andoni Iraola, cuts a thoughtful figure during the US pre-season tour. Photograph: Geoff Stellfox/Getty Images

The Liverpool midfielder revealed Iraola prefers not to address his players in the immediate aftermath of a game, a trait he discovered after the pre-season friendlies against Sunderland, Wrexham and Leeds. “He doesn’t speak after the game,” Szoboszlai disclosed. “I think every manager is different in his own way. That’s how he is. He always would rather speak the day after the game, which is fine for everyone. We have to get used to this.”

Iraola has also not spoken to Szoboszlai – or any other player for that matter – about filling one of the vice-captaincy positions vacated by Robertson and Salah. But the 25-year-old, who captained Liverpool on the US tour, says it would be a huge honour to be asked.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

He added: “There hasn’t been any conversation. We have Virgil [van Dijk] as the captain, we have Ali [Alisson], we have Joe Gomez [as vice-captains], so there was no conversation at all. Obviously Ali is not here and Joe is injured. Let’s see. It’s not fixed. If you get offered the vice-captain of Liverpool, you’re going to take it. It would be a proud moment for me but I respect everybody. Whoever it’s going to be, we’re going to follow them.”

The captain’s armband became an issue for Curtis Jones when Szoboszlai passed it to Kostas Tsimikas during the win over Wrexham in New York. But Szoboszlai, who recently signed a new five-year contract at Anfield, insisted there was no problem with his fellow midfielder.

“It was never a debate between us three,” he claimed. “We just discussed something on the pitch. After, you guys make it very big. But next time we will manage to do it in the changing room. Nobody was angry. It’s all cleared. We are cool, everybody.”

Sports.title: Liverpool eye PSG wonderkid, 18, alongside Bradley Barcola transfer
Sports.content:
Liverpool are eyeing up a move for PSG teenager Ibrahim Mbaye, talkSPORT understands.

The Reds are in the market for a new winger in the summer transfer window following Trabzonspor-bound Mohamed Salah's exit earlier in the year.

2 PSG teenager Mbaye has emerged as a top attacking target for Liverpool

Andoni Iraola's men have already signed Victor Munoz to strengthen the left flank, and are eyeing up a bumper move for Bradley Barcola.

And Barcola isn't the only PSG star that the Merseyside giants are courting.

Mbaye has emerged as a potential target for Liverpool as they seek to strengthen their right flank.

The 18-year-old started ten league matches for Luis Enrique's men as PSG secured Ligue 1 glory once again.

Mbaye, who is also able to play on the left flank, scored three goals and provided two assists in France's top tier.

The forward was also part of the Senegal squad for the 2026 World Cup, and struck what proved to be a late consolation in their eventual 3-1 loss to semi-finalists France.

PSG are reluctant to lose Mbaye, but may be forced to cash in on the talented teenager, who is contracted to the Parisian powerhouse until 2028.

Mbaye has been on the PSG books since 2018, when he joined from Versailles.

Where has Mohamed Salah gone?

Having announced he'll call time on a legendary nine-year spell at Liverpool back in March, Salah has only recently confirmed his next club.

A lucrative summer switch to Saudi Arabia was expected for the Egypt star, though a move to the Middle East failed to materialise.

2 Salah will sign for Trabzonspor this week

And having rebuffed Besiktas' offer, Salah has instead signed for fellow Turkish Super Lig side Trabzonspor.

"Negotiations have begun regarding the transfer of professional footballer Mohamed Salah to our club," a club statement read on Tuesday.

Trabzonspor finished the 2025/26 Super Lig season in third place, eight points behind eventual champions Galatasaray.

And a move to Papara Park will see Salah link up with former Premier League stars Andre Onana and Paul Onuachu.

Onana spent last season on loan with Trabzonspor, and re-joined the Turkish for the 2026/27 campaign at the start of July.

Sports.title: Premier League club increase capacity of stadium as part of £40m project
Sports.content:
Premier League club increase capacity of stadium as part of £40m project

Brighton have spent the summer giving the Amex Stadium a makeover in time for the new season.

The Seagulls confirmed their intention to expand their home ground earlier in the year.

2 Brighton boasted the seventh best home record in the Premier League last season Credit: Getty

"The club can confirm safe-standing will be extended to the lower rows of the North Stand in September 2026," a statement read on the club's official website at the time.

"Following a review of the voting, safe-standing is moving to lower rows but only in more central blocks where this had the most support.

"This may mean that sight lines are impacted for the seats situated immediately next to safe standing areas.

"For those supporters whose seats will be converted to safe standing, a priority window will be available to move elsewhere in the stadium."

And the summer renovations means they have expanded their capacity to 32,500 in time for Brighton's Premier League opener against Aston Villa on Sunday August 23.

The changes also mean that away fans will be relocated to the south-west corner of the stadium in time for the 2027/28 season.

Meanwhile, a new premium hospitality space, known as the 1901 Club, has been added to the North Stand as part of the project worth £40million.

What is safe-standing?

Brighton are the latest Premier League side to implement safe-standing.

The likes of Tottenham Hotspur, Manchester United and Chelsea, who signed Danny Welbeck from Brighton last week, have all adopted rail seating.

2 Safe-standing has become increasingly popular in the Premier League Credit: Getty

Safe-standing is a measure in place that ensures spectators are able to stand safely during events.

The idea is to boost the home team and provide a more intimidating atmosphere for visiting sides.

It's become popular once more among the top-flight teams, all of which were forced to implement all-seater stadiums in the 1990s owing to a number of fatal incidents at football matches, notably Hillsborough, where 97 Liverpool fans tragically lost their lives in 1989.

Brighton will be hoping to increase in capacity will benefit them when they face either Romanian side CFR Cluj or Norwegian outfit Tromso in their UEFA Conference League playoff later this month.

The Seagulls will play the first leg away from home on 20 August.

And they'll play the reverse fixture in front of their home fans a week later as they seek to maximise home advantage and book a spot in Europe's third tier competition.

Brighton first moved into the Amex Stadium in 2011, having earned promotion from League One to the Premier League in that time.

Sports.title: Mohamed Salah to make shock Turkey transfer as club gives statement
Sports.content:
Mohamed Salah is set to sign for Turkish club Trabzonspor on a two-year contract.

The Liverpool legend will join on a free transfer having brought the curtain down on an iconic nine-year spell at Anfield.



3 Salah joins as a free agent having mutually agreed to end his contract with Liverpool a year early Credit: Getty

And now he's set for a new challenge in the Turkish Super Lig, with Trabzonspor giving a statement confirming they were in for the 35-year-old.

It read: "Negotiations have begun regarding the transfer of professional footballer Mohamed Salah to our club."

Salah will arrive in Istanbul on Wednesday before making the journey to Trabzon, located in north east Turkey, on the same day to complete his move.



Trabzonspor add that they will share further developments on Salah's move in due course.

He joins a Trabzonspor side that came third in the Turkish top flight last season, finishing eight points behind champions Galatasaray.



That was not enough to qualify for the Champions League with Trabzonspor set to compete in a Europa League qualification play-off later this month. Their opponent is yet to be determined.

Liverpool departure

His imminent move comes months after Salah confirmed he was calling time on his Liverpool career in an emotional message to fans in March.



He leaves a Liverpool legend having won two Premier League titles, the FA Cup, the Champions League as well as boasting two Carabao Cup winners' medals.

3 Salah leaves Liverpool as a certified club and Premier League legend Credit: Getty

However, the individual accolades he won in Liverpool colours are arguably more impressive with Salah winning three PFA Player of the Year awards. He also won four Golden Boot prizes.

Just before the 2024/25 season, Salah put pen to paper on a two-year contract, however, he left halfway through.



talkSPORT understands Salah agreed to 'amend' the last year of his £20million-a-year contract to be allowed to leave for free in a similar settlement to the termination of former Liverpool boss Jurgen Klopp's contract in 2024.

Talks over an exit from Merseyside began before the start of the Africa Cup of Nations in late December.

This came shortly after a public falling out with then-Liverpool boss Arne Slot with Salah accusing the Dutchman of wanting him gone.

'Why on earth has he gone there?'

The news left former Liverpool forward Dean Saunders shocked, the Welshman suggesting that Salah could play at a higher level.



3

"Do you know what? I'm stunned. I'm stunned. What has Mo Salah done?" Saunders said on The Sports Bar.

"And this is no disrespect because I went to Galatasaray, Turkey. My son was born there and I had a great time in Turkey. And they're all really enthusiastic, nice people. And Trabzonspor is a big club in Turkey.

"But why on earth has Mo Salah left Liverpool to go there? I just, I mean, I can't, without sounding like I'm criticising Trabsonspor, I'm finding it hard to believe. Why didn't he stay at Liverpool?



"I honestly thought he was going to Saudi Arabia," Saunders added.

Salah can fire Trabzonspor to glory

Premier League fans may raise their eyebrows at Salah going to Trabzonspor but the former Chelsea player is set for a hero's welcome upon arrival to Turkey.

And Turkish football expert Ahmet Bob Turget believes Salah can inspire Trabzonspor to breaking the stranglehold the Istanbul clubs have on the league.

"I think probably Trabzonspor will be the biggest contender for the championship this season in the Turkish Super League," Turget told talkSPORT on Tuesday.

Salah is soon to call Manchester United goalkeeper Andre Onana a teammate with the goalkeeper joining on another loan this season.



Also in the Trabzonspor squad are ex-Manchester City defender Stefan Savic, ex-Southampton striker Paul Onuachu and former Premier League midfielder John Lundstram.

Another high profile player that could potentially move to Turkey is Marcus Rashford, with Fenerbahce said to be interested in him.

Sports.title: Man City interested in signing £54m Premier League star as Savinho pushes for Tottenham move
Sports.content:
Man City interested in signing £54m Premier League star as Savinho pushes for Tottenham move

Manchester City are interested in signing Chelsea winger Pedro Neto as a potential replacement for Tottenham target Savinho, talkSPORT understands.

Savinho has been tipped with a summer exit having struggled for game time at the Etihad Stadium last season.



3 Savinho could leave City this summer amidst renewed speculation surrounding a move to Spurs

3 And City may look to replace Savinho with Chelsea star Neto

Spurs are keen on the Brazilian and Liverpool's Cody Gakpo as they seek to bolster their attacking options.

Neto is also a rumoured target for Roberto De Zerbi's side, though their priority at this stage appears to be Savinho.



The north London outfit have been monitoring the former Girona man for the past 12 months and will hope to secure his services this summer.

And City are interested in Chelsea and Portugal star Neto should the 22-year-old leave the Etihad Stadium.



Neto and new City boss Enzo Maresca worked together during their time at Stamford Bridge.

The 26-year-old has started 54 league matches since his £54million arrival from Wolves in 2024.



In his two years in west London, Neto's been directly involved in 21 goals, scoring nine times.

However, the Portuguese forward may find minutes hard to come by under new Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso in the upcoming campaign.

Chelsea's failure to secure a European finish combined with the £117million addition of Morgan Rogers could see Neto restricted to a bit-part role.

3 Morgan Rogers' arrival could push Neto towards the Stamford Bridge exit Credit: Getty



Back of the Net-o

City may face competition for Neto should Chelsea sanction his summer sale.

Premier League rivals Liverpool have been linked with a move for Neto as the Reds consider their options in their quest to replace Mohamed Salah.

Salah confirmed he'll be leaving Liverpool at the end of the season earlier this year, though the Merseyside outfit are yet to sign a new right winger.

In addition, Serie A giants AC Milan are also believed to be keeping tabs on Neto with a view to a summer move.



Neto's compatriot Ruben Amorim took over as AC Milan boss back in June following Max Allegri's departure after the Italian side failed to secure a Champions League finish.

Sports.title: Manchester United player closes in on Middlesbrough transfer
Sports.content:
Middlesbrough are closing in on the permanent signing of Manchester United goalkeeper Radek Vitek, talkSPORT understands.

Vitek enjoyed a productive loan spell with Championship side Bristol City last season.



2 Vitek impressed during a loan spell with Championship side Bristol City last season Credit: Getty

The 22-year-old kept 12 clean sheets in England's second tier last term, the fifth most in the division as the Robins finished 12th.

Vitek is now close to a permanent switch to the Riverside Stadium to provide cover and competition for Sol Brynn.

The move to Boro brings the curtain down on a six-year spell at Old Trafford.



The Czech stopper joined the United academy from Sigma Olomouc in his homeland in 2020, though failed to make a single appearance for United.

Karl Darlow's arrival from Leeds United pushed Vitek further down the goalkeeping pecking order for Michael Carrick's men.



'I hope there is interest'

And the young goalkeeper admitted during pre-season that he is ready to leave United in search of regular action.

Speaking after a second-half appearance during United's 1-0 pre-season defeat to Wrexham in Helsinki, Vitek said: "I feel great and ready to go again somewhere to hopefully be number one.



"I hope there will be some interest. I think you will know when the things are more concrete."

When asked whether he'd hope for another loan or a permanent exit, he replied: "I'm ready for both to be fair.

2 Vitek has dropped down the Manchester United pecking order following Darlow's arrival Credit: Getty

"It depends on what the club wants and also depends on the options and, yeah, we'll see.



"There's been a few interests on the table, but we're hoping to get the best one and hopefully it will happen soon.

"I want to play every week and that's the goal for next season. Hopefully I find out soon where that's going to be."

Man Utd's summer business

Vitek will become the club's second high-profile sale of the summer after Rasmus Hojlund's loan move to Napoli was made permanent.

Casemiro left Old Trafford for MLS powerhouse Inter Miami, while Jadon Sancho and Tyrell Malacia departed after their respective contracts expired.



United have brought in Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans from Chelsea and Aston Villa, respectively, to ease Casemiro's exit.

Darlow, meanwhile, joined after his Leeds contract expired, and arrives as cover for first-choice shotstopper Senne Lammens.

Sports.title: Six Premier League clubs handed relegation warning with promoted teams for new season
Sports.content:
Six Premier League clubs handed relegation warning with promoted teams for new season

Premier League football returns this month and the relegation battle could be bigger than ever.

talkSPORT Breakfast hosts Jeff Stelling and Gabby Agbonlahor went through a list of teams that they believe could be contenders for the drop in the 2026/27 season.



8 Coventry and Ipswich will hope to avoid an immediate drop back to the Championship Credit: Getty

8 Hull will also be desperate to secure their status in the Premier League Credit: Getty

Coventry City, Ipswich Town and Hull City are the trio who earned promotion from the Championship to the top flight last season.

Typically, promoted sides find Premier League football too much to handle and head back down to the second tier a year later.



And even though Sunderland and Leeds United secured safety last season, Coventry, Ipswich and Hull will all be tipped to battle at the bottom end of the table.

But when discussing the fight against relegation, Stelling offered some hope for the Premier League newbies.



Who are talkSPORT's relegation candidates?

"The encouragement for all of those three promoted sides is there are going to be other candidates," he claimed, before hinting that Crystal Palace, Fulham, Sunderland and Brentford are at risk.

"Palace. New manager (Pierre Sage), they've sold (Maxence) Lacroix, no signings (other than Oscar Mingueza) through the door.



"Fulham. Unproven manager (Alvaro Arbeloa), they've lost (Raul) Jimenez, (Harry) Wilson, (Issa) Diop, (Samuel) Chukwueze.

"Sunderland. Brilliant season last season, can they cope with that second season syndrome, plus Europe?

"Brentford. Just because they're Brentford, to be brutally honest."

Agbonlahor then explained: "I think Fulham is one that scares me. If I'm a Fulham fan, I look at Marco Silva, he got that extra percentage from all those players.

8 Stelling and Agbonlahor are unsure about the future of Palace under Sage Credit: Getty



8 Fulham are another club to be tipped for a potential relegation battle Credit: Getty

8 Sunderland could find it hard to juggle Europa League and Premier League football Credit: Getty

"Like you said, Jimenez, Wilson, Diop, Chukwueze gone as well. New manager, what has he really done? Struggled when he came in at Real Madrid.

"He's signed two players, (Gonzalo) Garcia and (Cesar) Palacios. Garcia got six goals in 30 appearances last season in LaLiga. Palacios, five appearances, zero goals. A combined fee of £42million for both of them.



"LaLiga is different to the Premier League, it's going to be really tough for those players, we'll see how they get on with a physical league like the Premier League.

"New manager as well, a lot of the unknown with Arbeloa, so you can see it, they might struggle."

"You can say the same about Bournemouth, can't you?" Stelling said. "New manager (Marco Rose) there, and I mentioned Sunderland have got European football, but so have Bournemouth.

"Over the last couple of seasons, so many have left and this time round they've lost (Marcos) Senesi, (Eli Junior) Kroupi is out for a while, they may yet lose Alex Scott because there'll be so many admirers for him. You wonder how they will cope with all of that."



8 According to Stelling, Brentford are candidates - simply because they're Brentford Credit: Getty

8 Bournemouth are also at risk of going back down to the Championship Credit: Getty

"European football, a couple of injuries, and the squad is starting to look thin," Agbonlahor added. "You've got a game on Thursday and you travel back, and you've got a tough game on the Sunday.

"Sometimes, European football can be a bad thing. It was Burnley, wasn't it? They struggled with European football (Europa League) and the Premier League (in the 2018/29 season)."



Stelling then asked: "How do you think Newcastle are going to do?"

"I think they'll be down there," Agbonlahor claimed. "I don't see them having a season as bad as Tottenham over the last two seasons, but I don't see them in the top half, nowhere near.

"I feel that, that fanbase are angry, they're angry at what's happening with their football club. They're angry at losing all of their players, signing young players...

"They were all dressed in Saudi Arabian attire when the owners came in. They were thinking, 'Yes, we're going to go for (Kylian) Mbappe, we're going to get Neymar, we're going to get all these big players'.

"Now, there's no European football this season, just lost their manager. They've brought in a manager (Matthias Jaissle) who's managed in the Saudi league.



"It could start to turn a bit toxic there, if they start to lose a few of their early games. Joelinton's wanting to get out as well, this isn't what Newcastle fans thought was going to happen, did they?"

8 Agbonlahor believes Newcastle could become toxic in the new season Credit: Getty

"Let's not forget, as much as the problems with the Financial Fair Play rules and they've lost this player, that player, they didn't buy well last summer," he added.

"(Nick) Woltemade, (Yoane) Wissa, (Anthony) Elanga, over £160million for those three players, none of them produced last season. They've got to step up, all three of them, because Wissa looked very sharp for DR Congo at the World Cup, can he bring that form into next season?



"Jacob Ramsey is probably the only one who had a decent season last season, so those three signings have to step up."

Stelling then wanted to poke fun at Tottenham Hotspur, who finished 17th in the past two seasons to narrowly avoid relegation.

"Of course, we're talking about relegation. Well, you can never leave Spurs out of the equation, can you?"

However, to avoid the potential wrath from Spurs fans, he insisted: "I'm only joking!"



The 2026/27 Premier League season gets underway on Friday, August 21 when Arsenal host Coventry, live on talkSPORT.

Sports.title: Nottingham Forest explore shock move for Man City star as Lucas Bergvall alternative
Sports.content:
Nottingham Forest are interested in Manchester City midfielder Tijjani Reijnders, talkSPORT understands.

Forest are out to strengthen in the middle of the park following Elliot Anderson's club-record £116million move to City last month.



2 Reijnders struggled for minutes in the second half of last season Credit: Getty

And they are considering a move for Reijnders as they look to add bodies in the middle of the park.

The Dutchman only joined the Manchester giants from Italian side AC Milan last year.
