Reijnders enjoyed a promising start to life at the Etihad Stadium, scoring once and assisting another in a 4-0 win against Wolves on his Premier League debut.



However, the 28-year-old's game time dipped in the second half of the season as he made just two league starts between the start of February and the end of the campaign.

Despite the departure of Bernardo Silva and potential exit of Real Madrid target Rodri, City could be open to selling Reijnders as a result of the capture of Anderson and impending arrival of Ayyoub Bouaddi.



Even so, the Netherlands international joined the first-team squad for their pre-season tour of Asia.

Latest on Bergvall

Interest in Reijnders comes with Forest exploring other options to Tottenham Hotspur midfielder Lucas Bergvall.



talkSPORT understands that Bergvall had informed Spurs chiefs of his desire to leave the club this summer in pursuit of regular action.

2 Forest have cooled their interest in Spurs midfielder Lucas Bergvall

The Tricky Trees have seen at least one bid worth £38million rebuffed with the north London side keen to retain the 20-year-old Swede's services.

During the club's pre-season tour of New Zealand and Australia, head coach Roberto De Zerbi admitted that he made mistakes with how he handled Bergvall in the final knockings of the 2025/26 season.



Spurs beat the drop on the final day of the campaign and while the capital outfit are keen to retain the midfielder's services, the Italian reiterated that he will not stand in the way of players that wish to leave.

"I'm always being very clear with him and with you. I would like that he stays with us," De Zerbi said when asked about Bergvall's future.

"I think he's potentially a top, top, top player. But then I don't want to convince anyone to stay.

"Tottenham is already, without me, a top club and we are not to convince anyone to stay.



"He can find the space if he stays with us. The competition within the players will be very strong because we are Tottenham and we have to build a strong squad - not just 11 players - especially considering a lot of injuries we suffered in the last two, three seasons.

"Football is going in a clear direction – to compete for the highest places in the table, you have to manage 22, 23, 24 players. I don't want 24, but 21, 22 of a high level."

Spurs have strengthened their midfield with the additions of Mateus Fernandes and Sandro Tonali, the duo replacing the outgoing Joao Palhinha and Yves Bissouma.

And with no European football on offer in north London this season, Bergvall may find playing time hard to come by.

Sports.title: US cities chasing FIFA for millions in ‘unpaid’ contributions in fresh blow to Gianni Infantino
Sports.content:
Host cities were 'repeatedly assured' by FIFA of legacy contributions, but millions of dollars remain unpaid

US cities chasing FIFA for millions in ‘unpaid’ contributions in fresh blow to Gianni Infantino

World Cup host cities across the United States are chasing FIFA for 'millions of dollars' they believe they were promised for the 2026 tournament.

Gianni Infantino announced last year that football's governing body would make a contribution of $1 million to each of the 11 cities that were hosting matches during the Club World Cup competition.



3 World Cup host cities are chasing FIFA over unpaid contributions Credit: AFP

That money was described as a 'legacy contribution' -- with funds to be used to build mini-pitches, and support 'social projects' in each area.

After Infantino’s initial announcement, the American cities scheduled to host World Cup games in 2026 asked if they would receive the same contribution for the more substantial task of hosting multiple games across the international tournament.

The Athletic reports that FIFA management 'repeatedly assured' that cities would receive the same $1m contribution towards legacy, despite no public statement.



Executives told the outlet that the promise was made 'verbally' by members of senior management, and 'reiterated' in meetings.

However, that money has not been paid, and several cities are now asking FIFA staff for updates on the payments.



World Cup games were hosted in Atlanta, Boston, Dallas, Houston, Kansas City, Los Angeles, New York and New Jersey, Miami, Philadelphia, San Francisco and Seattle across 39 days this summer.

Two of those host cities told The Athletic that it has been 'difficult to understand' why FIFA would be stalling or non-committal on what are described as 'relatively minor' payments, given the organization celebrated revenues in excess of $15 billion between 2023 and 2026, and had an operating budget of around $2.7bn for the 2026 tournament.



"The challenge is exacerbated for the cities as some of the host committees are now winding up operations following the tournament, meaning it is not easy to work out the vehicle which would now be best placed to benefit from the payments," the report read.

"Others are seeking to draw up financial reports to their jurisdictions and authorities but do not have certainty over whether to include the payments."

Unpaid payments add another layer of controversy for FIFA and its embattled president in the wake of the World Cup.

3 News of FIFA's unpaid contributions is a fresh blow for embattled Infantino Credit: AFP



Infantino is already facing a rebellion over his plans to sell off stakes in competitions to private investors, which have been scrapped.

In recent days, opponents of the president are threatening 'non co-operation' with the body unless he steps down.

How much did US cities pay to host the World Cup?

While the World Cup boosted tourism across the US this summer, host city committees were tasked with organising security, transport, fan events beyond each game day.

The Financial Times reported last month that New York and New Jersey predicted around $3.3bn of economic activity would be generated, while California’s Bay Area hoped the combined impact of football games, as well as last year’s NBA All-Star Game and February's Super Bowl LX, would be $1.4bn.



However, doubts have since been raised over the economic windfall for each city.

American taxpayers contributed hugely to the costs of the 2026 tournament, with the Kansas City host committee revealing to The Athletic that it received a total public investment of $86.8m.

3 Kansas City's host committee has revealed the cost of hosting World Cup games Credit: Getty

Nearly $75m more was also handed out in federal security assistance and in federal grants for transportation.



Private donations, which remain undisclosed, were also received

A $1m legacy contribution for each host city would appear a drop in the water compared to those massive numbers, but remains an incentive yet to be paid.

Sports.title: Iconic WWE Hall of Fame wrestler dead at 85 as tributes pour in
Sports.content:
WWE Hall of Famer Dory Funk Jr has died at the age of 85, prompting a wave of tributes across the professional wrestling community.

Triple H announced Funk's passing on Tuesday, honoring the legend's in-ring style and the impact he made on the industry during his decades-long career.

'From the Double Cross Ranch to the WWE Hall of Fame, Dory's style inspired countless performers in our industry,' Triple H wrote in a tribute on social media.

'Whether it was at WrestleMania 2, WCW, ECW, or the dozens of NWA-affiliated promotions, his travels across North America and Asia were a part of the early blueprint that helped build this business into a global phenomenon.'

Funk began his professional wrestling career in 1963 and reached the pinnacle of the sport in 1969 when he captured the NWA World Heavyweight Championship.

He held the title for over four years, marking the second-longest uninterrupted reign in the belt's history.

WWE Hall of Famer Dory Funk Jr. has died at the age of 85

Funk began his professional wrestling career in 1963 and reached the pinnacle of the sport in 1969 when he captured the NWA World Heavyweight Championship

Alongside his younger brother, Terry Funk, who passed away in August 2023 at age 79, Dory made history as part of the only pair of siblings to both hold the NWA World Heavyweight Championship.

The duo wrestled together worldwide, including a notable tag-team appearance at WrestleMania 2, before being inducted together into the WWE Hall of Fame in 2009.

Beyond his accomplishments in the ring, Funk was instrumental in shaping the next generation of sports entertainment stars, spending decades training future legends such as Kurt Angle, Edge, Christian Cage and the Hardy Boyz.

'A hard-nosed and fierce competitor, his rugged in-ring style was only eclipsed by the decades he spent training athletes to perform in the squared circle he loved so much,' Triple H added.

'My thoughts and those of the entire WWE Universe are with his loved ones during this difficult time.'

Sports.title: Inside Jadon Sancho's fall from grace to 10th-tier Flixton: Who wants Man United exile and why he's still a free agent, how his career in England really unravelled and what United sources say about his 'bad boy' reputation
Sports.content:
Inside Jadon Sancho's fall from grace to 10th-tier Flixton: Who wants Man United exile and why he's still a free agent, how his career in England really unravelled and what United sources say about his 'bad boy' reputation

Unlock more from our team inside the Man United camp with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight, analysis and more

The sadness in the Jadon Sancho story is that he has succumbed to the very thing he warned against.

As a fresh-faced teenager, Sancho sat down for an interview on Borussia Dortmund’s YouTube channel in which he showed maturity beyond his years by highlighting the pitfalls of being a young superstar.

‘I’ve seen a lot of young talents disappear because it’s come too early and it’s got to their heads,’ he said in that 2019 chat, which now looks prophetic as he trains at an amateur football club as the most high-profile free agent in the game today.

‘My family have seen this. Luckily enough I’ve got great people around me to keep me grounded and humble and they tell me what I’m doing is not enough.’

People have a lot to say when it comes to Sancho. There are certainly a great many people on social media who take pleasure in goading, mocking and ridiculing him at every turn. Each and every indiscretion is, weirdly, celebrated.

Others, who have worked with him and insist the bad-boy public perception is far detached from the quiet, introverted reality, are pained by how the past eight years have played out.

Jadon Sancho (pictured with Flixton boss Alex Mortimer) has been using the 10th-tier side's facilities in Manchester

It's a sign of the times for former wonderkid Sancho, who left Man United in the summer after a disappointing five years at the club

The fact Flixton FC, a 10th-division team in Greater Manchester, felt it necessary to qualify that no, they had not taken Sancho on trial in recent days, underlined the absurdity of a career that once promised so much, but has now taken too many wrong turns.

‘To clarify, Jadon was not on trial with the club and was not involved in any transfer discussions,’ Flixton posted on Instagram.

‘He simply used our facilities for a private training session to maintain his fitness while preparing for the next chapter of his career.’

There are agreements in principle, we’re told, with a number of clubs across Saudi Arabia and the Middle East, while clubs in Europe, with Turkey one potential landing spot, also paying close attention. It is Sancho who is taking his time to choose his next destination.

But the days of Real Madrid, of Paris Saint-Germain, and the game’s elite fighting among themselves to catch Sancho’s eye are long gone. For that fresh-faced teenager that had the world at his feet, it really wasn’t meant to go like this.

During Sancho's first spell at Borussia Dortmund, the club he joined after turning his back on Pep Guardiola and Manchester City, it felt like his potential was limitless.

‘An 18-year-old scaring the life out of seasoned Premier League players. I love it,’ Rio Ferdinand, then working as a pundit for BT Sport, gushed after a game against Tottenham Hotspur at Wembley. ‘I think he’ll be the best English player in the coming years.’

Nobody was mocking Sancho or Ferdinand back then. It was not absurd to see the teenage winger as a potential Ballon d'Or winner.

But there were also the first signs of problems ahead. First when Sancho was dropped and fined for returning late from England duty ahead of a match against Borussia Monchengladbach in October 2019.

A fortnight later he was hooked after 36 minutes against Bayern Munich by boss Lucien Favre, who later said it was because Sancho was ‘not good enough’. Privately, Sancho and his camp felt he was being hung out to dry.

Sancho and his camp felt hung out to dry after then Borussia Dortmund boss Lucien Favre hooked him after 36 minutes of a game against Bayern Munich

Figures in Germany have remained fiercely defensive of Sancho but time-keeping became an area of concern.

In 2018, Phil Foden and Sancho were dropped for an England Under 19s win over Latvia after turning up late to a training session.

Nemanja Matic, a former team-mate of Sancho’s at Manchester United, named and shamed him as a time-keeping offender three years ago.

‘Among the players who would always be late were Paul Pogba and Jadon Sancho,' Matic told Austrian media outlet YU Planet. 'The rest of us who were always on time were angry, so we decided to form a kind of internal disciplinary committee with me serving as its president.

‘I put a sheet of paper up on the wall where I documented the names of individuals arriving late. During one particular season we collected around £75,000 in fines.’

Sancho's time-keeping issues are said to have been ironed out in recent years. But back to the early days at Dortmund, when he was a young, dazzling talent with the world’s biggest clubs queueing up to get him.

Manchester United pursued him relentlessly for two years as their great hope for their troubled right wing position before finally sealing a £73million move.

‘I always knew that I would return to England one day,’ said Sancho, who signed a five-year deal at Old Trafford at the age of 21. 'The chance to join Manchester United is a dream come true and I just cannot wait to perform in the Premier League.’

Sancho described his move to United as a 'dream come true' - but in reality it was a nightmare

Only what followed was not a dream, but a nightmare. A nightmare that started when he was hospitalised with an ear infection; then saw Ole Gunnar Solskjaer, the man who signed him and planned to build around him, sacked before Sancho had even scored.

Soon a no-nonsense disciplinarian in Erik ten Hag was calling him out publicly before sending him into exile, where he no longer had access to the first team canteen and was eating out a plastic container and training with academy players.

Then came a loan spell at Chelsea that saw the Blues pay a £5million penalty fee to avoid signing him permanently, another loan at Aston Villa that saw Villa pass up on a permanent move as they instead signed Alejandro Garnacho, and the end of his United career as he walked walking away for nothing.

We will never truly know how things would have gone had Sancho and Ten Hag never crossed paths.

Those inside United speak of a complete mismatch of personalities. Sancho is an introverted character - Daily Mail Sport spoke to him in Dortmund following a man-of-the-match performance against PSV Eindhoven where he was polite, cordial and a far cry from the problem child some desperately want him to be.

With that introversion comes a need for an arm-round-the-shoulder manager, rather than the coolness with which Ten Hag operated. An argument can be made that Ten Hag was the worst type of manager for Sancho and Sancho the worst type of player for Ten Hag.

Sancho made 41 appearances in his first full season under Ten Hag before he took time away from the first team in December 2022 after his manager cited 'physical and mental' factors, a move which privately was not welcomed by those close to the player. Pointing to mental health was clumsy from the manager.

By way of reparations, Ten Hag had arranged for Sancho, during a three-month break away from United, to train at the home of Dutch amateur side OJC Rosmalen, where three coaches, picked out by Ten Hag due to specialising in mental health, technical training and fitness, worked to restore Sancho to peak performance.

But then came the rift that Sancho’s career has, truthfully, never fully recovered from.

Former United boss Erik ten Hag (right) was a terrible personality match with Sancho

In September 2023, Ten Hag omitted Sancho from a 3-1 defeat at Arsenal due to, in his opinion, a lack of effort in training.

‘On his performance in training, we didn’t select him,’ Ten Hag said afterwards. ‘You have to reach the level every day at Manchester United.’

It was typically blunt from Ten Hag but nothing that he hadn’t communicated privately. Sancho disagreed that his effort, having been tasked with acting as an 'Arsenal' player in training alongside his fellow team-mates outside of Ten Hag's starting XI, was any worse than that of his peers.

So, with the help of those around him, Sancho hit post on an infamous, but now-deleted, social media jab at his manager. His Manchester United career would never be the same again.

‘Please don't believe everything you read,’ the statement read. ‘I will not allow people saying things that is (sic) completely untrue, I have conducted myself very well in training this week. I believe there are other reasons for this matter that I won't go into, I've been a scapegoat for a long time which isn't fair!'

Ten Hag was furious and figures at United found themselves caught in the crossfire of trying to repair a relationship that many, including players, desperately wanted to see resolved.

Ten Hag demanded an apology that never came. On Sancho’s side, there was a feeling that he was being singled out where others were never handed the same punishment.

So he trained alone with academy players, many of whom, off the record, praised his personality and candour, while he was not allowed into senior facilities. He got changed alone, and ate out of black lunch-boxes as he wasn't allowed into the first team canteen. It was unprecedented treatment that will never be seen again having since been outlawed by FIFA and FIFPro.

It's only two years since Sancho was playing in a Champions League final at Wembley for Borussia Dortmund

By the time he was back at United with Amorim in the hotseat, the ‘bomb squad’ had more members in it and Sancho and Co were restricted to turning up after 5pm when the first team had gone home. It was all manufactured to maximise humiliation.

At Chelsea, which followed a second loan spell at Dortmund where he was lauded as a homecoming hero, Sancho was a popular figure.

He was back home in London, settled into the dressing room, and had a major ally in Blues recruitment chief Joe Shields, who vouched for Sancho’s character after working with him at Manchester City.

A key part of the pitch from then Chelsea boss Enzo Maresca was about platforming Sancho’s game in Maresca’s wing-dominant system, which was reliant on wide players winning their one-v-one battles.

While that would later become a bone of contention - Maresca found Sancho's output frustrating in the one-v-one department - Chelsea sources remain insistent that they were still working to acquire him permanently.

He scored as Chelsea beat Real Betis in the Conference League final, and while the loan wasn’t flawless - some Chelsea sources recalled how Sancho would, on occasion, complain about team-mates not passing him the ball - it felt a good fit for club and player.

Chelsea and Sancho seemed a good fit during his loan there in 2024-25 - but the Blues opted against signing him permanently

Chelsea were covering around half of his £250,000-a-week wages during the loan but when it came to a permanent arrangement, they were seeking a drastically reduced salary, which saw the move break down and the Blues enact a £5million penalty clause to escape their £25million obligation to buy.

Then came the next roll of the dice, the late loan swoop from Aston Villa in a regrettable transfer window that would go on to cost Monchi, their then sporting director, his job in the Midlands.

Sancho was never Unai Emery’s go-to man and while the Spaniard did warm to Sancho towards the end - he loves rejuvenating high-calibre players - it always remained a remote prospect that this would be anything more than a temporary arrangement.

Insiders insist there were no issues with his attitude or performance in training, and Sancho didn’t allow his career to be derailed by a humiliating substitution after coming off the bench against Manchester City in October 2025.

Time-keeping was no longer the issue with Sancho. Now criticism came on his ability to change a game. Since signing for United, Sancho, who has never shown blistering pace, hasn’t hit 10 goals and assists in a single league season. A staggering statistic for a player who scored 50 goals and managed 64 assists in 137 games across four seasons in Germany.

At 20, Sancho was the ‘best young player on the planet bar none,’ Ferdinand claimed, and many other pundits were ready to back that up.

At 26, Sancho has played for Manchester United, Chelsea and Aston Villa, gone back to Borussia Dortmund, and is now weighing up what the future holds, and whether that future is to be played out in the Middle East.

There will be finger-pointing on all sides and the blame-game, in truth, should be split across the board. There should be no joy in the Sancho story, only sadness. It wasn’t meant to go like this.

Sports.title: WWE legend Brock Lesnar, 49, announces retirement as SummerSlam loss marks end of 26-year career
Sports.content:
See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

WWE legend Brock Lesnar has called time on his 26-year career in the business following his defeat to Oba Femi at SummerSlam at the weekend.

Lesnar, a wrestling great and former MMA star, made the announcement during an appearance on ESPN's The Pat McAfee Show on Tuesday.

Following his Hell in a Cell loss to Femi at SummerSlam in Minneapolis, the 10-time WWE champion confirmed the time has finally come for him to bow out.

'I’m here today to let the world know that I am retired and I wanted to say a big thank you to everybody,' he told WWE commentator McAfee and his co-host AJ Hawk. 'Saturday was a very emotional day for me.'

Lesnar, 49, has retired from wrestling and returned in the past, while he appeared to suggest the end was coming after leaving his gloves and boots in the center of the ring in an emotional moment after his WrestleMania 42 match against Femi earlier this year.

Yet despite having enough left to compete again at SummerSlam, he insists that defeat in Minneapolis will go down as his last in the business.

WWE icon Brock Lesnar has announced he is calling time on his 26-year career in the business

Lesnar, a 10-time WWE champion, made the announcement on ESPN's The Pat McAfee Show

'I still had some fuel in the tank, but Saturday for Brock Lesnar, that's it. That's it for me in the squared circle and for everything else too,' Lesnar added.

'So I just wanted to give a shout-out to everybody in this universe that has followed me since I was a little kid, all the way till Saturday.'

Lesnar began life with the WWE back in 2002, following a successful college wrestling career that saw him a two-time NJCAA All-American and accrue a staggering 106-5 record over four years.

After signing with the wrestling promotion, he worked his way into the main roster and eventually became one of the biggest stars in the organization.

However, his first stint in the WWE would come to an end in 2004. Following a defeat at WrestleMania XX, he cited burnout, injuries and creative dissatisfaction as his reasons for walking away.

Lesnar returned to the promotion in 2012 and earned a number of WWE championship titles before seemingly retiring at WrestleMania 36.

That decision, however, was short-lived and he returned to the ring in 2021 rocking a new 'cowboy' look that featured a beard and ponytail.

The wrestling great has opted to bow out following his loss to Oba Femi at SummerSlam

In 2023, Lesnar was named in a bombshell sex trafficking lawsuit against WWE co-founder Vince McMahon, filed by his former employee Janel Grant.

As a result of the lawsuit, he was removed from the WWE roster and wiped from their event plans. He would endure a two-year exile from the organization.

He returned at Summer Slam in August 2025, despite the Grant lawsuit remaining active at the time. He took part in a handful of fights between then and Sunday night, before officially retiring from the sport a year later.

Though he's best-known for his time in the squared circle, Lesnar also found success away from wrestling. After leaving WWE for the first time in 2004, he attempted to embark on a professional football career.

Lesnar participated in the NFL Scouting Combine at the time but later suffered a broken jaw and hand from a motorcycle accident which put his progress on hold.

Despite the injuries, a number of NFL teams still held an interest in Lesnar and, in July 2004, he signed with the Minnesota Vikings as a defensive tackle. However, his time with the franchise was short-lived and he was eventually released in August.

After his dreams of being on the gridiron came crashing down, he then decided to try his hand - literally - at mixed martial arts.

Lesnar also enjoyed success as an MMA star over the course of his extraordinary career

He began fighting for a promotion known as 'K-1', in April 2006, and won his first bout via submission in the first round - bring global attention to his MMA skills.

Lesnar would eventually sign with Dana White's UFC in 2008, which proved to be a massive success for the organization given his national star power.

Despite losing his first fight, UFC chief White stuck by Lesnar and offered him a multi-fight deal. Again, this proved to a wise call as Lesnar would later become the UFC heavyweight champion following a win over Randy Couture in November 2008.

In total, he had eight UFC fights, winning four of them and losing three - with the final bout being ruled as a no-contest after he tested positive for clomiphene.

Sports.title: NFL star is removed from practice after throwing a punch just weeks after landing $105m contract
Sports.content:
Tennessee Titans star Jeffery Simmons was ejected from practice on Tuesday after throwing a punch early in a team drill.

As a result of the violent scenes, the All-Pro defensive tackle was forced to spend the rest of practice working on a side field with a strength coach.

First-year head coach Robert Saleh stopped practice after the incident, pulling his Titans together on the field for a reminder to spend the second session in pads working and not fighting.

'Our policy is if you throw a punch you're ejected in the game, same thing with practice,' Saleh said.

'If you throw punch, you're out of practice. But rather than going to the locker room, he went to the other field. He still got his work in. So the projected reps and the work that he would have gotten, he got in off to the side.'

Simmons, who got a very big extension in late June, also had a brief tussle Monday in the Titans' first day in pads.

Tennessee Titans star Jeffery Simmons was ejected from practice after throwing a punch

Simmons, who got a big extension in June, also had a brief tussle during Monday's practice

Robert Saleh stopped practice and sent his defensive star to practice on his own in Nashville

On Tuesday, Simmons and center Austin Schlottman scuffled after a play before he swung at right tackle JC Latham. Assistant defensive line coach Tanzel Smart grabbed Simmons and took him down out of the scrum.

The Titans went 3-14 last season, and too many penalties for 1,011 yards didn't help.

Latham had the most with 14 penalties, including eight that stalled drives. Simmons ranked second with 12.

Saleh said he wants both lines playing with an edge up to toeing the line.

'We're always going to toe a line of being aggressive and call it instigating if you want,' Saleh said.

'It's just the nature of who we're going to be. But we've got to be disciplined enough to make sure that we always find our way back to the huddle without giving the other team freebies.'

In another concerning moment, left tackle Dan Moore Jr. walked off the field with a trainer.

Saleh had no immediate update after practice. Moore was one of the Titans' big free agent signees in 2025 and a key player for a line already looking for new starters at center and right guard.

Titans quarterback Cam Ward gave fans the play they had been hoping to see late in practice when he threw deep with Carnell Tate, the fourth overall draft pick, running under the ball in the end zone for a 65-yard touchdown.

Sports.title: Mohamed Salah closes in on Turkey move: Trabzonspor confirm talks with former Liverpool star who will fly in TODAY ahead of signing a two-year contract
Sports.content:
Trabzonspor are closing in on a two-year deal with former Liverpool forward Mo Salah.

The Turkish club's rivals Besiktas were understood to be the Egyptian's first choice but talks with them stalled last week.

On Tuesday night, Trabzonspor shared a brief message with their 1.9million followers on X, with the club writing: 'Public Announcement: Negotiations have begun regarding the transfer of professional footballer Mohamed Salah to our Club.'

The club then posted: 'Professional footballer Mohamed Salah, with whom we have begun transfer negotiations, will be at Istanbul Atatürk Airport General Aviation Terminal at 12:00 on Wednesday, August 5.

'The player is scheduled to arrive in Trabzon on the same day in the evening hours.

'The time and other details regarding the welcome program in Trabzon will be shared with the public through our club's official communication channels during the day.'

Mohammed Salah is closing in on a move to Trabzonspor in Turkey

Trabzonspor also shared a 17-second AI video of a camera shot panning from pyramids over mountains to a view of their 41,000-seater stadium Papara Park.

Salah's future has been the subject of huge interest since the surprising decision was announced back in March that he would leave Liverpool one year into his two-year contract extension.

Many anticipated that Saudi Arabia would be the most likely destination after Al-Ittihad made a £150million bid in summer 2023.

But Trabzonspor are now set to sign the winger, who fell out with Arne Slot at Anfield last term.

The Turkish side finished third last season behind Fenerbahce and champions Galatasaray.

Salah, who is the third-highest goalscorer in Reds history with 255, did not engage in talks with teams before the end of the season out of respect to the Merseyside club.

His long-serving agent, Ramy Abbas, repeatedly insisted nothing had been decided and reaffirmed that stance during the World Cup.

But since returning from the competition in the US, talks have accelerated with interested parties.

Salah, pictured returning to Egypt after the World Cup, looks set to sign a two-year deal

Salah is renowned for his remarkable professionalism and will back himself to remain at a high level deep into his thirties.

Salah was the star man as Slot’s side won the Premier League in Slot's first season, the Egyptian's second English title, but his level dipped last term with just 10 goals last term compared to a staggering 34 when he spear-headed the 2024-25 title win.

Liverpool are yet to replace the player who was voted Professional Footballers' Association (PFA) Players' Player of the Year three times at the club.

With the start of the season fast approaching, Bradley Barcola of PSG remains the most likely high-profile attacking signing.

But the 23-year-old, valued at £145million by his club, plays predominantly on the left and Jamie Carragher recently warned against buying him as a replacement for Salah.

Salah would be the most high-profile signing in Trabzonspor's history and if his expected move is confirmed, will join Man United loanee Andre Onana.

Ex-Man City defender Stefan Savic also plays for the Turkish side, who have won their domestic title seven times.

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino chairs crisis talks with FIFA staff in Morocco as pressure mounts on embattled president after being accused of BLACKMAIL by head of Jordan FA
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino chairs crisis talks with FIFA staff in Morocco as pressure mounts on embattled president after being accused of BLACKMAIL by head of Jordan FA

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Gianni Infantino has summoned senior FIFA officials to a hotel in Morocco for crisis talks as pressure continues to mount on the FIFA president.

It comes after Jordan FA president Prince Ali bin Hussein accused him of blackmail.

Infantino has come under intense scrutiny since plans to sell £3.1billion in World Cup stakes leaked last week.

The Swiss football administrator has since scrapped the proposals after widespread opposition – including an internal rebellion at FIFA.

UEFA and CONCACAF – the body for North and Central America and the Caribbean – are both calling for Infantino to step down, with Europe declaring a lack of confidence in the FIFA president.

Jordan, meanwhile, are the first Asian nation to rebel against Infantino – taking the total to 91, assuming all UEFA and CONCACAF nations follow the stance set by their continental bodies. 106 nations are needed to depose Infantino as president.

In a statement Hussein ripped into Infantino, accusing him of delaying prize money payments and refusing to address the problem unless Jordan endorsed him for a fourth term at the helm of world football.

Gianni Infantino has summoned senior FIFA officials to a hotel in Morocco for crisis talks

Infantino has been accused of blackmail by Jordan FA president Prince Ali bin Hussein

‘There is no shortage of issues regarding FIFA. Let me start by clarifying what some of these are from an FA perspective, in particular that of Jordan going into a World Cup for the first time,’ Hussein said.

‘We are a small country with a minimal budget for our FA and had to deal with enormous hurdles.

‘First, getting our fans into the USA: not all were granted visas, even though they had tickets - which we also know were sold at exorbitant prices.

‘Secondly, we are being taxed by the US government through FIFA for our participation. Money that should go to players and staff.

‘This was not the case for those who played and set up camp in Canada and Mexico. But we happened to be in the USA so now we face these huge costs in taxes for having participated.

‘Thirdly we have been waiting for reward money for our players since December for the Arab Cup in Qatar, which is a FIFA event.

‘The money our team should receive for having reached the final has not been delivered yet, while at the same time FIFA brags about how many billions they have in reserve.

‘It is clear the problem really is with leadership. For months, FIFA has been refusing to help us on any of these or other matters - until it was verbally communicated to me during the World Cup that if I endorsed Infantino it would go a long way to helping our FA out.

‘We pride ourselves in Jordan in upholding ethical values. We did not endorse him before and certainly will not now.

‘But the whole situation amounts to blackmail and we refuse to give in to that.’

Daily Mail Sport have contacted FIFA for comment.

Sports.title: Jack Draper breaks down in tears as Brit loses on return from injury at Canadian Open
Sports.content:
Jack Draper breaks down in tears as Brit loses on return from injury at Canadian Open

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Jack Draper's torturous attempts to return to tennis continued as he wiped away tears during defeat in the first round of the Canadian Open.

Trailing Frenchman Terence Atmane 4-1 in the deciding set, the British former world No4 sat in his chair at the changeover and wept.

It was a truly wretched sight and, while we must wait for the man himself to speak, it seems likely those tears were an indication that he is still feeling the pain of an arm injury which simply will not leave him alone.

Some natural ring-rust aside, there was nothing much wrong with Draper’s level in the first two sets, and when he won the second comfortably he looked well placed to take the match. But his serve began to subside dramatically and by the end he could do little more than just roll it over. The 24-year-old also, in apparent desperation, started to hit an increasing number of dropshots.

Atmane, in terrible form himself, won 6-3, 2-6, 6-2.

It has been well over 12 months now that Draper has struggled with bone bruising in the humerus of his left arm.

Jack Draper was in tears during the third set of his game against Terence Atmane in Montreal as he continues his return from injury 🎾 pic.twitter.com/ekhBse3Af3 — Sky Sports Tennis (@SkySportsTennis) August 4, 2026

Jack Draper was reduced to tears as he lost his comeback match following time out with injury

The British former world No 4 sat in his chair at the changeover and wept in the final set

Due to play at Wimbledon, he pulled out the day before his match. Set to return in Washington, he withdrew citing a twinge in that arm.

The injury is clearly chronic and, if this is indeed yet another setback, it is not easy to see where Draper goes from here.

Draper said earlier this week: 'It's important for people to recognise that the injury I have is very complex, it's very complicated and everyone around me is doing everything we can to help this keep moving along.

'It's not as simple as 'rest and heal up and you'll come back and you'll be fine'.

Terribly sad to say, it is becoming increasingly likely we may never see the best of this beautifully, brutally brilliant player again.

Sports.title: Liverpool consider move for 18-year-old PSG winger Ibrahim Mbaye - as well as his team-mate Bradley Barcola
Sports.content:
Liverpool consider move for 18-year-old PSG winger Ibrahim Mbaye - as well as his team-mate Bradley Barcola

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Liverpool are assessing whether to make an approach for PSG winger Ibrahim Mbaye - as well as his teammate Bradley Barcola.

Mbaye is an 18-year-old right winger who starred for Senegal at the World Cup.

Liverpool have been among the clubs made aware of the teenager's availability earlier in the window, but Manchester City and Tottenham were understood to have shown greater interest.

However, it is Bundesliga side Bayer Leverkusen who have been making the greater progress.

Now with concerns about the squad’s capability and lack of goal-power, Liverpool are considering an approach for both PSG flyers.

Mbaye would at least be a more natural fit to replace Mo Salah who left Anfield and is closing on a move to Trabzonspor while Barcola prefers the left.

Ibrahim Mbaye, pictured in action for Senegal at the World Cup, is an option for Liverpool

Much will depend on the asking price as PSG would likely ask for over £150m.

The situation is expected to become clearer in the coming days as the clubs maintain dialogue.

Mbaye is represented by agent Jorge Mendes.

The 6ft 1in winger has been at PSG since 2018 and made 33 appearances for the senior side, scoring four times.

He represented France at youth level before pledging his international allegiance to Senegal in 2025.

Mbaye was a bright light for his country at the World Cup in the US and became the youngest African scorer in tournament history when he netted a consolation against France.

Liverpool are looking to bolster their attacking ranks, though Cody Gakpo has emerged as a target for Tottenham.

But the club have no plans to sell the Dutch international Gakpo despite the north London side making their interest known.

Gakpo, 27, is contracted until 2030 and with current market prices escalating for players of his experience, it would take a huge sum to change Liverpool's stance.

The Dutchman had a weaker season than usual last time out, scoring only nine goals, but is highly valued by Liverpool all the same. His best season, 2024-25, saw him bang in 18 goals.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick's dream Marcus Rashford replacement as Man Utd sign £60million star
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick's dream Marcus Rashford replacement as Man Utd sign £60million star

Michael Carrick could go for an unorthodox approach in replacing Marcus Rashford at Manchester United

View 3 Images Marcus Rashford remains a Manchester United player - for now (Image: Getty)

The future of Marcus Rashford has once again been reignited. The Manchester United attacker remains on course for a return to Carrington after he completes his post-World Cup break.

‌



His reunion with the Red Devils was approved by United boss Michael Carrick despite not having played for the club since 2024. Loan spells with Aston Villa and Barcelona kept the 28-year-old away from Manchester, with many believing his career with his boyhood club had come to an end.

‌



However, Barcelona's decision to sign Anthony Gordon instead of paying the £26m option to acquire Rashford permanently left him in limbo. A meaningful offer to sign Rashford has yet to be received by United, but the wheels may be turning on his eventual departure from the Premier League giants.

‌



The Sun reports that Rashford is part of a three-man shortlist for Fenerbahce, including AC Milan forward Rafael Leao and Crystal Palace winger Ismaila Sarr. They add that the Englishman's representatives have been contacted by the Turkish giants over a potential move.

If a move for Rashford to the Super Lig pans out, Carrick's plan of replacing the England star could revolve around Newcastle left-back Lewis Hall. Such an acquisition may sound baffling at first, but it could be quite the masterstroke from the United boss.

Man Utd forward set for shock Premier League transfer 'approach' with stance clear READ MORE :

Patrick Dorgu became a key - and versatile - asset for United last season when fit, playing more games in left-midfield and left-wing than in his natural left-back position. With four goals and four assists to his name in the 25/26 campaign, the Danish international proved to be a legitimate option across United's attack.

‌



Matheus Cunha possesses Rashford's No. 10 shirt and his position on the left flank, with some suggesting Dorgu's go-to role this upcoming season will be playing back-up to the Brazilian.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

View 3 Images Lewis Hall is reportedly a top target for Manchester United (Image: Serena Taylor/Newcastle United via Getty Images)

‌



If that is the case, Carrick will only have Luke Shaw as his realistic option at left-back, thus opening the door to the arrival of Hall, who has emerged as a key target for United this summer.

The 21-year-old is reportedly considered as the long-term replacement to Shaw and United are said to be considering an initial bid of around £60m to prise him away from St James' Park. His departure would mark the fourth major exit from Newcastle this summer, following Gordon, Sandro Tonali, and boss Eddie Howe.

The England defender represents the present and future for United, with his versatility also proving to be a valuable asset. So far in his career, Hall has played 26 matches at left midfield, as per to transfermarkt.

‌



View 3 Images Patrick Dorgu was used in midfield and attack for much of last season (Image: 2026 Manchester United FC)

While he's keen to become an out-and-out first-choice left-back, reportedly blaming his World Cup omission on Howe's varied use of him in the second half of last season, he will slowly replace Shaw - now 31 - as United's starter.

Carrick will need such depth for what he'll hope is a much longer campaign than the last when United exited the domestic cup competitions early and had no European football. And if he could sell the long-term vision to Hall, then he'll have plenty of options to play with on the left side of the pitch.

Sports.title: Man Utd closing in on transfer deal after Michael Carrick dropped hint
Sports.content:
Man Utd closing in on transfer deal after Michael Carrick dropped hint

Michael Carrick left out Radek Vitek for Manchester United's most recent pre-season friendly against Atletico Madrid and the goalkeeper is now on the verge of sealing a move away

View 2 Images Radek Vitek is set to leave Manchester United (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Manchester United are in advanced talks with Middlesbrough over the sale of Radek Vitek. The goalkeeper has been in search of regular game time after an impressive loan spell with Bristol City last season.

‌



Vitek, 22, started United's first two pre-season friendlies under Michael Carrick after returning to Old Trafford. But Carrick left him on the bench for the Red Devils' 2-1 victory over Atletico Madrid on Saturday in a hint at his impending departure.

‌



Now, Vitek is on the verge of completing a move to the Riverside. Multiple reports say that the Czech is close to signing for Middlesbrough on a permanent basis, adding that United will insert both a sell-on clause and a buy-back option into the deal. No fee has emerged at this stage.

‌



Having swept the end-of-season awards at Bristol City, Vitek found himself in high demand. The 22-year-old made it clear at the start of pre-season that he was 'ready' to leave.

"I feel great and ready to go again somewhere to be, hopefully, number one, so we will see," Vitek told reporters. "We will see what is going to happen.

‌



"At the moment, I am still here, but we will see. I hope so. I hope there will be some interest. I think you will know when things are more concrete."

Vitek isn't the only United player who could be on the move in the coming days. Joshua Zirkzee has given the green light to join Juventus while Altay Bayindir is a target for Besiktas.

Who should Manchester United sign before the transfer window closes? Have your say in the comments section.

Carrick would like to add a third midfielder, particularly after Manuel Ugarte picked up a serious knee injury at the World Cup and will be ruled out for most of the season. However, the Red Devils hierarchy are weighing up whether to prioritise other areas instead.

Left-back is a position which United want to strengthen, with Luke Shaw's fitness always a concern and Patrick Dorgu being used further forward since Carrick was appointed. Newcastle's Lewis Hall is a target and he'd be open to the switch, but it'd likely take a huge fee to prise him away from a club who've already made big sales this summer.

Sports.title: Ex-Arsenal star makes winning return to English football with League Two club
Sports.content:
Ex-Arsenal star makes winning return to English football with League Two club

Vito Mannone, the ex-Arsenal goalkeeper, signed for Crawley Town as a player-coach this summer and he's already been thrust between the posts by boss Colin Kazim-Richards

View 3 Images Vito Mannone made his first appearance in 18 months (Image: Anna Gowthorpe/Shutterstock)

Former Arsenal goalkeeper Vito Mannone kept a clean sheet to help new club Crawley Town beat York City 2-0 on Monday and reach the Carabao Cup first round proper. Mannone, 38, signed for the League Two side as a player-coach in June after spending last season as a free agent while earning his coaching badges.

‌



The Italian got the nod for Crawley's first game of the season, travelling to York's LNER Community Stadium in a preliminary round of the Carabao Cup. Mannone and his team-mates advanced thanks to goals from Gianmarco Di Biase and Danilo Orsi.

‌



The victory booked Crawley a trip to Watford this Saturday. It was Mannone's first competitive appearance since February 2025 with former club Lille.

‌



He was on Arsenal's books for eight years, making a total of 23 first-team appearances. Mannone left the Emirates in 2013 to join Sunderland for £2million, spending the next four seasons at the Stadium of Light before moving to Reading.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Arsenal star gives honest verdict on Vinicius Junior as transfer hinges on fresh talks READ MORE :

Bruno Guimaraes to Arsenal saga has Newcastle in contention for all-time worst transfer window READ MORE :

He then plied his trade in France after signing for Monaco in 2020, later joining Lorient and finally Lille. Crawley convinced Mannone to make the drop from the French top flight to the fourth tier of English football by handing him a dual role, with the 38-year-old having recently been coaching at Brighton.

‌



Mannone will head up Crawley's goalkeeping department, taking training sessions and leading player development. "I am delighted and proud to take on this role and can't wait to meet everyone at the club and to start working with the staff and players," he said.

Who should Arsenal sign before the transfer window closes? Have your say in the comments section.

View 3 Images Vito Mannone made his debut for Crawley Town in Monday's cup tie (Image: Anna Gowthorpe/Shutterstock)

‌



"I'll give everything to the cause and hope to pass on my experiences as a player, leading into a successful season."

Crawley's manager, former Premier League striker Colin Kazim-Richards, explained: "To be able to add to my coaching staff, to the club, someone of Vito's calibre is a credit in itself.

"His knowledge, his footballing experiences, playing at the highest level with some of the best coaches in terms of standards, what it actually takes and ideas coming from a country that creates amazing goalkeepers, has really taken us up another level.

‌



View 3 Images Vito Mannone spent eight years at Arsenal (Image: David Price/Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

"Vito comes with an intensity, and it's something I'm looking forward to in terms of creating a relationship and benefiting from his skills from a goalkeeper's perspective, and also as a person. As soon as we spoke, I knew he was the right man, so I can't wait to work with him."

Sports.title: Tony Bloom's Royal Ascot heroine ruled out for rest of season after injury blow
Sports.content:
Tony Bloom's Royal Ascot heroine ruled out for rest of season after injury blow

Commonwealth Cup winner Venetian Sun has been ruled out for the rest of the season after trainer Karl Burke confirmed the sprinter has suffered a tendon injury

View 3 Images Tony Bloom (second left) with Venetian Sun, who followed up her success at Royal Ascot with a Group 1 victory in France (Image: PA)

Tony Bloom's Royal Ascot heroine Venetian Sun has suffered an injury setback that will sideline her for the remainder of the campaign.

‌



Among last year's top juveniles, the lightning-quick daughter of Starman – owned by Brighton & Hove Albion chairman in partnership with Ian McAleavy – has maintained her brilliant form this season, claiming a second Royal Ascot triumph when storming to Commonwealth Cup glory.

‌



Her most recent outing saw her produce an excellent runner-up effort against older rivals at Newmarket in the July Cup, and she had been under consideration for a trip to France for this weekend's Prix Maurice de Gheest at Deauville, the venue where she captured the Prix Morny as a two-year-old.

‌



Rossa Ryan convinces BHA panel to reduce 28-day ban to 10 days at appeal hearing READ MORE :

Saffie Osborne to captain Ryan Moore and Dylan Browne McMonagle in Shergar Cup at Ascot READ MORE :

Nevertheless, plans for the remainder of her three year old campaign have been shelved following the discovery of a tendon problem.

Her trainer Karl Burke said: "It's a big shame and unfortunately it happens. It's a long way from being a career- or life-threatening injury, but obviously is going to take time and it's very disappointing.

"We had more or less decided to swerve Deauville anyway because the ground was very fast out there last weekend with no sign of any rain and the French not watering like they used to do.

‌



View 3 Images Celebrations on the track after Venetian Sun's Royal Ascot victory (Image: Getty Images)

"It's just one of those things, we have a feeling she may have initiated it at Newmarket during the July Cup but she came back from there with a nasty little cut and she had been on antibiotics and anti-inflammatories and we think that may have masked it to a degree."

Venetian Sun has triumphed in six of her nine career starts to date, with her connections eagerly anticipating an autumn schedule that could have featured appearances in Haydock's Sprint Cup, at Ascot on British Champions Day and at the Breeders' Cup.

‌



Explaining the setback, Burke added: "It's basically a strain to the tendon, it happens a lot with jumping horses – it's unusual really at this stage in a sprinter's life, but can happen.

View 3 Images Venetian Sun sprinted to victory at Ascot (Image: Martin Dokoupil/ZUMA Press Wire/Shutterstock)

"It's a time thing now and she will have the next six or seven months on the easy list and then be reassessed from there.

Article continues below

"The little bit of work she has done the last few days has just aggravated it and we've had the vets in this morning and they weren't 100 per cent happy with a little bit of heat in the leg and that is what it turns out to be.

"The plan before today was if she finished the season in good shape she would stay in training and that may still be the plan, but that is a discussion for later on."

Sports.title: Harry Kane extending his Bayern stay is a no-brainer - and Ballon d'Or could play big part
Sports.content:
Harry Kane extending his Bayern stay is a no-brainer - and Ballon d'Or could play big part

The England captain will head back to his club in the next few days and Bayern will immediately resume talks over a new contract that will keep the striker in the Bundesliga beyond 2027

View 3 Images Harry Kane has had three very productive seasons with Bayern Munich (Image: Alex Grimm/Getty Images)

Just over nine years ago, Harry Kane mildly surprised a small gathering of reporters when he declared winning the Ballon d’Or to be one of his prime ambitions. Nothing wrong with aiming high, of course. But, at the time, Kane was a 23-year-old striker who had made 17 appearances for his country and had scored five goals.

‌



His numbers with Spurs were very good - 78 goals in 113 Premier League appearances - but he had only been an established top-flight player for three seasons. But Kane believed in himself and lifting that Ballon d’Or is a realistic prospect when the awards ceremony, for the first time in its history, comes to London in October.

‌



Carabao Cup draw confirmed as final fixtures announced for round one READ MORE :

Gianni Infantino ripped apart as explosive FIFA email leaked after botched World Cup plan READ MORE :

Bookmakers do not normally get these sorts of things wrong and every odds-maker has Kane as the favourite to become the seventh British player to receive the accolade. The influence of the World Cup, though, should not be under-estimated.

‌



Some of the 100 journalists who make the choice could well forgive Rodri an injury-interrupted and otherwise mediocre season with his club for his imperious role in Spain’s summer triumph. Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe would appear to be the only other realistic contenders.

And they are worthy contenders. If Kane does not win the 2026 edition, he will have the award in his sights for next year - a year with no major international tournaments.

And if he stays at Bayern Munich, goals are a guarantee. In three seasons in Germany, he has 146 in 147 appearances. If he moved to Barcelona - a switch that seems slightly fanciful but has been mooted reasonably strongly - goals would be a guarantee.

‌



View 3 Images Rodri won the Ballon d'Or in 2024 and is a strong contender for this year's award (Image: Getty Images)

Kane is not coming back to the Premier League any time soon, we can be fairly certain of that. He will report back for training with Bayern after the Bundesliga champions have returned from a pre-season trip to Korea and Hong Kong on Saturday.

Contract talks will immediately resume, as his current deal expires in the summer of 2027. And quite frankly, it is hard to see why Kane would not want to extend his agreement.

‌



He could ask for a release clause at the end of next season if he feels he might have the urge to come back and break the Premier League goalscoring record - he is currently 47 short of Alan Shearer’s total of 260 - but he seems extremely content in Bavaria. Plus, the style of play, the quality of play, the guarantee of competing for honours on all fronts, are all factors that will help him stay in top shape for the international challenges that still lie ahead, most notably leading England into Euro 2028.

He turned 33 a week ago but Kane has looked a better, all-round player for his time in Munich. He was certainly more impressive for England at World Cup 2026 than he was at either Euro 2024 or World Cup 2022. He is not unusual but playing in a dominant team suits him.

View 3 Images Harry Kane has plenty of international challenges left despite his World Cup disappointment (Image: Getty Images)

‌



When he sits down with his advisers and the Bayern hierarchy in the next week, there will, of course, be no escaping the relevance of his age. But over the past few years, the longevity of marquee players - and of strikers, in particular - will have probably had a bearing on his plans.

Since his 34th birthday, Kane’s predecessor at Bayern, Robert Lewandowski, has scored 125 club goals. Kane could return to the Premier League as a 35-year-old - in two seasons’ time - and still fancy his chances of beating Shearer’s number.

But before then, he will have his eyes on another individual accolade. And if the Ballon d’Or does not come his way on the 70th anniversary of the award (the first one, in 1956, was won by Stanley Matthews, hence why the ceremony is in London), you can guarantee he will be a contender again if he stays at Bayern Munich. The Premier League and Shearer’s record are going to have to wait.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."
