World.title: President Hichilema Salutes Dr Monze’s Exemplary Public Service
World.content:
President Hakainde Hichilema has described late Southern Province Permanent Secretary Namani Monze as a dependable public servant who served the Zambian people with integrity, commitment and humility during his tenure in public office.

Dr Monze was laid to rest at his family farm in Bwacha Ward of Choma District, where mourners gathered to pay their final respects, with First Lady Mutinta Hichilema among those in attendance.

The President, in a speech read on his behalf by Secretary to the Cabinet Patrick Kangwa, said Dr Monze distinguished himself through dedicated service across key sectors including health, education and infrastructure development.

“He was a dependable public servant who served with integrity, commitment and humility,” he said

President Hichilema further paid tribute to Dr Monze’s calm leadership style, noting that he was a civil servant who avoided controversy and instead focused on delivering results for the people.

He said such qualities were rare and worthy of emulation by those currently serving in government.

” Dr Monze understood public office and executed his duties with diligence, his death was a profound loss to the public service and the nation at large”, he said.

He also emphasized that government would remember Dr Monze not only for his professional contributions but also for his ability to work with communities and traditional leaders in fostering development at the grassroots level.

The President said his spirit of collaboration had helped strengthen service delivery in Southern Province.

The Head of State further extended his condolences to the bereaved family, urging them to take comfort in the legacy of service and respect that Dr Monze left behind.

“I encourage you to remain strong, as the nation stands with you during this difficult period of mourning”, he reiterated.

And Chief Hamusonde, speaking on behalf of other traditional leaders in Southern Province, praised Dr Monze for his responsiveness and inclusive leadership style.

“He was always prompt in responding to the needs of the people and made it easy for chiefdoms to work with government,” he said.

The Chief remarkably commended Dr Monze ‘s humility saying that his genuine interest in people knew no social status.

The chief also urged family members to continue comforting the widow and the children and warned against property grabbing.

The church, represented by Dr Vanny Munyumbwe, offered words of comfort to the bereaved family, urging them to remain strong and anchored in faith during the period of mourning.

“He was a dedicated Christian who supported the church and lived a life guided by faith and service,” she said.

And widow, late Dr Monze’s wife, Joleha Monze, described her late husband as a loving and respectful man who valued family and treated everyone with kindness.

“He was a caring man who showered me with love and respect and always put his family first,” she said.

The children remembered their father as a joyful and principled man who instilled values of integrity and humility in the family.

“My father was a cheerful man who lived with integrity and humility and always encouraged us to do what is right,” she said.

Family members, including his sister Kabanga Malekwa, described Dr Monze as a pillar of strength whose leadership extended beyond his professional life into the wider community.

“He was a pillar of strength to our family and a man who united everyone around him,” she said.

Though Dr Namani Monze has been laid to rest, mourners said his legacy of humility, dedication and service to the people of Southern Province will continue to inspire future generations.

The burial was also attended by former Southern Province Minister Credo Nanjuwa and, former Minister of Information and Media Cornelius Mweetwa.

Others who attended the burial include Ministry of Information and Media Permanent Secretary Thabo kawana, Central Province Permanent Secretary Milner Mwanakampwe and other senior government and UPND officials.

Dr Monze 52, died on 28th July 2026, and he is survived by a wife and four children.

World.title: Government Calls for Collective Action Against GBV
World.content:
Government has called for collective action to address teenage pregnancy, Gender Based Violence (GBV) and substance abuse among young people in Chadiza District.

Speaking during an Adolescent Health Awareness Walk held in Chadiza under the theme “Breaking the Cycle: Preventing Teenage Pregnancy, GBV and Substance Use,” Acting District Commissioner (DC)Masauso Mwale said child marriages, drug abuse, school dropouts and sexual abuse continue to affect many young people.

He said this in remarks made on his behalf by Chadiza District Community Development Officer, Charles Situmbeko.

The Acting DC said the challenges not only affect individual lives but also socio-economic development in the community.

“I encourage parents, teachers, traditional leaders, religious leaders, health workers, cooperating partners and young people to continue working together to protect every adolescent,” he said.

He mentioned that young people need safe spaces where they can learn, receive guidance, develop skills, access information and stay away from harmful activities.

Meanwhile, Chadiza District Health Director, Bless Shimuunza, said the awareness walk is worthwhile because it has brought positive change in Chadiza, specifically for adolescents.

Dr Shimuunza said government, in partnership with organisations such as Plan International and She Soars, is conducting sensitization programs in different areas of Chadiza to educate adolescents.

“We go round in different areas of Chadiza sensitizing adolescents,” he said.

World.title: President Hichilema Promises Revival of Chambishi metals
World.content:
President Hakainde Hichilema has called on the residents of Chambishi to vote for the United Party for National Development (UPND) in the forth coming general elections on August 13th to enable the government to continue implementing its agenda.

The Head of state explained that voting for the UPND means continued development in the country.

Speaking during the community engagement at twalubuka schools grounds in Chambishi, in Kalulushi district on the Copperbelt Province, President Hichilema says his government will work on the reopening of Chambishi metals if re-elected in the August 13 general elections.

“We are going to re-open the Chambishi metals if you are going to vote for us in the forthcoming elections,” President Hichilema said.

The Head of state said government will continue engaging stakeholders over the Chambishi dumpsite to enhance mining activities, while stressing the need for legal and safe mining practices.

” We want to work on legalising mining activities, no parent wants to see their children dying anyhow like that,” said President Hichilema.

He stated that he will work on paying all the ex-miners that were not paid a long time ago.

He advised the residents of Chambishi not to make a mistake of voting for political parties that were busy copying the UPND manifesto.

The Head of State also disclosed that if re-elected into office, the UPND administration will pay for 16,000 people in Kabaso area to be connected to the national gride.

President Hichilema added that farmers will not be sharing a bucket of fertiliser once the UPND is re-elected.

” When you vote for us in these coming elections, I assure you that you will not be sharing a bucket of fertiliser,” said President Hichilema.

He stated that the Food Reserve Agency will be paying farmers within two days through their mobile money accounts.

He further directed Zesco limited to connect about 16,000 people from Kabaso area to the national electricity grid, stating that high connection charges should not prevent citizens from accessing power.

President Hichilema further announced that government will improve radiology services at Chambishi Hospital and rehabilitate township roads in the area.

He added that government remained committed to resolving the outstanding payments for former miners who are yet to receive their dues.

The President noted that the Constituency Development Fund (CDF) has been increased from K1.8 million to K40.8 million per constituency to accelerate community development in the country.

World.title: Nora demands action as Beijing ‘withholds’ Mukoma from WAFCON
World.content:
The Football Association of Zambia has officially complained to FIFA and CAF over the failure by Chinese Women’s Super League side Beijing to release Copper Queens striker Fridah Mukoma for the ongoing Women’s Africa Cup of Nations in Morocco.

Mukoma was among the 26 players summoned by Zambia coach Nora Häuptle for WAFCON and was expected to join camp by 20th July.

Speaking ahead of Zambia’s decisive Group C match against Malawi on Wednesday night, Häuptle confirmed the matter has been escalated.

“Fridah Mukoma was not released by her club in China. She is one of our top players and she is not getting released by her club,” Häuptle said.

“We have escalated this matter to CAF and now to FIFA. We expect action from CAF and FIFA because clubs must respect the release of players to national teams,” she said.

“I mean national teams have authority over players. I expect punishment from her team in Beijing. This is a clear issue,” Häuptle added.

The non-release has deprived the Copper Queens of a key attacking option as they fight to advance to the quarterfinals.

Zambia must beat Malawi on Wednesday night to progress from Group C.

FIFA regulations compel clubs to release players for official national team duty during international windows, with sanctions possible for non-compliance.

World.title: Africa: All of Africa Today - August 4, 2026
World.content:
DR Congo Audit Confirms Oil Pollution Findings

The Democratic Republic of the Congo's Ministry of Hydrocarbons expects to complete and publish a full environmental audit of oil company Perenco by the end of September. This comes after preliminary findings that identified pollution linked to the company's operations. A ministry official said the audit found negative impacts on soil and air quality, with ageing infrastructure and pipelines contributing to environmental damage. The findings broadly support a recent Human Rights Watch report alleging that Perenco's activities, including gas flaring, open burning of oil waste and oil spills, have polluted air, soil and water sources and posed health risks to nearby communities. Perenco has denied causing pollution. However, the government said that the final report will recommend environmental remediation measures and infrastructure upgrades.

Benin Launches New Senate Chamber

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

Benin has launched its new Senate, a second chamber of parliament designed to beef up legislative oversight and protect the country's constitutional order. The Senate will scrutinise laws, request second readings of bills and has the power to block constitutional, electoral and political party reforms it deems a danger to democracy, peace or national unity. It can also suspend or revoke the political rights of public officials accused of undermining state institutions or social cohesion. Supporters say the chamber will provide better checks and balances and preserve Benin's democratic traditions. Its legitimacy has been challenged by critics, who warn that, because its members are appointed, not directly elected, it could undermine democratic accountability.

AI-Enabled Cybercrime on the Rise Across Africa

More than half of all reported cybercrimes across Africa are now powered by artificial intelligence, according to INTERPOL's 2026 African Cyberthreat Assessment Report. The report found that 55% of reported cybercrime incidents involved AI-enabled tools. Cybercrime is becoming increasingly automated and transnational, with financial losses across the continent more than doubling since 2024 to an estimated $484 million, the report said. The most common threat remains online scams, where criminals are increasingly using AI-generated synthetic identities to bypass biometric security systems and commit fraud. INTERPOL also highlighted the growing threat of phishing, ransomware and mobile money fraud, calling on governments and businesses to shore up cybersecurity as organised criminal networks exploit AI to mount faster and more sophisticated attacks across Africa.

Zimbabwe's Examination Board Releases June 2026 Exam Results

The Zimbabwe School Examinations Council (ZIMSEC) has announced the 2026 June Ordinary and Advanced Level examination results. Candidates are able to access them online via the ZIMSEC portal. The Ordinary Level pass rate for candidates who wrote five or more subjects fell to 3%, down from 5.87% in 2025. The Advanced Level pass rate for candidates passing at least two subjects rose by 11.88% points to 67.74%. ZIMSEC said the online results portal will remain open for five days. Printed results will be available for collection by examination centre heads from regional offices.

Close 

UN Opens Major Ebola Treatment Centre in DR Congo

The Democratic Republic of the Congo is facing its largest-ever Ebola outbreak. The virus has spread to 49 health zones across several provinces, with Ituri accounting for the vast majority of infections and deaths. In response, the United Nations and its partners are opening the country's largest Ebola treatment centre, with a capacity of 100 beds, alongside a new transit centre to improve early detection and referrals. WHO has warned that a major scale-up of response efforts is urgently needed. They cite conflict, displacement, cross-border movement and worsening humanitarian conditions as key factors driving the rapid spread of the disease.

World.title: South Africa: Water Crisis Turns Deadly in Durban - South African News Briefs - August 4, 2026
World.content:
Water Crisis Turns Deadly in Durban

Residents of Adams Mission, south of Durban, have accused government water tanker drivers of selling water that should be supplied free of charge, following the death of 43-year-old Celani Zungu, reports EWN. Community members allege Zungu was trying to stop a tanker from leaving without delivering water to residents when he was struck and killed by the vehicle. Local councillor Thembelihle Makhanya said there is no concrete evidence of water being sold. He condemned the allegations if proven true. Police are investigating a case of culpable homicide, while the eThekwini Municipality has launched an internal investigation.

Westbury Residents March Against Gang Violence



Residents of Westbury in Johannesburg are set to march, demanding decisive action to curb persistent gang violence and drug-related crime, reports SABC News. Community leader Bishop Dulton Adams said residents are calling for long-term solutions rather than temporary police deployments. He argued that law enforcement has a lack of a visible presence in the neighbourhood. He criticised authorities for failing to patrol the area adequately and urged stronger policing and sustained interventions to tackle gangsterism.

Parliament Defends GBVF Council Picks

Parliament's Portfolio Committee on Women, Youth and Persons with Disabilities has defended its recommendations for the newly appointed Gender-Based Violence and Femicide (GBVF) Council, rejecting criticism from COSATU over the absence of a labour representative, reports EWN. Committee chairperson Liezl van der Merwe said the selection process was fair, legally compliant and based on candidates' experience and expertise. COSATU maintains the council should include organised labour and plans to challenge the appointments. Parliament has said that legal advice confirms that labour representation is not a legislative requirement under the GBVF Act.

World.title: Somalia: Cabinet Officials Brace to Relinquish Kenyan Passports After Presidential Ultimatum
World.content:
A mounting cohort of senior Somali government ministers is poised to surrender their Kenyan passports and national identity documents within days, heeding President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud's ultimatum that dual citizens holding public office must forswear their foreign nationality or immediately vacate their posts, according to multiple informed sources.

The impending wave of surrenders represents the most aggressive enforcement of citizenship integrity standards within the executive branch in recent memory, building on Deputy Prime Minister Jibril Abdirashid Haji's unilateral decision to return his Kenyan travel documents,a move that effectively set a binding precedent for his cabinet colleagues.

Deputy Prime Minister Jibril Abdirashid Haji became the first senior figure to bow to the directive when he formally handed over his Kenyan passport to the Kenyan Embassy in Mogadishu earlier this week.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

In a terse statement, Jibril asserted the move was designed to guarantee "complete transparency" in the execution of his official duties and to preempt any challenge to his national allegiance.

Sources who spoke to Dalsan on condition of anonymity, citing lack of authorisation to engage publicly on the matter, disclosed that several ministers and state ministers are now finalising arrangements to submit their Kenyan travel credentials and identification cards to the diplomatic mission. The sources indicated that the officials are acting with haste to avoid being perceived as defying the President's edict, which was first articulated during a closed-door cabinet sitting last Thursday.

"The President made it unequivocally clear that retaining a foreign passport while occupying a senior government portfolio is untenable," one source told Dalsan. "Those who intend to retain their cabinet seats are moving swiftly to comply, and a series of handovers is widely anticipated before the week concludes."

The directive has cast a harsh glare on the prevalence of dual citizenship among Somalia's political elite--a sensitive issue long left unaddressed but now thrust into the open.

Although Somalia's provisional constitution does not explicitly outlaw dual nationality for public officials, the President's order effectively imposes a new litmus test for the upper echelons of power, compelling officials to choose definitively between their Somali responsibilities and foreign entitlements.

The enforcement drive comes against the backdrop of heightened scrutiny of senior officials' travel documentation, with some figures having recently encountered obstacles at Kenyan ports of entry.

State Minister at the Presidency Abdirashid was among those reportedly turned away by Kenyan immigration authorities, although it remains unclear whether that incident directly precipitated the presidential directive.

Close 

Villa Somalia has yet to issue a formal communiqué on the enforcement timeline, and the Kenyan government has likewise refrained from commenting on the expected influx of surrendered documents. However, insiders suggest the list of compliant officials will expand as the President's unannounced deadline looms, with further developments expected imminently.

World.title: West Africa: Ecowas Pledges U.S.$250,000 for June 29 Flood Victims
World.content:
An area in Accra flooded after heavy afternoon rain (file photo).

THE Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) has pledged US$250,000, equivalent to about GH¢3 million, to support victims of the June 29 floods that ravaged parts of Ghana.

The donation, announced by the Minister of Foreign Affairs, Mr Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa, is expected to bolster ongoing relief efforts for thousands of people affected by the disaster.

In a Facebook post, Mr Ablakwa said the Ministry of Foreign Affairs had received official notification from the ECOWAS Commission on the assistance.

He said the funds would be transferred in full to the appropriate state institutions immediately after they are received by the ministry.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

Related Articles

"The transfer will be done in the interest of transparency and accountability," the minister assured.

Mr Ablakwa expressed the government's gratitude to ECOWAS for the gesture, describing it as a demonstration of solidarity and genuine African compassion at a difficult time for the country.

The June 29 floods affected communities in seven regions, claiming lives, displacing thousands of residents and destroying homes, roads and other infrastructure.

Government agencies, supported by humanitarian organisations and other stakeholders, have since been providing relief to affected families while efforts continue to restore livelihoods in the flood-hit communities.

The ECOWAS support is expected to complement the government's ongoing response to the disaster and bring relief to victims.

The June 29 floods, triggered by hours of torrential rainfall, submerged several communities across seven regions, including Greater Accra, causing widespread destruction to homes, businesses, roads and other public infrastructure.

The disaster claimed several lives, displaced thousands of residents and left many households stranded, with emergency response teams undertaking rescue operations while government agencies and humanitarian organisations provided relief items to affected families.

President John Dramani Mahama subsequently visited some of the worst-hit communities, describing the situation as a national tragedy and assuring victims of government's commitment to provide immediate relief and support reconstruction efforts.

The ECOWAS intervention is expected to complement ongoing government and humanitarian assistance aimed at easing the plight of affected families and supporting the recovery of flood-hit communities.

World.title: Uganda: 14 Killed As Truck Crashes Into Taxi in Lwera
World.content:
At least 14 people have been confirmed dead in a grisly accident in Lwera swamp along the Kampala -Masaka Highway.

The accident according to Greater Masaka Regional Police spokesperson, Twaha Kasirye, happened at around 11pm on Monday at Kamunga Trading Centre in Lwera Swamp, Kalungu District.

"The accident involved a Toyota Hiace taxi (UA 662AQ) and a Sino truck (UBS 040F) transporting sand. Fourteen (14) people died on the spot, all from the taxi," Kasirye said.

He added that four other people, including two occupants from each vehicle, sustained injuries and were rushed to Masaka Regional Referral Hospital, where they are currently receiving treatment.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

He said police officers visited and documented the scene, while investigations into the cause of the crash are ongoing.

"Investigations are underway as efforts to trace the fleeing driver are ongoing."

The development comes as concerns over fatalities on Ugandan roads continue.

At least 37 people died in major road accidents within 10 days in July 2026, with four major crashes involving public transport vehicles, including three school buses carrying learners on educational trips and one passenger service bus.

The deadliest incident occurred on July 17 in Kapchorwa District, where 21 people, including 20 pupils of King David Junior School in Ndejje, Kampala, and one adult, died after their bus crashed while returning from a study tour at Sipi Falls.

The Isuzu bus, registration number UA 108BQ, reportedly developed mechanical problems before the fatal crash at Chekwatit Village, Kimawa Parish, Kawowo Sub-county.

Police preliminary investigations indicated that the driver lost control of the vehicle, which veered off the road, struck a large stone and overturned.

The tragedy raised concerns over the safety checks conducted before school trips and whether vehicles transporting learners meet the required safety standards.

Days earlier, on July 7, 2026, another fatal crash at Bobi Trading Centre along the Kampala-Gulu Highway claimed 14 lives and left 28 others injured.

The crash involved a passenger bus, registration number UBE 110H, belonging to OPIT Travellers Company, and a Mercedes-Benz Actros trailer, registration numbers KBS 564D/ZE 7948.

According to police findings, the bus driver was speeding and lost control while attempting to avoid a pedestrian crossing the road, resulting in a head-on collision with the trailer.

The police annual traffic report for 2025 indicated that Uganda registered 26,044 road crashes, indicating a 3.7% increase from the figure registered in 2024.

Close 

Of these, 4,602 were fatal, rising from the 4,434 reported in 2024 while 18,444 people got serious injuries and 3,668 got minor injuries.

In the accidents, men accounted for 83% of all the deaths while October with 523 deaths registered the highest fatalities.

World.title: South Africa: Anger After Farmers Dump Rotting Fruit Near Homes
World.content:
Farmers would never do this in their own suburbs, say Eastern Cape residents

Residents of Patensie, Eastern Cape, say farmers dumped truckloads of rotting fruit, nets and other farm waste on land earmarked for a housing project.

Kouga Local Municipality removed 14 truckloads of waste and says the illegal dumping has been referred to law enforcement for investigation.

Acht Boerdery says it has a longstanding arrangement to provide waste fruit for animals and denies dumping the nets and cables. Waterwiel Boerdery says it only left flood-damaged netting at the site after people requested it, and has since removed the material. Quacha Boerdery did not respond.

Residents of Patensie in the Eastern Cape have accused farmers of dumping truckloads of oranges and lemons, as well as farm equipment on land near their homes. They say farmers "would never do this in their own suburbs".

The rotting fruit attracted insects, as well as pigs and cattle, and created a heavy stench over Ramaphosa Village. Meanwhile, discarded nets, cables and irrigation pipes littered the site.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

The Kouga Local Municipality has cleared the area, removing 14 truckloads of waste.

The open land in Stuurmanskop is earmarked for a housing project.

Community leader Eric Blaauw posted on the What's Happening in Patensie Facebook page on 19 July: "New illegal dumping site by our farmers around Patensie. This is not good at all for the health and safety of our kids. This area is for housing development, not dumping. We're really being undermined."

Ward 10 councillor Mbandana Msingathi Gerald said he was alerted on 19 July to complaints about the stench from rotten lemons. Residents accused Acht Boerdery and Quacha Boerdery of dumping the fruit.

"I contacted local farmers' association chairperson Grewar Oosthuizen and gave him the names of the alleged dumpers. He promised to act immediately. Nets, wires and irrigation pipes were scattered across roads in Ramaphosa Village," Gerald said.

He said cattle ate the oranges but not the lemons.

Residents had previously buried fruit and vegetables at the site, but this stopped once the site was designated for housing.

Gerald said Patensie's only dumping site closed a year ago. Residents now have to travel 15km to Hankey to dispose of waste, and many cannot afford it. He said there is no local transit site, which is a serious issue for a town that exports fruit internationally.

Kouga Local Municipality spokesperson Monique Basson said officials had acted immediately after seeing reports on social media.

Basson told GroundUp: "We removed 14 truckloads of waste. The waste management section conducted a site inspection which confirmed illegal dumping.

"The matter was referred to law enforcement for investigation with the aim of identifying those responsible and taking legal action in terms of municipal by-laws," she said.

Acht Boerdery director Christof Opperman said the farm had a longstanding arrangement with the local livestock farmers' committee and the councillor's office to provide waste product for cattle, pigs, goats and chickens in an area where the animals already graze.

Opperman said recent floods and market pressure linked to the conflict in the Middle East had affected export and juicing channels, leaving fruit it believed still suitable for livestock.

"We also use the Hankey municipal dump for other waste and were not advised that the livestock product was excessive," he said.

Opperman said the farm was not involved in dumping the nets and cables. "We remain committed to sustainable farming and would not knowingly endanger the community, its people or its animals."

Opperman said staff may take waste fruit home for personal use and for their livestock, while remaining waste fruit is taken to the agreed grazing area and residual waste is mulched.

Close 

Charl Malan of Waterwiel Boerdery said his farm only dropped off flood-damaged covering nets at the site after people requested them. He denied dumping any fruit.

"After the floods, people asked me for netting that was damaged. After it was dropped off in heaps, it was scattered around by people taking the nets. I was unaware that fruit was dumped there. That must have happened afterwards and was not done by me," Malan said.

Malan said he did not anticipate the netting would become a health hazard.

Malan said the farm regularly experiences vandalism and theft. He said he hoped giving away damaged netting would reduce theft from the farm.

Malan said that as soon as he became aware of the problem, he sent his own workers and machinery to remove the netting. GroundUp saw workers using one of Malan's tractors to collect the nets.

Quacha Boerdery did not respond to requests for comment.

World.title: Zimbabwe: ZIMSEC Releases 2026 June Exam Results - O-Level Pass Rate Drops, A-Level Performance Improves
World.content:
The Zimbabwe School Examinations Council (ZIMSEC) has announced the release of the 2026 June Ordinary and Advanced Level examination results, with candidates able to access them online from 6pm Monday.

The Ordinary Level pass rate for candidates who wrote five or more subjects fell by 2.87%, from 5.87% recorded in 2025, to 3% in June 2026.

The Advanced Level pass rate for candidates who passed at least two subjects (Grade E or better) increased by 11.88% from last year, to 67.74% in 2026.

Speaking during a media briefing in Harare, ZIMSEC board chairperson Professor Paul Mapfumo said the results would be available on the examination body's online portal for only five days.

"The Zimbabwe School Examinations Council board and management would like to advise the nation of the release of the 2026 June Ordinary and Advanced Level examination results.

"With effect from today, 3 August 2026 at 6pm, Ordinary and Advanced Level examination results will be accessible to all candidates and authorised personnel online through the ZIMSEC portal accessed via the ZIMSEC website.

"Please take note that this portal will be open for five days only," said Mapfumo.

Mapfumo also said heads of examination centres would begin collecting printed results for their respective schools and centres from ZIMSEC regional offices on Tuesday.

World.title: Africa: Over Half of Africa's Cybercrimes Are AI-Enabled - Interpol
World.content:
Nairobi — More than half of all cybercrimes reported across Africa are now AI-enabled, the International Criminal Police Organization (INTERPOL) has revealed, warning that digital attacks have rapidly evolved into an industrialized, borderless ecosystem that is becoming increasingly difficult to detect and combat.

According to the newly released INTERPOL African Cyberthreat Assessment Report 2026, 55 percent of cybercrimes reported across the continent now involve Artificial Intelligence (AI), underscoring a major shift in the cyber threat landscape.

The report says cybercrime has evolved into an increasingly automated underground economy, where criminal networks are using AI and other advanced technologies to launch attacks faster, at greater scale, and across multiple countries simultaneously.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

The report further shows that cybercrime-related financial losses across Africa have more than doubled since 2024, reaching an estimated $484 million.

The assessment, based on survey data from 36 member countries and intelligence from private sector partners including Fortinet, Mastercard, the Shadowserver Foundation, S2W and TrendAI, found that 72 percent of surveyed countries reported the presence of organized scam centres, with the highest concentration in Southern and West Africa.

Among the most alarming developments highlighted in the report is the growing use of AI-generated synthetic identities to bypass biometric security systems.

Criminals are combining stolen personal information with fabricated data to deceive identity verification processes, enabling them to open bank accounts, obtain mobile loans and register SIM cards under false identities.

Online scams remain the most frequently reported form of cybercrime across the continent, while the financial services, telecommunications and government sectors continue to bear the brunt of AI-enabled credential theft and automated social engineering attacks.

The findings mirror Kenya's own evolving cyber threat landscape.

In June, the Communications Authority of Kenya (CA) announced that it detected 3.37 billion cyber threat events between January and March 2026. Although this represented a 26.15 percent decline from the previous quarter, the authority cautioned that attacks had become increasingly sophisticated, with system attacks targeting critical information infrastructure accounting for 3.23 billion of the incidents.

The INTERPOL report also noted that Kenya ranked among SOCRadar's top phishing detections globally in September 2025.

Recent cyber incidents have further illustrated the growing risks facing the country. One notable case occurred on July 18, 2026, when hackers compromised the official website of the President William Ruto, defacing its homepage with messages targeting President Ruto and demanding a ransom of five Bitcoins, worth about Sh41 million at the time.

The attackers threatened to leak unspecified information if their demands were not met. The government immediately took the website offline, with Information, Communications and the Digital Economy Cabinet Secretary William Kabogo assuring the public that response protocols had been activated and that there was no evidence of unauthorized access to sensitive government data. The presidential website was restored two days later.

The growing sophistication of cyberattacks has prompted coordinated international operations aimed at dismantling transnational cybercrime networks.

Under Operation Red Card 2.0, conducted between December 8, 2025, and January 30, 2026, across 16 African countries, law enforcement agencies arrested 651 suspects and recovered more than USD 4.3 million. Investigators identified 1,247 victims, whose reported losses exceeded USD 45 million.

In Kenya, authorities arrested 27 individuals linked to online investment fraud schemes that relied on messaging applications, social media platforms and fabricated testimonials to lure victims.

Investigators said suspects convinced victims to make initial investments of as little as USD 50, displaying fake investment dashboards showing fictitious profits before blocking withdrawals and disappearing with the funds.

A separate global operation, Operation Synergia III, conducted between July 18, 2025, and January 31, 2026, brought together law enforcement agencies from 72 countries and territories.

The operation resulted in the takedown of more than 45,000 malicious servers and internet addresses linked to phishing, ransomware and information-stealing malware campaigns, while leading to 94 key arrests worldwide.

"Cybercrime in 2026 is more sophisticated and destructive than ever before, but Operation Synergia III stands as a powerful testament to what global cooperation can achieve," said Neal Jetton, Director of INTERPOL's Cybercrime Directorate.

Jetton said organized cybercriminal syndicates continue to inflict severe financial and psychological harm on individuals, businesses and communities through increasingly sophisticated online fraud schemes, emphasizing that Operation Red Card demonstrates the critical role of international collaboration in combating transnational cybercrime.

Close 

The report also highlights significant regional variations in cyber threats. East Africa has emerged as a hotspot for mobile money fraud and ransomware attacks targeting critical infrastructure, while West and Central Africa remain major centres for business email compromise and romance scams.

Southern Africa continues to attract global threat actors seeking to maximize disruption due to its high levels of digital connectivity.

Meanwhile, cybersecurity partner TrendAI recorded approximately 600,000 detections linked to AI-generated deepfakes, digital sextortion and other forms of synthetic media abuse.

As cybercriminals increasingly harness AI to automate attacks and expand their operations across borders, INTERPOL is urging governments, businesses and individual users to strengthen cybersecurity awareness, verify digital communications before acting on them, and safeguard personal information against an increasingly sophisticated and rapidly evolving cyber threat landscape.

World.title: 2026 Midterms State of Play: Key races unfold as Stevens, El-Sayed battle in Michigan

The 2026 midterms kicked into high gear Tuesday as voters headed to the polls across five states, with Michigan's marquee Democratic Senate primary leading a slate of closely watched contests.

The contest between Rep. Haley Stevens and former public health official Abdul El-Sayed has become the marquee race of the night, drawing millions of dollars in outside spending and attention from top Democratic figures.

The winner will face Republican Mike Rogers in November in one of the country's most competitive Senate races and a contest that could help determine control of the chamber.

2026 MIDTERMS: PRIMARIES, KEY RACES AND ELECTION RESULTS

World.title: Lindsay Clancy strikes evidence deal as fingerprint gap opens trial debate, expert says
World.content:

Lindsay Clancy spoke directly in court Tuesday, repeatedly answering, "Yes, Your Honor," as she agreed to let prosecutors treat certain forensic facts as established hours before a state police trooper testified that investigators recovered no usable fingerprints from a knife or three exercise bands.

The developments narrowed the Massachusetts mother’s murder trial toward its central dispute: whether Clancy was criminally responsible when her three children were killed inside the family’s Duxbury home.

Before jurors entered the courtroom, Judge William Sullivan questioned Clancy about a stipulation covering certain evidence.

HEATED LINDSAY CLANCY COURTROOM EXCHANGE OVER 911 CALL, CRIME SCENE PHOTOS SETS STAGE FOR MOM’S MURDER TRIAL

"You understand that by signing the stipulation, you’re agreeing that the Commonwealth does not have to prove these certain facts that are contained in the stipulation," Sullivan said. "Do you understand that?"

"Yes, Your Honor," Clancy replied.

Asked whether anyone had forced or threatened her to accept the agreement, Clancy said, "No, Your Honor."

Sullivan found that Clancy was competent and had entered the stipulation "knowingly, intelligently, voluntarily and willingly."

LINDSAY CLANCY’S EX-HUSBAND DETAILS PILL USE AS EXPERT SAYS EVIDENCE COULD SHAPE MURDER TRIAL

Defense attorney Kevin Reddington said the agreement would prevent prosecutors from calling dozens of witnesses solely to establish the chain of custody for blood, bodily fluids, exercise bands and DNA evidence.

"We have not been contesting the government’s case in chief, if you will," Reddington said.

The stipulation is not a guilty plea or an admission that Clancy was criminally responsible for the deaths of Cora, 5, Dawson, 3, and Callan, 8 months.

WATCH: Former prosecutor explains strategy behind Lindsay Clancy evidence agreement

Margaret McLean, a former criminal prosecutor and trial attorney who teaches law at Boston College’s Carroll School of Management, said the agreement allows the defense to steer jurors away from repetitive forensic testimony and toward Clancy’s mental state.

LINDSAY CLANCY’S HUSBAND COULD TESTIFY FOR HER AT TRIAL OVER DEATHS OF THEIR THREE CHILDREN

"The legal strategy behind the move by the defense is to steer the jury’s focus away from the horrific nature of the acts and to that central issue of criminal intent, or what we would call mens rea," McLean told Fox News Digital.

McLean said Clancy’s measured responses Tuesday should not be taken as evidence of her mental condition on Jan. 24, 2023.

"She sounded rational. She understands what she’s doing," McLean said. "But remember, the Commonwealth’s burden of proof is to prove that she was sane beyond a reasonable doubt at the time the crimes were committed -- not today, not two weeks ago."

Later, Massachusetts State Police Trooper Jonathan O’Loughlin testified about examining a knife and three exercise bands collected from the home.

O’Loughlin said the knife contained an area of friction-ridge impression, but investigators could not use it to identify anyone.

"There was not enough characteristics or minutia to do any comparison," O’Loughlin said, adding that the impression had "no value."

The yellow, black and blue exercise bands similarly produced no impressions suitable for comparison.

"The bottom line is that you didn’t get any fingerprints," Reddington said.

"Correct," O’Loughlin replied.

McLean said the absence of identifiable prints could make jurors wonder whether gloves were used or the items were wiped, potentially viewing the missing prints as evidence of planning.

World.title: Tarik Skubal's Dodgers debut ends in decisive 5-1 loss to Cubs as LA drops fifth straight game
World.content:
The Los Angeles Dodgers ruined baseball this past weekend when they attempted to make their team better, an unforgivable crime in the world of modern online baseball fandom.

With Shohei Ohtani nursing a nagging knee injury, injuries to Blake Snell and Tyler Glasnow, and inconsistent performance from some of the team's other starting pitching options, the Dodgers used some of their impressive outfield prospect depth to acquire reigning American League Cy Young Award winner Tarik Skubal from the Detroit Tigers.

This set off a firestorm of criticism from fans online, who announced they were quitting the sport, that the season should be canceled, that owners should lock players out indefinitely until players agree to allow billionaire owners to keep 99.9% of revenue, or that the outcome of the 2035 World Series was already determined or something.

SENDING ACE PITCHER TARIK SKUBAL TO THE LOS ANGELES DODGERS WOULD OFFICIALLY RUIN BASEBALL

Well, Skubal made his Dodgers debut Tuesday night in Chicago, facing the Cubs at Wrigley Field. The Dodgers lost their fifth straight game, 5-1, falling to 3-7 in their last 10 games. Baseball is ruined.

Skubal, for his part, pitched well, allowing two runs on four hits over six innings while striking out six and walking two. His first run allowed came on a Dansby Swanson home run in the third inning, with the second coming on an unlucky break.

After striking out Pete Crow-Armstrong to start the sixth, he walked Seiya Suzuki, before Alex Bregman hit a ball to right field that Kyle Tucker wasn't able to make the play on. The Dodgers got Suzuki at home on a Michael Busch grounder, before Nico Hoerner hit a swinging bunt that bounced too high for anyone to make a play on, bringing in Bregman.

The Dodgers offense never got much going against Cubs starter Javier Assad, outside of a Kyle Tucker home run, then did even less against their bullpen. On the rare inning with a baserunner, a Dodger hitter would work tirelessly to hit into an immediate double play.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

The LA bullpen, however, was extremely accommodating. Chicago added two runs in the seventh inning when Pete Crow-Armstrong threw his bat at the ball to drive in Swanson, then Seiya Suzuki blooped another single in to bring in the fourth run of the game. Nico Hoerner homered off Edwin Diaz in the ninth to cement the win.

With baseball ruined, the Dodgers will look to avoid their second consecutive series loss via the sweep on Wednesday, sending superstar starter Eric Lauer to the mound against Shota Imanaga.

This game, and this series, is a microcosm of the absurdities of online baseball discussion. Skubal, arguably one of the best two pitchers in baseball, was outpitched by Javier Assad, a 29-year-old with such mediocre stuff that he's struck out just 51 hitters in 75.1 innings this year. The Cubs are so terrified of starting Assad in a postseason game that they traded for two starting pitchers at the deadline in hopes of avoiding it. Dansby Swanson entered the series on an 0-21 streak, only to go 5-8 with a home run in the first two games.

Meanwhile, Pete Crow-Armstrong's reality defying streak continues, with a .415 batting average on balls put in play since the start of June, an impossible number when league average is around .300. But therein lies the problem with ruining baseball and predicting the World Series in August. You just don't know who will be hot, cold, or underperforming when October rolls around.

A baseball season of 162 games gets compressed into a best-of-five or best-of-seven, the definition of a small sample size, that does quite literally nothing to determine the better team. Good teams often slump. Bad teams sweep good teams.

Since the start of June, the Dodgers have the seventh highest winning percentage in baseball, worse than the Cubs, Red Sox, Astros, Brewers, Tigers, and the... Miami Marlins. That's not in a postseason series, that's over a two month sample. You can't ruin baseball because the gaps between teams are so small. Even now.

OUTKICK IS NOW ON THE FOX APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD

Edwin Diaz has now allowed nine runs in 8.2 innings, with a whopping 20 baserunners. Kyle Tucker's been a league average hitter. Mookie Betts, for all his prior accolades, is hitting .223 with a .280 on base percentage and .390 slugging percentage. His OPS has dropped nearly 200 points from 2024. LA's bullpen since the start of July has an ERA of around 5, and the 27th best FIP in MLB. Ruining baseball indeed.

World.title: Sunrise Movement co-founder defeats establishment-backed Dems in pivotal Michigan race
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

The far-left insurgency within the Democratic Party scored another victory on Tuesday night, with a co-founder of the progressive Sunrise Movement trouncing two establishment-backed Democrats in a contentious Michigan primary.

William Lawrence defeated former U.S. ambassador to Ukraine Bridget Brink and former Navy SEAL Matt Maasdam to win the Democratic nomination for Michigan's 7th Congressional District, anchored in Lansing.

Lawrence will now go on to face Rep. Tom Barrett, R-Mich., a military veteran who is seeking a second term in Congress this November.

DEMOCRATS' CIVIL WAR HEADS TO MICHIGAN, WHERE PROGRESSIVES FACE BIGGEST TEST YET IN HIGH-STAKES SENATE SHOWDOWN

Barrett ran unopposed in the Republican primary after winning the seat in an open race in 2024. It was previously held by Democrat Elissa Slotkin, D-Mich., who vacated it when she successfully ran for Senate that year.

Lawrence's victory is a commanding win in the wider civil war for the soul of the Democratic Party, with battles being waged across the country.

Mike Marinella, spokesman for House Republicans’ campaign arm the National Republican Congressional Committee (NRCC), told Fox News Digital after Lawrence’s victory, "The Democrats' path to the House majority is evaporating in real time. Every embarrassing defeat leaves them with a radical socialist nominee, an emptier bank account, and another must-win seat off the board."

BERNIE SANDERS, DSA REVEAL DEMANDS FOR DEM PARTY AFTER SOCIALISTS SWEEP NEW YORK ELECTIONS

The establishment left's main opponent has been the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA), which has not endorsed a candidate in this race.

But Lawrence does have backing from Rep. Rashida Tlaib, D-Mich., his fellow Michigan Democrat and a prominent DSA member who's stirred controversy for her comments about Israel.

He was also endorsed by Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., a self-described democratic socialist.

The Sunrise Movement, which Lawrence co-founded in 2017, began as a youth-focused climate activist group that pushed the Green New Deal alongside progressives in Congress.

HOUSE PROGRESSIVES REVIVE GREEN NEW DEAL FOR PUBLIC SCHOOLS AS DEM CIVIL WAR EMPOWERS FAR LEFT

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Since then, its non-climate policy platform has included calls to get Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) out of U.S. cities and abolishing police, according to its website.

Lawrence's victory is likely the best outcome for Republicans, who are fighting a nationwide uphill battle to keep control of the House of Representatives.

World.title: Roddy White questions 49ers’ handling of Brandon Aiyuk as receiver's future in San Francisco remains unclear
World.content:

Brandon Aiyuk’s unresolved status remained one of the lingering questions as the San Francisco 49ers opened training camp, with the team offering no update and the next move seemingly left to the wide receiver.

Aiyuk remains in limbo on the reserve/left squad list, where he has been since the end of 2025. After missing all of last season amid a lengthy standoff with the Niners, the All-Pro wide receiver would likely need to apply to the NFL for reinstatement to begin a potential return in 2026.

He could also move the process forward by reporting to training camp or informing the 49ers that he plans to report. Aiyuk’s situation with the 49ers has been strained for roughly a year.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

The dispute appeared to reach a boiling point last July, when San Francisco voided the remaining guaranteed money in his contract after he failed to participate in rehab work for the torn ACL, MCL and meniscus in his right knee.

Aiyuk has appeared to reference the uncertainty around his future with the 49ers in multiple social media posts, only adding to the chatter surrounding the matter. Former NFL wide receiver Roddy White is among the latest sports figures to weigh in.

White argued the 49ers mishandled Aiyuk’s path back from injury and may have complicated any potential effort to move him.

"I think this situation has been handled wrongly by the 49ers," White told Hard Rock Bet. "They should've been more patient with Aiyuk and his situation. They should have done all they could to get him back on the field to give him an opportunity to show he can still play football. When you have a guy who is angry and just wants to leave, it's hard to get any compensation for him."

49ERS BRING BACK DEEBO SAMUEL TO FILL VOID LEFT BY RICKY PEARSALL'S KNEE INJURY: REPORT

White finished his 11-year career with the Atlanta Falcons with 10,863 regular-season receiving yards.

The 49ers’ decision last week to bring back Deebo Samuel appeared to draw a cryptic response from Aiyuk, who wrote on Instagram, "San Fran wanna see a real reunion?"

His posts have not been limited to San Francisco, though, as the receiver has also taking aim at the NFL Players Association. And while Aiyuk has expressed interest in joining the Commanders, that possibility has reportedly cooled off after he called out Washington quarterback Jayden Daniels.

Daniels downplayed any possible lingering tension last week, telling reporters that he and Aiyuk had "handled everything privately."

Aiyuk and Daniels were teammates in 2019 when they both played college football at Arizona State.

Late last month, general manager John Lynch made clear the 49ers were keeping their focus on the players already in camp. "I’m personally, and we as an organization, are going to focus on the players who are here," Lynch told reporters on July 25. "We wish him well, we wish his family well."

Ricky Pearsall entered camp looking like a potential breakout piece for the 49ers’ offense after injuries limited him to 20 games over his first two seasons. Instead, San Francisco’s wide receiver corps absorbed an early setback when swelling returned in the PCL of Pearsall’s right knee. He was moved to injured reserve on Aug. 1.

Aiyuk appeared in seven games in 2024 before being sidelined by injury. One year earlier, he put together the best season of his career, recording 1,342 receiving yards and earning second-team All-Pro honors.

World.title: Progressive activist wins Democratic primary in one of the country’s biggest House races
World.content:
Democrat William Lawrence, a co-founder of the progressive Sunrise Movement, has won his party’s primary in Michigan’s 7th Congressional District, NBC News projects — a big victory for the insurgent left that also sets up a dramatic general election contrast with Republicans in a crucial battleground seat.

Voters in five states participated in primaries Tuesday, including several with major battleground districts up for grabs in November. And few are more hotly contested than this Michigan district, where Lawrence bested two prominent Democratic rivals with national security backgrounds after having differentiated himself as the more liberal candidate and as an aggressive critic of data centers.

Meanwhile, the battle between his two Democratic opponents, former Ambassador Bridget Brink and retired Navy SEAL Matt Maasdam, became increasingly bitter as the race drew to a close, and the two candidates ultimately appear to have split the more moderate wing of the party.

Lawrence will take on GOP Rep. Tom Barrett in one of the most tightly divided swing seats in the country. President Donald Trump carried the district by just 1 percentage point in 2024, and super PACs and other outside groups have reserved more ad spending there than in all but one other House race in the country.

Lawrence won support from an array of prominent progressives and outside groups, and a mysterious super PAC spent more than $1 million in the race’s final weeks to boost him and tear Maasdam down. The spending raised concerns among some Democrats that Republicans might be boosting Lawrence because they think he’ll be easier to beat in the general election.

Michigan voters are also cementing other key battleground House races Tuesday, albeit with less fanfare.

In Michigan’s 4th District, Republican Rep. Bill Huizenga will face off against Democratic state Sen. Sean McCann in the Kalamazoo-area district. Huizenga had Trump’s backing, while McCann was endorsed by top Democrats in the state like Gov. Gretchen Whitmer and Secretary of State Jocelyn Benson.

Republicans are still waiting to find out who will be their nominee against Democratic Rep. Kristen McDonald Rivet. And in the 10th District in suburban Detroit, which is being left open by GOP Rep. John James and his run for governor, Trump-endorsed military veteran Mike Bouchard will run against Democrat Christina Hines, a former special victims prosecutor.

In Virginia, the matchups are set in four districts expected to fit into the battleground puzzle in different ways this fall.

In the Norfolk area, Republican Rep. Jen Kiggans and Democratic former Rep. Elaine Luria head to a rematch of the 2022 2nd District election, which Kiggans won. In the Richmond-area 1st District, Republican Rep. Rob Wittman will face Henrico County Commonwealth’s Attorney Shannon Taylor in a district that could be competitive this fall — one that Trump won by 5 points in 2024.

Farther out on the battlefield, Democratic Rep. Eugene Vindman will face off against Republican Doug Ollivant, a retired Army lieutenant colonel, in the Fredericksburg-area 7th District, a race in which Vindman will start with a significant resource advantage. And Republican Rep. John McGuire will run against Democratic former Rep. Tom Perriello in a district Trump won by 12 points in 2024.

Missouri is home to one of Republicans’ best opportunities to gain a seat this fall after the GOP-controlled state Legislature redrew the congressional map to put Democratic Rep. Emanuel Cleaver into a seat Trump won by 18 points in 2024.

Republican Rick Brattin, a state senator backed by Gov. Mike Kehoe and the Club for Growth, is projected to win the nomination there, with Trump having weighed in for him in the race’s final days.

In Washington state, Republicans are targeting Democratic Rep. Marie Gluesenkamp Perez in a district Trump won by 3 points in 2024. She will face state Senate Republican leader John Braun, who has Trump’s endorsement, this fall.

Meanwhile, two Democratic incumbents faced serious primary challenges Tuesday. One, Rep. Wesley Bell of Missouri, is projected to win his primary, a rematch against former Rep. Cori Bush, whom he defeated in 2024. The other, Rep. Shri Thanedar of Michigan, is narrowly leading state Rep. Donavan McKinney in a race that has not yet been called.

Voters in a handful of safe seats are also picking nominees who are all but certain to win this fall.

In Michigan’s Oakland County, state Senate Democratic leader Jeremy Moss cruised to victory in Democratic Rep. Haley Stevens’ district, with Stevens running for the Senate.

In Missouri, Salem Radio Network host Chris Stigall won the Republican primary in the seat from which GOP Rep. Sam Graves is retiring.

And in Washington’s 4th District, Trump-backed Yakima County Commission member Amanda McKinney will move on to face retired Air Force Maj. John Duresky, a Democrat, in a red seat Trump won by about 20 points in 2024.

GOP Rep. Dan Newhouse, one of the last remaining House Republicans who voted to impeach Trump in 2021, is retiring.

World.title: Trump-backed John James wins Michigan’s GOP primary for governor
World.content:
Rep. John James has won Michigan’s Republican nomination for governor, NBC News projects.

James, who represents the Detroit suburbs, prevailed in the primary despite being vastly outspent by his opponent, wealthy businessman Perry Johnson.

President Donald Trump, despite harboring early concerns that a bid for higher office would put the two-term congressman’s competitive House district at risk, endorsed James and last week traveled to the state to campaign for him.

James, 45, will face Michigan Secretary of State Jocelyn Benson, the winner of Tuesday’s Democratic primary, this fall in one of the most fiercely contested battleground states. Term limits prevent Gov. Gretchen Whitmer, a Democrat, from seeking re-election.

An Army veteran who lost two Senate races before winning his House seat in 2022, James presented himself throughout the race as a capable public servant with applicable business experience, given his work with his family’s logistics company.

“This is an amazing state with all the great ingredients, but for the past seven-and-a-half years, under Gretchen Whitmer, we’ve been led to higher taxes, more crime on the roads — and frankly, the roads we have aren’t fixed yet,” James said during a televised debate last month, throwing back to Whitmer’s 2018 campaign vow to “fix the damn roads.”

“We’re going to work together to make sure that our children can read, to make sure that we put criminals in jail, and we hold those accountable who continue to let them back out,” James added. “And we’re going to be making sure that we come together to accomplish the mission of increasing hope and purpose with tested, positive leadership that has actually been tested from the battlefield to business to delivering for you right now.”

Johnson, 78, pounded the state with more than $31 million worth of ads, according to AdImpact, an ad-tracking firm. He drew on his work in quality control and improving business efficiencies while campaigning on a plan to eliminate the state’s income tax. Johnson also drew on his personal wealth, self-funding his run while declining political donations.

“In the state of Michigan, people are really tired of the politicians,” Johnson told NBC News in an interview last month. “I am an outsider. Nobody denies this fact. I’m the outsider of outsiders.”

James’ campaign spent a fraction on advertising — $2.8 million, according to AdImpact.

One potential factor in the results was the absence of former state Attorney General Mike Cox, who dropped out of the primary on July 17 and threw his support to James. Several polls had shown Cox grabbing a substantial share of the Republican vote and raised the possibility of an unpredictable three-way split that could have benefited Johnson.

Meanwhile, the general election challenge eased a bit for Democrats in May when former Detroit Mayor Mike Duggan ended his independent bid for governor. Duggan, a longtime Democrat, had expressed disappointment with both major political parties but caught attention — and grief — from Democrats who noted his reluctance to aggressively criticize Trump.

Michigan voters have not elected a Democrat to succeed a Democrat as governor in more than 65 years.

Benson deputy campaign manager Alyssa Bradley wrote in an email that the secretary of state “begins the general election with something no other candidate can claim: a record of delivering.”

An accompanying campaign memo took a parting shot at both Republican candidates for governor.

“John James and Perry Johnson spent this year lobbing personal attacks at each other and competing for Donald Trump’s attention, not talking to Michigan families about the cost of housing, healthcare, or keeping the lights on,” the memo read. “Both Republican candidates focused on election denying and Donald Trump, while Jocelyn has stayed focused on the issues affecting Michigan families every day.”

World.title: Rep. Wesley Bell defeats former Rep. Cori Bush in a Missouri Democratic primary rematch
World.content:
ST. LOUIS — Rep. Wesley Bell defeated former Rep. Cori Bush in a Democratic primary rematch, NBC News projects, in the latest chapter of a long-term fight over a deep-blue St. Louis-based district.

Bell overwhelmed Bush on the airwaves, fending off her push to make the race a referendum on his support for U.S. aid to Israel.

In total, Bell’s campaign and outside allies outspent Bush by a staggering 27-to-1 ratio, according to AdImpact, an ad-tracking service. United Democracy Project — the super PAC linked to the American Israel Public Affairs Committee, the pro-Israel advocacy group known as AIPAC — spent $2 million to support Bell, largely through negative ads attacking Bush. One such ad slammed Bush for being critical of former Vice President Kamala Harris.

It was a reference to Bush’s criticizing the Biden-Harris administration for supporting Israel amid what she deemed a genocide in Gaza. She endorsed Harris in the 2024 election.

As Bell cast his vote Tuesday, he criticized Bush for focusing on Israel and talking “over and over ... about an issue that is not impacting folks right here in St. Louis.”

“And while we take those issues seriously, you know, the M in Missouri doesn’t stand for Middle East,” Bell told NBC News. “It stands for Missouri.”

At a campaign stop later Tuesday, Bush hit back at Bell’s claims and said Missourians “are not happy” that he filled his “campaign coffers” with money from outside groups.

“Why are they meddling in our primaries?” she asked. “Why does he allow that?”

AIPAC loomed large in the race after it helped Bell oust Bush two years ago. United Democracy Project poured $9.3 million into ads in that primary, according to AdImpact, accounting for nearly half of the spending in the race.

Sidney Clark, a Democratic candidate for state representative currently serving in local government, said he supported Bell in 2024 but was voting for Bush this cycle because Bell, in his view, has “been paid for.”

“There are people out there who are using their money and financial influence to buy candidates, and I think that’s the wrong direction for our country,” Clark said after having voted at a St. Louis polling place.

Airest Wilson, another Democratic voter, told NBC News that candidates who take corporate money cross a red line for him — even if they are otherwise aligned with his political views.

“They don’t get that money for free,” he said. “You got to represent their interests. You can’t represent the constituents freely.”

“Cori, it took a lot of courage, but she rejected dark money. So that’s why I support Cori,” Wilson added.

This year, Bush ran two TV ads in the primary, each touching on multiple issues. But both linked Bell to AIPAC and cast him as more interested in sending money to Israel than Missourians, including those suffering from the aftermath of last year’s tornado.

Bell presented himself as a fighter against President Donald Trump, saying of Bush in one of his ads: “She fights Kamala Harris, Joe Biden and other Democrats.”

Bush said Tuesday that if she were to lose, it would not be a setback for the progressive movement.

“If there is a loss, then that just means that there is more work for us to do,” she said.

Asked whether she could see herself voting for Bell if he wins the primary, Bush told NBC News: “See myself voting for a Republican? Oh, I don’t think that’s on the ballot for me.”

World.title: GOP’s Ty Masterson and Democrat Cindy Holscher to meet in Kansas governor’s race
World.content:
Republican state Senate President Ty Masterson will face Democratic state Sen. Cindy Holscher in Kansas’ election for governor this fall, NBC News projects, setting up a contest that represents the GOP’s best gubernatorial pickup opportunity this year.

Both candidates won their respective primaries on Tuesday. Masterson rode an endorsement from President Donald Trump to emerge from a crowded GOP field, while Holscher focused on a progressive, anti-establishment message to defeat a fellow state Sen. Ethan Corson, who was backed by term-limited Democratic Gov. Laura Kelly.

Holscher pitched herself in ads as someone who “gets that working people are tired of being sold out by both parties.” She also made her support for a proposed moratorium on new data center construction a big part of her message.

Corson massively outspent Holscher in the primary, and leaned heavily on his support from Kelly, who won two terms in a state Trump won by double digits in the past three presidential contests.

One of his recent TV ads featured Kelly praising him as someone who can “stand up to Trump and ICE” and has the “strength and judgement and backbone” for the state’s top job. Another ad, run by a pro-Corson PAC called Heartland Priorities, showed Kelly lauding Corson for having a “record of standing up for Kansas values” and for “stepping up and fighting back” against Trump.

Kelly, who has maintained strong job approval ratings, told the Kansas City Star in a recent interview that Corson was the only Democrat in the race capable of winning the support of the state’s “extraordinarily moderate” Republican and independent voters in November. She said that, “if he’s not elected, I’m very concerned about the direction Kansas will go in,” while also suggesting that Holscher was an “extremist.”

Meanwhile, on the GOP side, Masterson and his allies were outspent on the airwaves by his opponents, but his support from the president put him over the top.

In a tele-rally last week, Trump lauded Masterson as a “fighter,” a “winner” and as someone who has “done a fantastic job — throughout life, actually.”

“We love each other, we love that state,” Trump said.

In Kansas, registered Republicans outnumber registered Democrats nearly 2 to 1. The Cook Political Report with Amy Walter has rated the general election contest as “lean Republican.”

World.title: Missouri voters block GOP-led effort to raise bar to pass constitutional amendments
World.content:
Missouri voters blocked a Republican-led effort to raise the bar for passing citizen-led constitutional amendments, NBC News projects.

Under current state law, such ballot measures require a simple statewide majority for passage, a process that has been used in recent years to grant abortion rights, expand Medicaid and legalize marijuana.

But Amendment 4 would have required citizen-led ballot initiatives to win a majority in each of Missouri’s congressional districts, boundaries that are drawn by state lawmakers. Other ballot measures, like those referred from the Legislature, would not have been subject to this higher bar.

It would have created “the strictest passage threshold in the country for citizen-initiated ballot measures only,” according to Hannah Ledford, the deputy director of the Fairness Project, a group that supports citizen initiative processes. She added it could have left Missouri’s direct democracy process “functionally dead.”

Missouri is one of 26 states that allows voters to legislate directly by petitioning to place a constitutional amendment on the ballot.

The amendment was first proposed by Republican state Rep. Ed Lewis, after Missouri voters used the method to advance a spate of progressive priorities in a state where the GOP has full control of government. Many recent amendments would have failed under the stricter standard proposed by Amendment 4.

“This amendment is really an amendment to protect our Constitution,” Lewis said on a radio program earlier this month. “We have the absolute lowest and weakest process and that’s why we’ve had six initiative petitions passed in the last eight years that have really done real harm to our state and to our Constitution.”

The state’s Republican-controlled Legislature has repealed or limited some changes made through ballot initiatives, including repealing paid sick leave.

Opponents of the proposal heavily outspent its supporters, pouring more than $6 million into broadcast ads, according to data from the tracking firm AdImpact. The measure’s backers did not air any broadcast ads, AdImpact’s data shows.

The more-moneyed campaign against Amendment 5, a proposal to end income taxes and expand sales taxes, also included arguments against Amendment 4 in their ads.

The effort to change the constitutional amendment process also came after Republican lawmakers redrew the state’s congressional map last year to carve up the lone Democratic-held district. Earlier Tuesday, Missouri Secretary of State Denny Hoskins said that a referendum that sought to undo the new map would not appear on the state’s ballot, arguing the effort was unconstitutional.

Missouri isn’t the only state where Republicans have sought to make it more difficult for citizen-led constitutional amendments to pass. In November, North Dakota and South Dakota voters will decide whether to bump the threshold up from a statewide majority to 60%. And in Utah, there will be a similar measure on the fall ballot specifically related to tax increases.

World.title: Senate Republicans advance Todd Blanche nomination after ‘anti-weaponization’ fund holdup
World.content:
Republicans on the Senate Judiciary Committee on Tuesday advanced Todd Blanche’s attorney general nomination after it had been delayed over concerns from two GOP members on the panel.

Blanche’s path to confirmation had been on hold after Sens. John Cornyn of Texas and Thom Tillis of North Carolina — both of whom are leaving Congress in January — raised concerns about the “anti-weaponization” fund that the Trump administration tried to establish in May to give taxpayer-funded payments to Trump allies, potentially including Jan. 6 rioters the president pardoned on his first day back in office.

Blanche said Sunday that he had reached a deal to amend the settlement that Cornyn and Tillis later said satisfied their concerns. Trump had recently defended the fund and said he would revive it if Blanche’s nomination was blocked.

The nomination will now advance to a vote before the full Senate, where Republicans hold 53 seats.

Kicking off Tuesday’s hearing, Senate Judiciary Committee Chairman Chuck Grassley, R-Iowa, said that the demands from Tillis and Cornyn about the IRS settlement were “common sense.”

Speaking in front of the committee before the vote, Cornyn thanked Blanche for “being willing to work with us.”

“I’m glad we could address these issues here in committee, so that this nomination can move forward,” he said.

Blanche, who served on Trump’s legal defense team during his hush money trial, was confirmed as deputy attorney general last year. He was nominated for the top position after Trump fired Pam Bondi in April amid reports that he was frustrated with her for not pursuing legal action against his political foes more aggressively.

The fund would have been established with a symbolic $1.776 billion in connection with a lawsuit Trump and his family members brought against the government he controls over the leak of his tax returns.

Even with the carveouts in the Blanche documents that would block the “anti-weaponization” fund from moving forward, the Justice Department has ways to make payouts to Trump allies through the long-established Judgment Fund.

Hundreds of pardoned Jan. 6 rioters have made claims against the government and it’s not clear how the Justice Department will handle those claims moving forward, even though the government would have an easy method to get them dismissed because they weren’t filed in a timely manner. The Justice Department moved to dismiss one of the lawsuits Monday.

Democrats at Tuesday’s hearing also brought up the possibility that Trump could move to enforce the original settlement deal since only Blanche signed the order amending it.

“To state the obvious, Mr. Blanche’s statement on the slush fund and the IRS immunity agreement are not signed by the parties to the settlement agreement and are therefore unenforceable,” said Sen. Dick Durbin of Illinois, the top Democrat of the panel. “The parties could still sue to enforce the agreement, and the cop beaters fund can easily be revived with a new order from the Department of Justice 15 minutes after Mr. Blanche is confirmed as attorney general.”

“Indeed, the president himself has loudly telegraphed that’s his plan,” Durbin added.

Speaking to reporters during a Cabinet meeting at Camp David on Friday, Trump said the anti-weaponization fund “is dead, but you know, I wish it weren’t.” During an Oval Office event Monday, Trump said that he viewed the fund “as a positive, and a lot of Republicans do too.”

“These people were treated horribly, and this fund could have given them some solace,” the president added. He also noted that he “didn’t look at” Blanche’s agreement dissolving the fund. “All I know is that Todd Blanche is great,” he said.

Durbin issued a warning to Republicans ahead of the vote Tuesday.

“To my Republican colleagues, you gave Mr. Blanche the benefit of the doubt when you supported his nomination to be deputy attorney general,” Durbin said. “Seventeen months later, there is no doubt where his loyalty will lie.”

World.title: Suspect arrested in connection to devastating Spokane wildfire
World.content: A man with a previous manslaughter conviction was arrested in Spokane, WA and had his first appearance in court today. Authorities say he is responsible for the fire that has reduced hundreds of homes to rubble and forced thousands of people to evacuate. NBC News’ Morgan Chesky reports.Aug. 4, 2026

World.title: SpaceX hit by surging AI costs as insiders prepare to sell their shares
World.content:
For a rocket company, SpaceX is spending a lot of money to build out its AI capacities.

Too much, according to investors.

The company reported revenue in its first quarterly update as a public company that surpassed analysts’ expectations. Most of its revenue came from its Starlink satellite offering.

But investor focus turned to capital expenditures related to its xAI unit, which runs the Grok AI service. Those hit $15.8 billion, higher than expectations of $13.09 billion, according to Bloomberg News data, and about double the previous quarter. The AI spending also accounted for most of SpaceX’s overall $18.4 billion quarterly spending on capital expenditures.

The report caused SpaceX shares to reverse a healthy run-up during regular trading hours Tuesday. The stock fell 6.5% in trading after the closing bell, after having surged 9%.

Musk at Tesla's Gigafactory in Grünheide, Germany, in March 2022. Patrick Pleul / AFP via Getty Images file

SpaceX immediately became a multitrillion-dollar company after a record-setting IPO on June 12 — but nearly just as quickly, it erased $1 trillion in value as the stock plunged amid anticipation of insider stock sales and broader jitters about the pace of AI spending.

Still, it continues to enjoy a market valuation of more than $1 trillion, making it one of the most valuable companies in the world. The stock got an additional boost Tuesday when the company announced a deal with Nvidia to partner on a future satellite project.

Investor speculation that SpaceX may try to merge with its sister company Tesla has grown. That would give Elon Musk even more control over his multifaceted technology empire than he already exerts.

The vast majority of SpaceX’s stock is privately held, with just 5% of the 13.9 billion shares trading on the open market.

Along with Musk, who owns about 42%, the other shareholders are known to regulators as “insiders” and have been barred so far from selling their shares.

That “lockup period” will expire Wednesday, when up to 20% of the total SpaceX shares held by insiders may be sold on the open market.

More shares on the market equals more supply, which means the price per share is likely to fall further.

But some retail investors aren’t concerned by the steep drop in SpaceX’s share price.

Forde Todd, 20, received three shares of SpaceX stock as part of the company’s IPO, then bought and sold several more on the open market.

Todd told NBC News he plans to hold on to his IPO shares despite the stock’s plunge.

“I’m in it for the love of the game — like, I’m in it for SpaceX,” Todd said. “I truly believe in this company.”

“At the end of the day, everybody is going to want a part in the space economy,” he added.

World.title: Rick Brattin wins Republican primary for Missouri seat redrawn to favor GOP
World.content:
Trump-endorsed state lawmaker Rick Brattin has won the Republican nomination for Missouri's 5th Congressional District, CBS News projects, setting up a battle against an 11-term Democrat in a district that was made dramatically more GOP-leaning last year.

Brattin defeated a crowded field of GOP primary candidates Tuesday. Incumbent Rep. Emanuel Cleaver ran for the Democratic nomination unopposed.

A Marine veteran, Brattin was elected to the Missouri state Senate in 2020, after serving in the state House of Representatives. President Trump offered his endorsement Monday, calling Brattin a "MAGA Warrior," and he was backed by Missouri Gov. Mike Kehoe.

The seat previously covered a deep-blue area surrounding Kansas City, but it was transformed during last year's nationwide redistricting scramble, which led state lawmakers to split up the state's second-largest metro area between three different districts.
